News.title: Scary moment driver high on laughing gas smashes into lorry & ploughs past it as passenger pleads ‘use the break’
News.content:
Next

THIS is the horrifying moment a driver high on laughing gas smashes into a lorry as the passenger pleads with him to “use the break”.

Cheten Bhardwaj, 35, crashed into multiple vehicles in Bradford, West Yorkshire, on May 9 last year leaving one woman with serious injuries.



Bhardwaj was dangerously driving his Volvo V40 on Halifax Road whilst under the influence of nitrous oxide, otherwise known as “laughing gas”.

The shocking dashcam footage shows him swerving past a bollard before he hits the accelerator as the passenger screams “slow down”.





Bhardwaj then mounts the pavement next to a Lidl supermarket before careering into a lorry and knocking it completely off the road.

Terrified pedestrians can be seen leaping out of the way as he ploughs through the vehicle, refusing to stop as he carries on down the street.



As Bhardwaj continues to race down the road, other motors can be seen pulling to the side to avoid being hit.

The passenger can again be heard screaming to “press the break, press the break!”

Further down the road, the Volvo mounts the pavement again as he speeds past a Tesla and weaves in and out of traffic.

Bhardwaj, of New Cross Street, admitted to causing serious injury by dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation.

He also admitted driving a motor vehicle with a proportion of a specified controlled drug above the specified limit.



On Friday, he was sentenced to three years and eight months behind bars at Bradford Crown Court.

He was also disqualified from driving for three years and ten months.

Chief Inspector James Farrar of the Roads Policing Unit said: “The actions of Bhardwaj were simply reckless and selfish; this case highlights the very real and often catastrophic consequences of dangerous driving and driving whilst taking nitrous oxide.

“Bhardwaj made a choice to get behind the wheel, whilst under the influence and put other road users at risk.

“I am thankful nobody was killed.



“Nitrous oxide has been a banned drug since November 2023 and the footage in this case highlights the dangers of using it at the wheel.

“It has similar effects to other drugs and can severely impair your ability to drive.”

News.title: Three Brits arrested in Alicante after man shot four times in broad daylight near Costa del Sol beach bar
News.content:
SHOOTERS SNARED Three Brits arrested in Alicante after man shot four times in broad daylight near Costa del Sol beach bar







Next

THREE Brits have been arrested in Alicante after a man was shot in a car park next to a beach bar.

The 31-year-old survived – despite being shot four times in the abdomen and legs – for what is believed to be a settling of scores by drug gangs.



Gunshots rang out near the Andalucía Beach residential complex, close to the Estepona coastline, at around 5.30pm on July 28.

Witnesses claimed that the men were wearing hoods at the time of the brazen attack.



As soon as their victim was on the ground, they escaped in a dark car with foreign plates.

Terrified bar staff rushed to help the seriously injured man, who was lying in a pool of blood.



He was later rushed to the Costa del Sol University Hospital in Marbella.

According to reports following the incident, the victim was a Lithuanian national, but his name has not been released.

Since the arrest of the three British nationals, two of them have been put in preventive detention for attempted murder and other crimes.

The third was released on provisional bail pending continuation of the investigation.



Police have further carried out searches of houses in the La Zenia area of Orihuela Costa.

Fake documents, weapons and a small amount of drugs were seized as part of the operation, and more people have been detained.

Parts of Spain popular with British tourists have been plagued by crime in recent weeks.

Earlier this week, a football ultra was shot in the face while holidaying in Costa del Sol.

Ümit Yalçın, 47, is fighting for his life after the attack at a restaurant on the marina. He is said to be in a serious but stable condition in hospital.



Spanish police are still hunting for the three men believed to be behind the bloodbath and are yet to confirm the motives behind the shooting.

News.title: Creepy foot fetish voyeur, 31, who had THOUSANDS of photos of girls’ feet & staked out schools avoids prison
News.content:
VILE VOYEUR Creepy foot fetish voyeur, 31, who had THOUSANDS of photos of girls’ feet & staked out schools avoids prison







Next

A CREEPY foot fetish voyeur who had more than 10,000 pictures of girls’ feet on his phone has avoided prison.

Pervert Samuel Tobin, 31, also had 444 videos and even more images stashed on a USB stick.



The sickening haul included pictures of girls in school uniform, with some showing a school sign in the background.

A USB stick was divided into folders labelled “flats”, “loafers”, “flip-flops”, “sandals” and “schoolgirls”.



Prosecutor Hollie Davies told Basildon Crown Court another 28 USB sticks were still “awaiting further assessment”.

Tobin appeared to have staked out a school, the court heard, with many of the images showing girls in uniform.

But none of the pictures were indecent, with the majority showing feet, ankles and shoes.

They appeared to have been taken without the women or girls knowing and for Tobin’s sexual gratification.

Tobin, of Westcliff, Essex, sat with his head in his hands in the dock on Wednesday.

He had first been made subject to a sexual risk order in 2021 to “help manage the defendant’s sexual preoccupation with feet and shoes”.



The order banned him from taking pictures of people’s feet without their consent.

But he has breached it three times since — in 2023, 2025 and 2026.

Essex Police carried out a random spot check at Tobin’s home in June.

He was found using his computer in his bedroom and grabbed his phone when an officer entered.

The prosecutor said he began “fussing with it, pressing buttons” before the officer took the phone from him.



His gallery was empty, but officers found around 10,000 pictures and 444 videos in the deleted folder.

Miss Davies said: “Looking through those images, the majority were of feet.

“Nearly all were of female feet either in sandals or school-type pumps and taken from varied angles.”

One picture amounted to voyeurism — showing a woman sunbathing in the privacy of her back garden.

The other thousands of images were dealt with as breaches of his sexual risk order.



Tobin had previously been given community orders for his two earlier breaches.

He was still subject to the latest order when he carried out the offences.

Defence barrister Angelina Nurse said Tobin had been diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder and was awaiting a possible ADHD diagnosis.

She said he had an “obsession” and “compulsion” to photograph feet, ankles and shoes.

Miss Nurse told the court the offences had “crossed the custody threshold” but probation believed his risk could still be managed in the community.



Tobin had already started therapy to try to control his urges, she added.

Recorder Peter Clark sentenced him to two years in prison, suspended for two years.

He must also complete 120 hours of unpaid work, a “building better choices” course and up to 30 additional rehabilitation activity days.

The judge said there was a “realistic prospect of rehabilitation” despite Tobin’s “terrible history”.

But he imposed a ten-year sexual harm prevention order, meaning Tobin will remain on the sex offenders register for the same period.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Recorder Clark warned him: “You are really getting to the last chance saloon now.

“It’s in your hands now to make sure you don’t tip over the edge.”

News.title: At least 13 dead after military plane crashes in desperate emergency landing near houses as army generals killed
News.content:
Next

AT LEAST 13 people, including three army officers, have been killed in a horror plane crash in Democratic ‌Republic of Congo.

The military aircraft was travelling to the capital, Kinshasa, when a technical problem forced the pilot to make an emergency landing.



“With no landing strip available in Kenge, the plane crashed into a residential plot,” Remy Saki Bokinda, the Kwango vice ​governor said.

Passengers included General Likulia Bakumi, the ​army’s auditor general, as well as a major, ⁠captain, military personnel and civilians.



“All those on board died; 12 were burned beyond recognition, while the pilot’s lifeless body was found outside the aircraft,” Bokinda said.

Grim footage of the crash site shows the aircraft wreckage engulfed in flames.



A crowd watched on in shock as thick plumes of black smoke rose above the inferno.

The plane was reportedly a small, Czech-made L-410 operated by TRACEP.

Congo’s aviation accident investigation authority is launching a probe into the crash, a government statement said.

The Congolese army has suffered significant setbacks in the last year.



⁠Rwanda-backed ​AFC/M23 rebels have seized large swathes of the east capturing the region’s largest strategic hubs.

The tragedy comes just days after three people were killed in a plane crash in the Swiss Alps.

The light aircraft had taken off from Sion Airport in the Rhône Valley before crashing into a northern mountain slope around ten minutes later.



Emergency crews, including police, firefighters and rescue teams, raced to the scene along with three helicopters.

Two Brits, Anthony Hall, 42 and Owain Davies, 55, were identified among the casualties.

In a separate incident, a pilot was killed after two gliders crashed mid-air over upstate New York.

One plane plunged into a heavily wooded and remote area, while the other was able to land safely after the collision.

Each aircraft was operated by a single pilot and carried no passengers.

It took investigators more than two hours to find debris from the wreck of the Schempp-Hirth Ventus-2B glider.

The body of the pilot, who has not been identified, was found at the scene.

News.title: Military dads may soon be given more time with their babies under plans being considered by ministers
News.content:
CALL OF DUTY Military dads may soon be given more time with their babies under plans being considered by ministers







Next

MILITARY dads could soon be given more time with their newborn babies under plans being considered by the Government.

Ex-Armed Forces Minister Al Carns has urged Wes Streeting to extend paternity leave for troops after revealing he had just two days with his daughter before returning to Northern Ireland for three months.



The Sun understands former Defence Secretary John Healey had been preparing to announce improved paternity leave around Armed Forces Day before he resigned in June.

And a government source confirmed the proposals remain alive, telling The Sun: “We’re looking at it.”



Mr Carns has now urged Mr Streeting to pick up the plans and suggested Remembrance would be a good time to unveil them.

Serving personnel who qualify currently receive up to two weeks of paternity leave on full pay.

The former Royal Marine was serving in Northern Ireland when his partner was due to be induced and tried to time his two weeks off around the birth.

But the induction took nine days, leaving him just days with his newborn before he had to return to duty for another three months.

Mr Carns told The Sun: “It was pretty miserable because you were waiting when you were trying to time it, and then had two or three days, and I was straight back up to Northern Ireland for three months…

“The reality is, in the military, you spend less time with your family or children than probably any other profession.



“Having that bespoke period of time around your child’s birth is absolutely critical.”

He said the policy should already have been largely worked up under Mr Healey and could now be taken forward by his successor.

Mr Carns said: “If John Healey was looking into it, the policy will be written, and it’ll be a case of just moving it forward and making sure it’s correctly costed.

“I’m sure Wes will be looking at it. Remembrance is always a good time to make announcements.”

George Gabriel, co-founder of The Dad Shift, said: “Two weeks might work for a family holiday to Spain, but the idea it’d be enough for fathers when a new baby arrives is a joke. This government says it has squaddies backs, well here’s a chance to prove it.”



Mr Carns said any extension would need safeguards to ensure it did not interfere with operational requirements.

An MOD spokesperson said: “We recognise the unique demands Service life places on personnel and their families and we are committed to providing fair, compassionate and accessible parental leave.”

News.title: Body of man who went fully dressed into water near castle is found two days later & 20 miles away
News.content:
TRAGIC END Body of man who went fully dressed into water near castle is found two days later & 20 miles away







Next

A MAN who entered the water fully-dressed near a Welsh castle has been found dead 20 miles away two days later.

Cops were called to West Kirby Marine Lake in Merseyside last week after they were informed a man had been found unresponsive on the tidal side of the wall.



Paramedics, who had informed the police at around 3.50pm last Wednesday, sadly pronounced the man dead at the scene.

It is believed that he had entered the water near to Flint Castle in Wales – around 20 miles away – on the evening of Monday, September 14.



North Wales Police is now urging the public to help in its investigation.

They described the man as an Asian male, around 5ft10in tall and of a medium build.



He is also said to have been wearing a a black sweatshirt, ripped blue jeans, black trainers, and possibly in possession of a crossbody bag.

A spokesperson for the force said: “At 3.50pm on Wednesday 16 September, Merseyside Police were informed by the ambulance service that a male had been found unresponsive on the tidal side of the wall at West Kirby Marine Lake, Merseyside.

“He was sadly pronounced deceased at the scene.

“It is believed he entered the water around the Flint Castle area during the evening of Monday, 14 September.”



Detective Chief Inspector Richard Griffith is appealing to anyone who may have seen him to get in touch.

He added: “We are aware from CCTV enquiries there were several people walking, cycling and driving around the area of Flint Castle at the time.

“I am particularly keen to speak to anyone who saw the man between 6pm and 9.30pm on Monday, 14 September.

“He was an Asian male, described to be around 5ft10 tall and of a medium build.

“He was wearing a black sweatshirt, ripped blue jeans, black trainers, and possibly in possession of a crossbody bag.



“I’m also appealing to anyone who might have any pictures, videos or dashcam around the castle between these times to contact us.

“Your information or images could be crucial in assisting our investigation.

“My thoughts remain with the man’s family at this difficult time.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Anybody with information, photos or footage has been urged to upload them to the Major incident Police Portal.

They can also contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously via their website.

News.title: Sick couple who left stepbrother with 50 rib fractures & lying in own urine & weighing just 40kg are jailed for life
News.content:
'ABHORRENT' ABUSE Sick couple who left stepbrother with 50 rib fractures & lying in own urine & weighing just 40kg are jailed for life







Next

A SICK couple have been jailed for life after they murdered their vulnerable stepbrother following a sickening campaign of abuse.

Rubin Blount was discovered with 50 rib fractures before his tragic death in Tamworth, Staffordshire four years ago.



The 28-year-old – who had severe learning disabilities – was left weighing just 40kg and had been forced to lay in his own urine.

Staffordshire Police said his carers had subjected Rubin to “horrendous physical and emotional abuse”.



They assaulted him on a number of occasions, denied him medical care and forced him to stand for long periods of time.

Kenneth Newton, 57, and Melanie James, 64, both from Birmingham, were today sentenced to life imprisonment at Stafford Crown Court.



In November 2022, Rubin was raced to hospital and suffered a heart attack upon his arrival.

Despite being resuscitated, he remained in a critical condition and he wasn’t expected to survive.



When assessing him, doctors found Rubin to have extensive pneumonia, severe infection, rib and spine fractures, as well as burns, lesions and grazes.

He was also severely dehydrated and malnourished and weighed only 40kg when he was admitted to hospital.

He tragically died three days later.

At the time of Newton and James’ arrest, they told cops they were aware of Rubin’s vulnerabilities and care requirements, denying they had caused him any harm.

But an investigation revealed they had threatened, verbally abused and physically assaulted him in their home.



Officers added they had discovered mould and “abhorrent conditions” in Rubin’s bedroom.

Stafford Crown Court also heard Rubin had reported being sexually abused, reports ITV.

Newton and James were both convicted following a six-week trial and will spend the rest of their lives behind bars with a minimum term of 21 years.

A member of the public shouted “rot in hell” as they learned their fate.

Rubin’s mother said her son deserved “compassion, dignity and a chance to live his life” in a victim impact statement read to the court.



She believed those entrusted with his care “loved him and would take care of him”.

“He was a son, a brother and friend and a person who was deeply loved by so many people – not just us, but people who knew him in the community,” she said.

“His life mattered and his loss has been felt by us all.

“His future was stolen and our family must now live with a lifetime of heartbreak.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Speaking following the sentencing, Detective Chief Inspector Ian Fitzgerald said: “The loss of Rubin will continue to affect those who knew him, deeply, and I’d like to extend my thoughts to them at this time.



“The suffering and abuse I have seen during our investigation of this case has been difficult to comprehend, and I’m pleased with the outcome at court today.”

News.title: Horrifying moment girl, 6, is snatched by leopard & dragged to her death while playing in garden at home
News.content:
Next

THIS is the horrifying moment a leopard stalks, pounces and fatally mauls a six-year-old-girl as she played in her garden.

Terrifying footage shows the spotted beast run up behind Prisha Solanki, 6, before dragging her away into the shadows in Junagadh district, India.



The young girl had been playing in the courtyard outside her home in Dedkiyal village when she suddenly disappeared.

The CCTV footage shows the leopard sneakily following Prisha before it pounces at lightning speed.



Her family and local residents carried out a frantic two-hour search before finding Prisha’s body hidden in a nearby soybean field.

The leopard had moved away from the area by the time Forest Department officials arrived and began their operation to locate and capture it.



Eight cages were placed at different locations around the area in an attempt to trap the animal, while intensive patrolling and tracking operations continued.

A statement shared by Gir West Divisional Forest Officer Prashant Tomar said: “The leopard attacked and killed Prisha Solanki.



“Her body was found later near the farm.

“A team reached the spot and placed eight cages in the vicinity to trap the animal. Intensive patrolling and tracking operations are underway.”

Forest officials urged residents to remain cautious at night as the search and trapping operation continued.

The leopard remains at large.

The department also said the process of providing compensation to Prisha’s family had been given priority.



Leopard attacks remain a serious concern in parts of India as habitat loss, human encroachment and rising wildlife populations are causing a spike in attacks.

In July, an elderly man, 88, was killed in a savage leopard attack.

Ram Yadav was asleep on his veranda in the Bahraich district of Uttar Pradesh, India when the wild cat crept up to the property.

The leopard launched itself at the 88-year-old before dragging him away screaming.

Ram suffered severe injuries, particularly to his neck, in the savage attack and was declared dead on his arrival at hospital.



The animals are increasingly sighted in and around human settlements.

Also in July, a ferocious leopard barged its way into a booze shop and launched itself at a terrified worker.

The leopard uses its razor-sharp claws to swipe at Sanjay Gurjar, 25, at the store in Todaraisingh, northern India.

Sanjay suffered claw injuries to his hand, shoulder and nose and the two other men were also injured by the beast.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It triggered a huge five-hour operation to track the predator, which they ultimately tranquillised and returned to the wild.



India’s national leopard assessment estimates the population to be around a total of 13,800.

News.title: Watch: What could the potential sanctions for Man City be?
News.content: Football finance expert Kieran Maguire says the potential sanctions for Manchester City will be 'significant' after the sources told BBC Sport that the club has been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they were accused of breaching.

News.title: I'm not tempted to call an early election, Burnham says
News.content:
Andy Burnham has insisted he is not tempted to call an early general election, arguing it would throw "the country into a backward-looking process".

During a round of BBC interviews ahead of Labour's annual conference, the prime minister said his focus was on helping people with the cost of living and supporting businesses.

Recent polling has suggested Labour's position has improved since Burnham replaced Sir Keir Starmer in Downing Street in July, although Reform UK and the Conservatives are not far behind.

An early general election could give Burnham a mandate of his own and free him from commitments made in Labour's 2024 manifesto. The next general election must be held by August 2029.

Asked by ITV Calendar if the next election would be in 2029, he replied: "Yes, that's when the next election will be.

"All of this speculation on an early election, I can knock that dead."

News.title: Some BBC channels and radio stations may well have to close, director general says
News.content:
Brittin took over as BBC director general in May after a decade as president of Google in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

Asked by Kuenssberg if he would allow a programme to be made and presented by AI, Brittin replied: "I would do, within guardrails."

He added: "We want to experiment with this technology and understand what it can and can't do, but I'm here because I believe in human creativity.

"I don't think anything we do should be replaced by AI. I think there are lots of places where AI can help us make the licence fee go further, but also help us in our decision-making and creativity. But it's not a substitute for humans."

He also warned of the danger of a handful of tech companies having too much control over information in the future.

"We're also in this moment where AI is in takeoff. So I think there's a danger that six companies will control access to information in future and the creation of information and misinformation," he said.

"Six companies, none of them European, let alone British. In that world, here's the BBC. It's the most trusted organisation by over half a billion people."

Asked if he trusted big tech companies he replied: "There's a lot of platforms out there, so I wouldn't trust any platform innately.

"And I think what you do is you keep under review how those things work and whether your content can show up in the right place and fulfil its mission.

"I think the BBC and our apps and services should be the antidote to the algorithm. Everywhere else you go is driven by some commercial interest."

The interview will be available on BBC Sounds and YouTube on Saturday 26 September, then on Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg on BBC One and iPlayer at 09:00 BST on 27 September.

News.title: Daniel Thomas pleads not guilty after dinghy slashed
News.content:
Anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas has pleaded not guilty to criminal damage after a video appeared to show him slashing at a dinghy in the Channel with a knife.

The 37-year-old, known to his supporters as Danny Tommo, was arrested after the livestreamed video on Tuesday.

Thomas, who appeared at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in Hampshire via videolink, is also charged with failing to disclose the PIN to his phone.

He pleaded not guilty to both charges and was remanded in custody until his next court appearance at Portsmouth Crown Court on 29 September.

News.title: British climber dies after falling 60m on Spanish mountainside
News.content:
A 28-year-old British climber has died after falling about 60m (200ft) from one of the highest mountains in northern Spain.

The man fell into a gully while descending from the summit of Torrecerredo in the Cantabrian Mountains on Thursday, the Spanish Civil Guard said.

Police and an air unit were deployed to the scene after emergency services were called around 13:27 local time (11:27 GMT). The man's body was recovered by a mountain rescue unit.

The UK Foreign Office said it was in contact with local authorities "following reports of the death of a British national in Spain".

Spanish emergency services said they initially received a call saying that a person had fallen on the eastern face of the mountain and dispatched a rescue group aboard a medical helicopter.

A doctor among them confirmed the man's death at about 14:18 and remained at the scene to guard the body until a Civil Guard helicopter could arrive about an hour and 20 minutes later.

Specialist mountain rescuers were then lowered by winch to the site of the accident, where they recovered the man's body and belongings.

The identity of the climber, who Spanish authorities said was English, has not been given. The accident occurred when he was about 20 metres from the mountain's summit.

His body has been transported to the Institute of Legal Medicine, which provides forensic pathology services, in Asturias, the Civil Guard said.

Torrecerredo, which has an elevation of about 2,650m, is in the Picos de Europa, which is popular with climbers and walkers.

The region's tourism board describes the route up the mountain as "very difficult" with a demanding ascent, warning climbers to take particular care on steep and exposed upper sections on their way down.

Sepa Asturias - the body responsible for emergency services in the region - said it also transported a 54-year-old French woman to hospital after she suffered a leg injury on the mountain range on Thursday afternoon.

News.title: Noah Woods left playground through gap in fence, inquest hears
News.content:
Suffolk Coroner's Court heard from police that Noah had left the playground, walked into a memorial garden and left that through an open gate. He then ran down a path on a new housing estate towards nearby Decoy Pond.

Det Ch Insp Matt Connick from Suffolk Police told the court that CCTV showed Noah in the play area being looked after by a relative, which was "part of a normal routine".

The detective said Noah "left through a gap in the fence leading to the memorial garden where he left through an open gate".

After he had left the play area, he was closely followed by the relative trying to catch up with him, Connick added.

The inquest heard the relative had shouted out to Noah, who lived in neighbouring East Bergholt, but he went out of sight shortly afterwards.

Another man was said to have joined the search and then police were called.

At the time of the search, volunteers were told that Noah was non-verbal and partially deaf.

A statement from Brantham Parish Council, which maintains the play area at Merriam Close, said it was "deeply saddened by Noah's death and our thoughts remain with his family and all those affected at this extremely difficult time".

"The parish council understands that there was a break in the internal fencing, being constructed to separate the play area from the memorial garden, however the whole of the area at Merriam Close, including the play area and memorial garden are completely enclosed by appropriate perimeter fencing," it said.

"The council will co-operate fully with any investigation and, while inquiries are ongoing, does not consider it appropriate to comment further."

News.title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records
News.content:
NHS staff in England suspected of looking at patient records without a valid reason will be immediately suspended as part of a "zero-tolerance crackdown" on snooping.

Those under suspicion will also be locked out of NHS computer systems, preventing any further viewing of confidential records, including from home.

NHS England chief executive Sir Jim Mackey has written to every trust, ordering the measures to be introduced immediately to strengthen protection against data breaches.

The move follows a series of high-profile incidents involving the records of Nottingham and Southport attack victims and a child who was injured in a crocodile enclosure in Cambridgeshire.

This week, Bristol Foundation NHS Trust said it had launched an internal investigation after it emerged the medical records of an 18-year-old had been accessed years after his death.

The boy's mother, Paula McGowan, told the BBC she was "deeply concerned and hurt" and called for the NHS to do more to deal with the problem.

News.title: PM rules out giving Wales independence referendum powers
News.content:
The prime minister has ruled out handing powers to hold a referendum on independence to the Welsh government.

Andy Burnham said other UK nations do not have such powers and he did not "think we can create a different arrangement for Wales".

He added that the decision should be made jointly with Westminster, arguing that the UK Parliament has to have a "say on an issue of that magnitude".

Wales First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth said last week he would seek powers to hold an independence referendum, although he ruled out staging one before the next Senedd election in May 2030.

Burnham also said he was open to looking at the Welsh government's "Cynnal" plans to trial offering Â£10 a week for 15,000 children aged under six, in households already receiving universal credit.

This would require the agreement of the Department for Work and Pensions and HMRC to avoid the payment being taxed or other benefits - paid for by the UK government - being reduced.

"I'll certainly ensure that there's a proper discussion about the issue," he said.

"I mean, I did things as mayor of Greater Manchester without there having to be any tax implications.

"So I'm not quite sure why that arises in this in this instance, but we will have a look at it for certain."

News.title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse
News.content:
The victims of child sex offender Jeffrey Donaldson have described the impact the abuse had on them.

Donaldson was convicted in June of 18 counts of sex abuse including one of rape, which he committed against two women when they were children.

The former Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader appeared at Newry Crown Court for a hearing prior to his sentencing in October. He is seeking to appeal his convictions.

The prosecution barrister told the court that one of the women said her childhood had been stolen, while the second said the abuse affected her every day.

In her submission to the pre-sentencing hearing, Rosemary Walsh KC outlined what she described as the "salient facts" that were heard during the course of the trial.

She also described the impact the offending had on both victims, whom were described during the trial as Complainants A and B.

She said both complainants often wondered what life would have been like if they hadn't experienced the abuse.

In her victim impact statement, Complainant A described the "profound impact" the abuse had on her.

Walsh said the complainant believed her childhood had been "stolen" and that she felt an "enormous amount of anger that is always simmering away under the surface".

Walsh said the abuse Complainant B had suffered affected her "every day and every relationship", and that she had to fight on a daily basis the wish that she would die.

The prosecution barrister also outlined further aggravating and mitigating factors.

She said, in sentencing, the youth of the victims had to be taken account, as well as the "multitude of offences", which "spanned a considerable period of time", and the fact there were two victims.

Donaldson's defence barrister Keiron Vaughan KC told the court that the 63-year-old was "of previous good character" and that there had been no offending of this type over the last 18 years.

"In that period of time, Mr Donaldson has or did achieve significant things in his life," he said.

"I readily accept that these convictions obliterate all those achievements that he has made in his life, and that's certainly something he will have to live with."

Vaughan said he acknowledged the court would impose a "lengthy custodial sentence", but that he had complete confidence that the court would treat Donaldson in the same way it would any other defendant of a similar age and in similar circumstances.

Addressing Donaldson directly, Judge Paul Ramsey said: "Mr Donaldson, I will be sentencing you as soon as I can next month."

News.title: Contentious Orange Order parade can go ahead, commission says
News.content:
The Parades Commission has announced that a planned Orange Order parade is to be allowed on the mainly-nationalist Garvaghy Road in Portadown.

The commission said the parade on Sunday should start earlier than the Orange Order wanted and with fewer people - but can go ahead.

The decision is facing a legal challenge from the Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition which opposes the march and has said the challenge will be heard on Saturday morning.

Rather than start at 13:00 BST on Sunday as intended, the commission has said the march can begin at 08:00 and with 35 participants rather than the 60 the Orange Order requested.

Follow live: Parades Commission says Orange Order Drumcree parade can go ahead

In a detailed document known as a determination, which was published on its website, external, the commission said: "This decision is not, and should not be perceived, as a victory for one side or a loss for another.

"It is the outworking of the application of the legal framework to the facts available to the commission."

News.title: PM says bailed sex offender case must be reviewed
News.content:
The prime minister has said that the decision to bail a sex offender and repeatedly allow him to return to his home overlooking the playground he targeted must be reviewed.

Zafer Dogan, 32, of Enfield, north London, was jailed on Thursday for two years and four months for taking thousands of pictures of children and using AI software to "nudify" them.

Andy Burnham called the case "disturbing", adding: "I would ask those working across the criminal justice system to look at it and to make any necessary changes as a result."

The Ministry of Justice said while the Crown Prosecution Service had the right to challenge them, final bail decisions were "made by the independent judiciary".

The ministry added: "The protection of victims, witnesses, and the public must always be considered when deciding whether or not an offender should be released on bail."

London's victims' commissioner Andrea Simon said victims and their families had been "grossly failed" by the court system that granted Dogan bail.

She said the case showed "the justice system did not centre victims" and called for a multi-agency review.

Speaking outside the court where Dogan was jailed, Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley criticised the "unfathomable decisions" of the justice system.

Burnham told BBC London's political editor Karl Mercer that Sir Mark "certainly has a point and it needs to be heard".

"It's a matter for the courts when these decisions are made," the prime minister said. "They need to hear the voice of the commissioner of the Metropolitan Police.

"This case is disturbing and I would ask those working across the criminal justice system to look at it and make any necessary changes as a result."

Burnham also told BBC London the plan to release some offenders before the end of their custodial sentences, to free up space in prisons, was "not an ideal situation".

"The failure to build prison spaces over a number of years has led to this unacceptable situation," he said.

Dogan had pleaded guilty to three counts of making indecent images of a child, which included 900 category C images, 294 category B images and 653 category A images, which are the most serious.

He also admitted possessing extreme pornography, possessing a prohibited image of a child, creating purported intimate images of an adult, obstructing a constable in the execution of their duty and a further two counts of making indecent photographs of a child.

According to the police, he had taken more than 5,000 pictures, many from his bedroom window.

Despite protests from the police and prosecutors, he had previously been bailed back to his flat, forcing one family who had fallen victim to his crimes to move into temporary accommodation.

Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today, Simon said: "I think victims and their families were grossly failed by the decision to allow this paedophile to return to an address where he was overlooking a playground near to his victims.

"The case [shows that] the justice system just does not centre victims. To know that the police and prosecutors opposed bail multiple times, but nevertheless, he was returned to the community, is an indication that the capacity pressures on prisons are not being balanced with the impacts that that's having on victims' lives.

"We seem to be lurching from one crisis to another, and victim safety and their rights seem to be put to one side, as the justice system struggles."

News.title: Ex-GTA developer's studio faces closure after debut game flopped
News.content:
Benzies set up Barb in 2016 - the same year he left Grand Theft Auto maker Rockstar Games after a legal row over unpaid royalties.

It began work on Everywhere, intended to be a multiplayer role-playing game set in a futuristic city, before pivoting its focus to action-adventure MindsEye.

The project attracted a lot of interest and, according to company documents, external, Barb had managed to attract more than Â£233m of investment by 2024.

Former staff previously told BBC Newsbeat the development process had "no coherent direction" and accused senior managers of failing to listen to their concerns.

Following the game's turbulent launch, between 250 to 300 members of staff were made redundant.

Shortly before this, during an all-staff call, Benzies alleged "internal and external" forces had conspired to hinder MindsEye's release, and vowed to root out "saboteurs" within the company.

When Newsbeat asked Barb about this, it released a statement saying: "Leslie and the entire senior management team take full responsibility for the initial launch [of MindsEye].

"The version of the game that was released did not reflect the experience our community deserved."

Since its release, the company has failed to attract a bigger audience to the game with a series of fixes and content updates.

After further layoffs, reports last week suggested the remaining workers at the studio had also been let go.

News.title: Glasgow City Council pauses plan to fire and rehire 23,000 staff
News.content:
Glasgow City Council has agreed to pause plans to fire and rehire more than 23,000 members of staff.

The decision follows online talks between the council and three trade unions, chaired by Deputy First Minister Jenny Gilruth.

Negotiations between the council and the GMB, Unison and Unite unions will resume early next week to try to reach a new deal on pay.

Letters which had been due to be sent to staff informing them of the fire and rehire plans will not be issued.

The SNP-led council had threatened to sack thousands of members of staff and then rehire them on new contracts after negotiations with unions over equal pay proposals broke down.

The talks were about the council's plans to replace a pay system found to discriminate against mostly women workers. The changes would see the majority of staff unaffected or better off, but they would cut pay for 11% of staff.

Gilruth said the Scottish government did not support fire and rehire schemes and had urged the council and trade unions to get back around the negotiating table.

She said: "Given the significance of this situation and the impact on staff, I wanted to bring all parties together to make clear that I expect negotiations between the council and unions to continue so that a collective agreement can be reached and bring an end to discriminatory pay practices.

"My expectation is that all parties act in line with the principles of fair work and continue to exhaust all avenues for collective agreement."

On behalf of unions Unite, Unison and GMB, the Scottish Trades Unions Congress said: "We are pleased at the lifting of the threat of fire and rehire and that meaningful negotiations will take place next week.

"We also welcome the Scottish government's clear statement that the practice of fire and rehire' does not align with the principles and expected practice of fair work."

News.title: Cyber attack on police force may have 'compromised' staff information
News.content:
A cyber attack on a police force in Wales may have resulted in staff information being "accessed or compromised".

Dyfed-Powys Police said the hack had caused disruption to some non-emergency systems but no personal data relating to members of the public was believed to have been accessed.

The force said the incident was identified on 14 September, and an investigation is under way.

The Information Commissioner's Office, external (ICO) has been notified, with a spokesperson saying: "We can confirm we have received a breach report from Dyfed-Powys Police and we are assessing the information provided."

Dyfed-Powys Police said it remained fully operational and its response to emergency incidents had not been affected.

It said online and email contact services were unavailable for a period following the attack, but these had now been restored and 999 and 101 service had not been affected.

The force said it was receiving support from cyber-security specialists and its systems had been subject to "precautionary measures" while specialist teams investigated the incident and worked to restore services safely.

A spokesperson said: "At this stage, our investigation has found no evidence that members of the public's personal data has been accessed or compromised as a result of this incident.

"We are, however, continuing to investigate whether any information relating to our staff may have been accessed or compromised, and are taking all appropriate steps to protect that information, and will provide appropriate advice to colleagues if required."

They added they "understood the potential concern this may cause" and wanted to "reassure the public that we have and will continue to take all necessary steps to protect our information and maintain the security of our systems".

The force said it would provide further updates when it was in a position to do so.

The ongoing investigation is being managed by Tarian, the Regional Organised Crime Unit (ROCU) for southern Wales, and force systems are being monitored.

The IOC spokesperson said anyone worried about their personal information can visit the ICO website for advice and support.

"We advise checking regularly for updates from the organisation impacted and following their advice if they confirm that an individual's personal information has been compromised," they added.

Dyfed-Powys Police and Crime Commissioner Dafydd Llywellyn said the attack was "serious", adding that "police information and the information that police systems hold is very sensitive data from the public's perspective".

"What's important to note in this case is that personal information from the public has not been breached, to my knowledge," he added.

"Some systems were closed down for a protective measure to ensure that no further information was breached in that way."

He added that the response from the force had been "very strong" and the "security weaknesses have been patched up".

The area served by Dyfed-Powys Police includes Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire and Powys, and equates to more than 500,000 people - a number that rises significantly with tourists each year.

The force has 1,349 police officers, as well as 1,063 police staff, police community support officers (PCSO) and special constables, according to an information request in March 2026.

Dr Nisha Rawindaran, lecturer in Cyber Security and Forensics at the University of South Wales said: "Cyber attacks happen every day across public and private sectors but what we hear publicly is a fraction of the actual events because only a smaller number turn into something that has a wider impact and requires a coordinated response."

She added that with any cyber incident "the key is not just if information has been stolen, but whether systems have been disrupted, and how quickly organisations can recover from this".

News.title: No action taken against Iranian man who tried to enter nuclear base
News.content:
No action is to be taken against an Iranian man who tried to enter the Faslane nuclear submarine base earlier this year.

The 34-year-old was arrested at HM Naval Base Clyde near Helensburgh, Argyll and Bute, on 19 March, along with a 31-year-old Romanian woman.

The Crown Office said it had carefully considered the case and decided there should be no further proceedings against the man.

It had previously said in March that no proceedings would be brought against the Romanian woman.

A Florida family’s multimillion-dollar house was incinerated when their Tesla exploded in the garage after the electric vehicle’s battery system was exposed to saltwater during a hurricane, according to a federal lawsuit obtained by The Independent.

Tampa Bay auto dealer Michael Murphy was out of town when the Model S combusted, but his wife, young daughters, and in-laws were at the home – and were pulled to safety by rescuers, their complaint states.

However, it goes on, the fire reduced the entire 5,400-square-foot structure to ashes, “destroying, in a single moment, every piece of property the family had spent their lives accumulating.”

“Worse yet, the fire consumed the Murphy home so quickly that rescuers did not reach the family in time to save their dog, who tragically died in the fire,” according to the complaint.

The Murphys’ complaint, which was filed September 24 in Tampa federal court, contends Tesla had previously received “multiple warnings that its vehicles were prone to sudden and explosive fires when their batteries were exposed to water.”

open image in gallery A 5,400-square-foot home in Tampa Bay burned to the ground when a Tesla in the garage was exposed to saltwater during Hurricane Helene, according to a federal lawsuit ( U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida )

Despite repeated warnings, Tesla “continued to market and sell the defective vehicles,” including the 2021 Model S Plaid that allegedly devastated the Murphys’ house.

In an email, attorney Samuel Heller, who is representing the Murphys, told The Independent that the experience “certainly has been tragic” for the family, but declined to comment further, citing active litigation.

A Tesla spokesperson did not respond Friday to a request for comment.

Michael and Sylvana Murphy raised their two daughters in a waterfront home on the western side of Tampa’s Interbay Peninsula, according to their complaint. The local Toyota dealership Murphy owns provided him a 2021 Tesla Model S Plaid for business and personal use, it explains.

Murphy kept the Tesla parked every night in the ground floor garage “beneath the home where his wife and daughters slept, trusting it as he would any other car he parked in his own garage,” the complaint goes on.

On September 26, 2024, Hurricane Helene struck Tampa Bay as a Category 4 hurricane, causing the worst storm surge the area had seen in more than 100 years.

When Helene made landfall, Murphy was in California on business and could not get home, as all air travel was shut down in advance of the storm, the complaint states. But, it says, Sylvana, the Murphys’ two daughters, and Sylvana’s parents were inside the house.

open image in gallery Tesla CEO Elon Musk and President Donald Trump in a Tesla Model S, the same vehicle type that exploded and destroyed a Tampa Bay home, allegedly due to faulty batteries that can catch fire when exposed to saltwater ( Getty Images )

Because the Murphy home sat directly on the water, it was exposed to the full force of that surge, the complaint states. As saltwater entered the garage, the Tesla’s undercarriage was soon submerged, the complaint continues.

“Soon thereafter, [Sylvana] heard a loud explosion coming from the garage,” the complaint states.

She then went downstairs to find the Tesla in flames and fire spreading quickly throughout the garage, according to the complaint.

Within minutes, a fire ignited underneath the Tesla and completely consumed the garage, the complaint contends. Rising floodwaters cut off all access for emergency vehicles, leaving Sylvana and the others helpless inside the burning home with no avenue for escape and first responders unable to get through.

Thousands of miles away and powerless to do anything himself, Murphy contacted Grey Bull Rescue, a Tampa-based organization run by former military personnel that the family has long supported, the complaint states. Against the odds, the complaint says a Grey Bull team managed to reach the Murphy home by boat and spirited Sylvana and the others to safety.

“Without Grey Bull Rescue’s efforts, there would have been no way for the family to escape and they would have died in the fire,” the complaint asserts.

Still, it says, the fire eventually rampaged throughout the entire five-bed, six-bath residence, ruining, “in a single moment, every piece of property the family had spent their lives accumulating.” Even worse, the complaint states, the fire burned so hot, and spread so fast, that rescuers could not reach the family dog, who died in the blaze.

open image in gallery A federal lawsuit claims Tesla knew its batteries were unsafe and alleges the company ignored warnings, concealing the issue from the public ( Getty Images )

The explosion was caused by, according to the complaint, “the batteries themselves and the design of the battery pack,” and says Tesla “knew about this defect and concealed it from its customers.”

The company, which is owned by Elon Musk – the world’s richest person and a staunch supporter of President Donald Trump – has been aware of the issue since at least 2010, when it filed patents for fire retardant material meant to mitigate the tendency for lithium-ion batteries to enter so-called “thermal runaway,” an uncontrollable, self-heating chain reaction where a rise in temperature triggers chemical reactions that generate even more heat.

In 2022, U.S. Sen. Rick Scott (R-FL) warned that lithium-ion batteries exposed to saltwater can set off thermal runaway, and wrote a letter to the Department of Transportation asking the agency to do something about it. He said electric vehicle fires have destroyed homes that would have otherwise survived hurricanes, and that area fire departments have been forced to steer much-needed resources away from other pressing issues in order to control the fires, which can take up to six hours to extinguish.

A Pinellas County home went up in flames, also during Hurricane Helene, when floodwaters engulfed a Tesla parked in the garage and reportedly burned the house down within 15 minutes.

Another Tampa home was burned to the ground in Helene, allegedly due to a Tesla catching fire in the garage after being exposed to saltwater.

open image in gallery Electric vehicle fires burn hotter and longer than those involving gas-powered cars, according to experts ( AFP via Getty Images )

The blazes are not limited to interactions with water. In 2024, former NFL player Randall Cobb’s home in Nashville, Tennessee, burned down when a defective Tesla charging cable caused an arc that caused some $4 million worth of damage.

Tesla’s advertising claims that electric vehicles catch fire less often than gas-powered ones. At the same time, lithium-ion battery fires burn hotter and are much more difficult to extinguish. In one astonishing example, a Tesla Cybertruck that rolled into a ditch burst into flames so intense, the driver's skeletal system literally disintegrated, according to a lawsuit later filed by his widow.

The Murphys’ complaint says Tesla “had access to safer battery protection for years, including its own patented intumescent fire retardant material, and did not use it.”

Even though Tesla knew of the dangers, it “told the public the opposite,” according to the complaint.

“It represented that its vehicles were safe, that its safety systems increased safety, and that it could prove a Tesla was safer to drive than any other electric vehicle on the market,” the complaint maintains. “Ultimately, Tesla had more than a decade to fix these known defects and chose, over and over, not to.”

The Murphys say Tesla was negligent in allowing vehicles with serious “design and manufacturing defects” to be sold. They are demanding a judgment for damages, punitive damages, and “any other relief deemed proper,” to be determined by a jury.

Zohran Mamdani has responded to reports that Man City have been found guilty of the Premier League charges by highlighting “114”.

The mayor of New York City, and an avid Arsenal fan, pointed out the reported number of breaches the Premier League club have been found guilty of, with the club initially facing a total of 115 charges.

The Independent understands that the former champions have been found guilty of breaking the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

And just hours after the landmark ruling, which was first reported by The Athletic, Mamdani simply posted on social media: “114”.

Mamdani has displayed his affection for the Gunners, who pipped City for the title last season to break a 22-year drought, in recent months, including an appearance at Eid al-Adha prayers in the Bronx while wearing a club-themed kurta.

Mamdani recalled supporting Arsenal from the age of nine thanks to his uncle and idolised players such as Tony Adams and, particularly, Nwankwo Kanu, given the Nigerian “had been born in Africa but now lived somewhere else, just like me.”

Mamdani told the New York Times about how Arsenal had become an escape for him and recalled the intense battles with City in recent seasons: “Over these past two years, no matter how chaotic life became, Arsenal remained the constant.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has reacted to the verdict over Man City's charges ( Reuters )

“And throughout every moment, when a Manchester City resurgence felt inevitable, when the socialist project felt fragile, when both football and politics appeared determined to reward only wealth and cynicism, I have returned to the words of a man with no enemies: Bukayo Saka. “It’s a process.” And we should trust it.”

And while the Gunners would not benefit directly, should Premier League titles be rescinded and handed to the runners-up during that nine-year period, City did edge out Arsene Wenger’s side in the 2018 Carabao Cup final.

City are currently top of the Premier League after five games, three points clear of the defending champions Arsenal.

But with sanctions to follow over the alleged breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, Arsenal are positioned to benefit and remain favourites to claim a second title in as many seasons under Mikel Arteta.

Mamdani’s Arsenal could return to the top of the Premier League should they secure a heavy victory over Leeds on 10 October before City’s next game against Liverpool on 11 October.

Family and friends of one of Britain’s greatest living explorers, Sir Ranulph Fiennes, have called for an investigation into his care arrangements after allegations he has been illegally placed in a series of care homes under a fake name by his wife.

Those close to the 82-year-old want the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) to establish whether his wife Louise Millington-Cotes, 59, is correctly discharging her duties as his legal guardian.

John Simpson, the veteran BBC foreign correspondent and friend of Sir Ranulph, has joined the calls for transparency. In a post on X he wrote: “Horrified to hear what’s happened to my good friend Ran Fiennes.

“I’d like to tell the relevant authorities everything I know about the way he’s been treated. He’s the world’s bravest man, and he’s vulnerable. We must know what’s happening to him.”

Alexander Millington-Cotes, Sir Ranulph’s stepson and Mrs Millington-Cotes’s estranged son, told The Telegraph he called the OPG and spoke to their safeguarding team, but had “heard nothing back so far”.

open image in gallery The Care Inspectorate of Wales concluded Sir Ranulph was being ‘unlawfully deprived of his liberty’ ( Getty )

It comes after a watchdog concluded the retired explorer, who has not been seen in public in two years, has been “unlawfully deprived of his liberty”, according to The Telegraph.

It has been claimed that his wife put extreme conditions on how he is looked after, and not allowed him to see friends or family.

A care home owner in Wales, where Sir Ranulph had been placed for seven weeks this year, spoke to the newspaper, saying they had reported several concerns about Sir Ranulph’s wellbeing to the authorities, including the police.

They reportedly approached the OPG to raise concerns about his wife’s medical arrangements for him, as well as a “do not resuscitate” document that she had provided.

The care home owner also raised concerns with the Care Inspectorate of Wales, which declared Sir Ranulph was being unlawfully kept in care homes and unable to consent to his care or treatment.

In an email seen by the newspaper, the care inspectorate wrote: “Currently [Sir Ranulph] is being deprived of his liberty unlawfully as there is no authorised deprivation in place which reflects the current residence and restrictions in place.

“[Sir Ranulph] is under continuous supervision and control, is not free to leave and is not able to consent to care, treatment and accommodation.

“As such, the provider is required to make an urgent and standard application under the deprivation of liberty safeguards as soon as practicable.”

The care home owner said Mrs Millington-Cotes provided a private carer, gave staff at the home strict instructions on his day-to-day activities and provided all of his medication, rather than registering him with a local GP.

Mrs Millington-Cotes was told by the owner that she must ensure that a deprivation of liberty safeguards (DoLS) order was in place as his legal guardian, but failed to ever provide one.

The owner emailed her to express the urgency of the situation, which led to “a falling out with her because she didn’t want us to apply for a DoLS”.

open image in gallery Sir Ranulph’s stepson is crowdfunding a legal challenge to his mother’s lasting power of attorney ( Getty )

Sir Ranulph had reportedly spent time in a care home in London, before being moved to a facility in Wales, and then to one in Cheshire.

The Telegraph reported last week that Sir Ranulph’s visitors were made to sign non-disclosure agreements by his wife if they wanted to visit him at the care home in London.

Sir Ranulph’s stepson Alexander Millington-Cotes visited the care home in Cheshire last week and was told by staff his stepfather was not there. He is now crowdfunding a legal challenge to his mother’s lasting power of attorney.

An OPG spokesperson said: “A Lasting Power of Attorney is an important way to ensure that certain decisions about care and finances are made by someone you trust if you lack the capacity to make them yourself. We cannot comment on individual cases.”

The Care Inspectorate have been approached for comment. The Independent was unable to contact Mrs Millington-Cotes.

Margot Robbie has surprised fans by discreetly taking her husband’s name.

In a new business listing available via the U.K. government’s Companies House, Robbie is named as “Margot Elise Ackerley” on the registry for LuckyChap Entertainment, the production company she runs with husband Tom Ackerley.

The name change comes ahead of her 10th wedding anniversary with Ackerley this December. In previous documentation, the Barbie star was named as Margot Elise Robbie.

In recent years, there has been speculation that the actor had taken Acklerly’s name in her personal life, while continuing to use Robbie in her professional life. She was listed as Margot Robbie in the credits for her latest project, Sterling Point, the coming-of-age drama she co-produced through LuckyChap Entertainment.

Some fans of Robbie have been shocked at the name change, as one person wrote online: “It doesn’t have the same ring to it.”

open image in gallery Margot Robbie has used her husband’s surname on business documents for their production company, LuckyChap Entertainment ( AFP/Getty )

Another person suggested that taking her husband’s name somehow contradicted the feminist values in her film Barbie, writing on X: “Barbie would never have done that... Barbie would never take a man's last name.”

Others were more complimentary, as one person wrote: “Margot Ackerley sounds really elegant.”

“Margot Ackerley sounds like a Victorian novelist name and I mean that as the highest compliment,” commented another.

“Wishing them both nothing but the best,” added another fan.

Robbie met her husband on the set of the World War II drama Suite Française in 2013. Robbie was an actor on the rise at the time, having enjoyed success as a soap star playing Donna Freedman in Neighbours. Ackerley, who is from Guildford, England, was working on the film as an assistant director.

open image in gallery Robbie met her husband on the set of the World War II drama ‘Suite Française’, in 2013 ( AFP/Getty )

They began dating and founded LuckyChap Entertainment together a year later. The production company has since been behind films such as I, Tonya, Birds of Prey, Barbie, Saltburn and Wuthering Heights.

The couple has kept their relationship out of the spotlight and married in a private ceremony in Byron Bay, Australia, in December 2016. Their son was born in October 2024.

“[We spend] 24 hours a day [together],” Ackerley previously told The Sunday Times about how their personal and professional lives cross over.

“It’s seamless. We don’t have a toggle on, toggle off. It’s all become one thing,” he said.

Asked whether they ever have arguments at home, Ackerley said the topic that he and Robbie clash over is chocolate cookies – specifically “whether Tim Tams or Penguins are better”.

Investigators believe Tasia Fortune was already dead before the Black woman's body was hanged from a tree behind an abandoned home in the Mississippi capital this summer, a detective testified Friday.

The hanging of Tasia Fortune's body, which was found on Aug. 3, was “staged," Jackson police Det. Samuel Dukes testified, citing the medical examiner's opinion.

Authorities haven't disclosed the exact cause of Fortune's death, but they did rule it a homicide and have arrested two men, both of them Black, on murder charges and issued a warrant for the arrest of a third person.

Dukes also testified that the motive for the killing appears to have been a drug dispute. He said interviews with others revealed that Fortune fought hard before she was killed.

The case has attracted widespread attention because the scene recalled lynchings in the Southern state, which has a long and troubled history of racial violence.

Authorities haven't said why they believe the defendants hanged Fortune's body after she was already dead.

Dukes testified at a hearing for Jarques Ratliff, 51, who was the first person arrested in the case earlier this month. Ratliff remains in custody in the Hinds County jail without bond. The hearing will resume Sept. 30.

Police arrested the second defendant, 25-year-old Earnest Lloyd Jr., this week.

During Friday's hearing, Ratliff said that Fortune had been a friend of his.

Fortune's mother, Christy Spivey, has said her daughter, who had four children, struggled with homelessness in recent years, and that she wasn’t sure where Fortune was living at the time of her death. She said Fortune had talked about starting a cleaning business and was trying to get her life in order.

President Donald Trump is approaching the midterm elections with a historic 50 percent of Americans strongly disapproving of his job performance — shattering the rejection record he set before the 2018 midterms, CNN's polling guru said Friday.

“They don't just dislike him,” Harry Enten said. “There's record hatred for the president of the United States going into a midterm.”

Trump also fares worse with independent voters, with 56 percent expressing strong disapproval, Enten said.

"Among the group that determines elections in this country, you see the hatred for the president of the United States. This is what the voters are saying now," he said.

The White House didn’t immediately return an inquiry from The Independent.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump gets a record-high 50 percent ‘strongly disapprove’ rating from Americans ahead of the November midterm elections ( AFP via Getty Images )

Enten said Trump’s overall 50 percent “strongly disapprove” rating eclipses the 45 percent he notched in 2016.

Before that, President George W. Bush held the record when 41 percent of Americans strongly disapproved of his job performance ahead of the 2006 midterm elections, according to CNN’s chief data analyst.

And while Trump's “historically polarizing” effect on American voters has sometimes worked to his benefit, Enten said, it's not doing so now.

That's because the president's “strongly approve” rating is just 18 percent, one-third less than the average 27 percent for previous presidents going into the midterms — including Trump in 2018, Enten said.

“So, Trump actually has fewer people loving him than what we see with the average president,” he said. “What's going on here is normally Trump is able to counteract that strong hatred with strong love, but not anymore.”

open image in gallery CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten says Trump broke the record 45 percent ‘strongly disapprove’ rating he set before the 2018 midterms ( CNN )

The 2018 midterms took place during Trump's first term, when Democrats flipped six seats in the House and two in the Senate, but failed to win a majority in either chamber.

But Trump is now a lame duck, like Bush was in 2006, when Democrats gained control of both chambers by flipping 31 seats in the House and five in the Senate, along with two seats won by independents who caucused with them.

The latest so-called generic congressional ballot polling average shows Democrats with an 8.7 percent edge over Republicans, according to data posted Friday by Real Clear Polling.

Democrats have enjoyed an “incredible upswing” during September, when they began with a generic congressional ballot lead of 6.7 percent, according to the Silver Bulletin.

That's now up to 8.1 percent, or 8.8 percent with a “likely voter” adjustment, according to the Silver Bulletin.

The Cook Political Report also said that Democrats were on track to gain control of the House, with 15 races shifting in their favor, largely because voters are unhappy with Trump’s handling of the economy.

Democrats now hold 215 House seats and need just three more for a majority.

The Republican advantage in the Senate is 53-47, and The Cook Political Report described it Wednesday as a “true toss-up” after three races shifted toward Democrats.

A verdict over Premier League charges against Manchester City is finally set to be delivered after a bombshell report said the club have been “found guilty on almost all of the charges”.

The Athletic reported on Friday that the former champions have been found guilty of breaking the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018, in what would be a seminal moment for the richest football league in the world.

The landmark ruling follows one of the most significant court cases in the history of sport, with the verdict also having major repercussions for City’s rivals. The Premier League have declined to comment, however.

City, currently top of the Premier League after five games, were charged with over 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules in February 2023, with the club always denying any wrongdoing throughout the process.

An independent commission was appointed following a four-year investigation. Sanctions have not yet been decided, according to The Athletic, and City are expected to appeal. A club spokesperson said the Premier League process “remains ongoing”.

City have been England’s most successful team since the club’s fortunes were transformed by Sheikh Mansour’s takeover in 2008. There are a wide range of punishments available to the top-flight’s authorities. Sanctions could include fines and/or points deductions, and even expulsion as a member of the Premier League.

News.title: Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges
News.content:
Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been announced.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise questions marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

The charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

Of the 115 charges:

Fifty-four were for failing to provide accurate financial information from 2009-10 to 2017-18

Fourteen were for failing to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from the same period

Five were for failing to comply with Uefa’s rules from 2013-14 to 2017-18

Seven were for breaching Premier League profitability and sustainability rules from 2015-16 to 2017-18

Thirty-five were for failing to co-operate with the investigation from 2018-23.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

Case is far from being resolved

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

It would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

News.title: Britain sends team to South Sudan as country braces for Ebola
News.content:
British Ebola specialists have been deployed to South Sudan because of fears the haemorrhagic fever will spread from neighbouring Congo.

A rare form of Ebola, known as the Bundibugyo species, is spreading rapidly in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 7,800 people have caught the virus since May, 3,700 of whom have died.

To prepare for the threat of imported cases, Britain has positioned three experts in and around the South Sudanese capital, Juba. They will assist and train local authorities on infection control, set up awareness campaigns for local communities, and test people crossing the border for the virus.

The team is employed by the UK Health Security Agency’s (UKHSA) Public Health Rapid Support Team (PHRST), which is regularly sent to the epicentre of disease outbreaks overseas – for instant the cruise ship at the centre of a deadly hantavirus in the South Atlantic earlier this year.

The current Ebola outbreak is the fastest-growing ever recorded and is on course to become the largest in history, overtaking the 2014-16 West Africa Ebola outbreak, in which around 30,000 people contracted the haemorrhagic fever and roughly a third died.

Experts fear it is only a matter of time before the virus spreads to South Sudan, which shares a 500-mile border with the DRC. Thousands of people cross the frontier each day to work, attend school and trade goods, mostly fish, in lucrative markets between the two countries.

If the virus gained a foothold in South Sudan, which became the newest country on earth after severing ties with Khartoum in 2011, experts fear the consequences would be catastrophic and worsen an already dire humanitarian situation.

“It’s so variable as to where the outbreak is spreading at the moment, there are cases from some of the border towns [with South Sudan],” Ed Newman, director of the PHRST, told The Telegraph.

“There’s a feeling [Ebola could spread] any day. Maybe you could say we’ve been lucky so far,” Mr Newman said, on the sidelines of a UKHSA conference in Manchester.

News.title: Russell capitalises on Antonelli error to take Azerbaijan GP pole
News.content:
Russell – who begins the weekend 81 points behind the Italian – simply has to capitalise. And he really should do. Even if Antonelli hadn’t crashed out, he has looked on a different level this weekend, dominating practice and qualifying. Russell topped Q1, Q3 and Q3, securing the 12th pole of his career with a lap which was nine tenths quicker than his best lap in Q2 and eight tenths quicker than Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, the next fastest driver. He could hardly believe it himself.

“That was a pretty decent lap,” he told his team over the radio on his cooldown lap. “How much was [the gap]?”

“Just over eight tenths to Leclerc.” came the response. “Woah!”

This has not been the easiest season for Russell, who began the year the overwhelming favourite for the title, having dominated his younger team-mate over the course of last season. So he could be forgiven for feeling proud of having done such a good job.

“It’s been a while so it definitely feels good,” he admitted. “This was probably the biggest pole margin of my whole career, including my F2 and F3 days.

“The lap felt really sweet, car’s been feeling really great this weekend. On a track like this where you can hug it, it feels amazing.”

News.title: Buttler injury derails England chase and sends Sri Lanka series to decider
News.content:
Enter Buttler to play a wonderful counter-attack, whacking Wellalage for four and six and dumping leg-spinner Sachindu Colombage over the rope twice as he raced to 41 off 22 balls.

Buttler was at a crossroads after the T20 World Cup in February. Despite England making the semi-finals, he averaged just 10 in the tournament to complete a third poor World Cup in a row. A break with his family, and a very good Indian Premier League, where he made a crucial technical correction, changed his fortunes.

Matthew Hayden, the batting coach at the Gujarat Titans, asked him whether he was watching the ball closely enough. Buttler discovered that, now 36, he is a right-eye dominant batsman, so with Hayden’s help he opened up his stance to give himself a better view of the ball. A summer rich in runs has followed with an average of 51 for England and a strut back in his body language. The injury has surely ended Buttler’s summer and there are worries that he could be out of the Pakistan ODI triangular tournament next month as well, just to add to the night’s woes.

This was not a vintage England performance. Atkinson made a crucial error on the boundary, dropping a straightforward chance off Kusal Mendis on 17. It kickstarted Mendis, who went on the charge smashing 51 in 24 balls. He put on 137 in 120 balls with Kuminda Mendis. Josh Tongue had an off day going at seven an over and Jofra Archer was given similar treatment, although he bowled better than figures suggest, as anything wayward with pace on the ball was hit away.

Overton was more effective with his cutters and slower balls, while Ahmed did at least bag a couple of wickets, credit for keeping his head after some early rough treatment. Kusal Mendis was given out leg before on 99 but overturned the decision and stroked a four next ball for a deserved hundred.

Thanks for joining me. A global rout in bond markets deepened overnight as traders expect the US to keep raising interest rates.

Japan’s 10-year bond yield surged to 3.08pc on Thursday, its highest level since 1996, as markets responded to stronger than expected US economic data and higher oil prices.

It followed sharp rises in the US on Wednesday, when the yield on 10-year Treasuries – a benchmark of global borrowing costs – surged as high as 5.12pc, up from 4.96pc. It was the biggest jump since the “liberation day” tariff turmoil in April last year.

Bonds were sent into turmoil as traders bet that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates three times by April next year in an effort to bring down inflation. Money markets suggest there is a 70pc chance of the Fed following this month’s first rate rise in three years with a second in October.

This followed closely watched industry data on Wednesday, known as PMIs, showed US private sector activity jumped unexpectedly to a five-year high in September.

Meanwhile, oil prices spiked 3.9pc on Wednesday to move back above $100 a barrel, risking an inflationary spiral in the world economy.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “The main driver was a strong batch of PMIs, along with a rebound in oil prices, which both led to mounting speculation about faster rate hikes.” Here is what you need to know.
