What happened overnight

Debt markets were in turmoil after Japanese bond yields hit 30-year highs.

As Tokyo markets reopened after a three-day holiday, the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield jumped to its highest level since 1996.

This came after a steep sell-off in the US market overnight. Oil prices remained around $103 a barrel and the dollar held gains after Tehran’s leader vowed to never surrender following a warning by Donald Trump that he could “annihilate” Iran.

Japan’s benchmark stock market, the Nikkei 225 rose 1pc to 65,645.10, as some chipmakers got a boost from the recent interest in AI. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.7pc to 8,702.00.

News.title: Zelensky lashes out at EU
News.content:
Volodymyr Zelensky lashed out at the European Union over its moves to weaken sanctions on Russian oligarchs.

In his address to the UN General Assembly, the Ukrainian leader warned that beyond making life “more comfortable” for Russians, “it also gives the war more time for Putin to send poor people into the kill zone. So Russia’s revenues must remain a target.”

His criticism came after France and Luxembourg successfully pushed for sanctions exemptions for Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, Russian oligarchs, on Tuesday.

Kyiv branded the decision “shameful and unjustifiable”. The men are known to share close ties to Vladimir Putin and have net worths of $14bn and $16bn, respectively.

In his fourth address to the UN as a wartime leader, Mr Zelensky said it was paramount that the international community increased pressure on the Kremlin to stop “the madness” of the war spreading.

Under pressure from Donald Trump to halt attacks on Russian energy targets, Mr Zelensky defended his country’s aerial offensive for successfully depriving Putin of revenue for his war.

“When someone gives Russia more money through trade, they give this war more time. And that is exactly why we insist on limiting trade with the aggressor, and why we are burning Russia’s revenues ourselves,” he said.

‘End the war before winter’

Washington has recently attempted to revive the long-stalled negotiations between Ukraine and Russia. On Tuesday, Mr Zelensky implored Mr Trump to help Kyiv end the war “before winter”.

Mr Trump appeared optimistic, suggesting an agreement would happen “more quickly than people understand”.

Sergei Lavrov, the Russian foreign minister, told the UN Security Council on Wednesday that Russia was prepared to negotiate for a lasting peace but would not “pause the war”.

Mr Zelensky sought to remind world leaders that the conflict was not constrained within Ukraine’s borders at a time when the global community was distracted by a myriad of conflicts and crises.

Citing the support of Iran and North Korea for Russia, he warned that Putin’s war kept “spreading further”.

“Putin is always looking for someone who can help him kill more, kill more people for every kilometre of land, take more territory and take another country instead of simply stopping and running his own country,” Mr Zelensky said at the UN.

He noted that fighters from at least 47 countries were helping to prosecute Moscow’s war against Ukraine and urged leaders to prevent their citizens from being dragged into the conflict.

After Mr Zelensky’s address, reports emerged that Kirill Dmitriev, Putin’s envoy, was on his way to the US where he would meet Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the Trump administration representatives.

Sources told Reuters that the meeting would take place in New ‌York on the sidelines of the UN summit.

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, also confirmed Mr Trump had invited his Russian counterpart to attend the G20 summit of world leaders in Miami in December.

News.title: Male contraceptives could hit pharmacies in ‘three to five years’, says WHO
News.content:
Game-changing contraceptives for men could be on pharmacy shelves as soon as 2029, according to the World Health Organization.

Speaking to the Telegraph, Dr James Kiarie, head of the UN agency’s contraception and fertility care unit, said he expects male birth control to be available in just a few years, in a major expansion of contraceptive options for men.

“In three to five years, we will actually have a method available, [so] men can be more than supporters of their female partners in using contraception – men can actually be users,” he said.

On Tuesday, the WHO released its first Target Product Profiles (TPPs) for these products, setting out guidelines for the desired and minimum standards any male contraceptive product must meet.

“[The TPPs] signals that this is a priority issue for the WHO,” said Dr Kiarie.

“Currently men do not have much option in terms of their contraceptive methods. They have to either use condoms… [or] they have to use withdrawal, which has a high failure rate, or they have to use vasectomy, which is a permanent method.”

At the moment, the most advanced new product is called NES/T. It is a daily hormonal gel that is applied to the shoulders and upper arms, and suppresses sperm production without affecting testosterone levels.

Other candidates include injectable hydrogels that block sperm travel, an approach that has been described as a “reversible vasectomy”. ADAM, developed by Contraline, is in phase 1 trials while Next Life Sciences is set to trial a similar product called Plan A.

A third option is YCT-529 – the first non-hormonal, daily male birth control pill. It is currently in phase 1b and 2a clinical trials.

Dr Kiarie said it was important to have multiple options as “there’s no one size fits all” approach, but warned development could take longer than five years if clinical trials face unexpected hurdles.

The French defender spent two seasons in the Prem in the hope he could transform into Vincent Kompany’s long-term partner.

Instead he started a journeyman career on loan across Europe.



And then came the big guns.

City broke their transfer record to bring the former Chelsea midfielder Kevin De Bruyne – at £55m – back to England from Wolfsburg.

Alongside him former Three Lions star Raheem Sterling, who made the shock move from Liverpool as one of the most expensive English players ever at the time at £44m.

And once Guardiola had arrived, he wasted no time getting stars in the squad who could shape the next decade.

Pep’s first City purchase was Ilkay Gundogan, brought in from Borussia Dortmund for around £21m.



He waded through serious early injury trouble BUT ultimately became captain, a serial title winner and one of the club’s most decisive midfielders.

John Stones, who arrived from Everton for around £47.5m, became one of the most expensive defenders in history at the time.

Winger Leroy Sane followed from Schalke with a £37m price tag attached.



The winger impressed in his debut season, even winning the PFA Young Player of the Year award during another title-winning season in 2017/18.

But Guardiola and City were not going to call time there.

They went on to complete a major shopping spree in the transfer market picking up the likes of Kyle Walker (£45m), Bernardo Silva (£43m), and Ederson (£35m).

City also got the chequebook out for Monaco left-back Benjamin Mendy (£49.5m) and Real Madrid’s Danilo (£25.8m), before Aymeric Laporte (£55.9m) arrived in January 2018.

And from that they saw results, on results.

THOMAS TUCHEL has sensationally questioned whether Cole Palmer wants to play for England after his latest international withdrawal.

The Three Lions manager, preparing for the Nations League opener against Spain at Wembley tomorrow, has warned the Chelsea forward that he does not feature enough for his country and this is a “missed opportunity”.



Palmer, 24, although not selected for the World Cup, has only played three games for Tuchel and this is the FOURTH time he has withdrawn from a senior squad.

It was put to Tuchel, 53, that it sounds as though Palmer does not want to play for England. The German said: “It’s hard to argue against what you’re saying.



“It leaves us with Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers, Morgan Gibbs-White and Eberechi Eze. All in camp. All desperate to be here. All available. And all ready to go, ready to stop a holiday after one day in Dubai [Gibbs-White].”

Tuchel was also asked what advice he would give to in-form Palmer if he was his friend.

Tuchel said: “I am not his friend. I am his national team coach and I can only judge him on what he is delivering for the national team and he is just missing too many opportunities.

“He misses too many opportunities and I don’t blame him for it. It is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries.

“I only want to rely on what I personally witness and what I see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp, there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve.

“You can only leave when you are actually with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch so, yes it is a missed opportunity.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“My understanding is that he faces discomfort and pain and he cannot compete on the highest level.

“He just informed us, or Chelsea did. That is my understanding. We are not managing load.”

Kobbie Mainoo, Declan Rice, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento are the other players who pulled out.

Yet Tuchel appears convinced that the quartet’s fitness concerns are genuine.



Tuchel said: “Every case is individual and if Declan calls me and explains to me…and I actually saw him play v Brighton… I see straightaway on TV that something is off, and he just confirmed that impression

“Every case is different and I knew from Marcus, I knew from Kobbie that they play with discomfort and they try to be available for their clubs.

“I know that it looks strange if a player, not only Cole but Kobbie and Marcus, finish a match at the weekend for their club and then suddenly are not here but okay, first of all, in doubt, we trust the players.

“I have no reason not to trust them because they were with us in the US and they were fantastic.

“There is always a slight dropout and Tino Livramento is also injured. This is just what happens. In total with Dan Burn out, with John Stones out, with Deano Henderson who played with a fractured foot for some matches – it is just what is happening.”



Palmer’s pal Morgan Rogers said: “Unfortunately, he couldn’t be here, but I think he’s got to focus on his body as well and what he went through last year. He needs to be in a good physical state as well, and that obviously comes first as players.”

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho and Jurgen Klopp waiting in wings for Premier League titles as amazing comments about Man City resurface
Sports.content:
Next

JOSE MOURINHO and Jurgen Klopp’s comments about winning extra titles have resurfaced after Man City were found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules.

City were found to have breached all but one of the Prem’s 115 charges in a bombshell verdict on Friday.



It’s not known what punishment the club will face, but it has been suggested they could be handed a points deduction or even relegation.

City have always denied the charges and are expected to launch an immediate appeal.



The club were charged by the Premier League following an investigation into alleged breaches between 2009 and 2018.

The stunning news has led to fans questioning whether City will be stripped of their titles.

City won three Prem titles in that time period in 2012, 2014 and 2018.

That last one saw City make history by winning the title with 100 points as Manchester United finished second on 81 points.

And Mourinho – who managed United in that season – previously said he hadn’t given up hope of having a fourth title added to his record ahead of City’s verdict.

He said in October 2024: “As you know, we won the Europa League [in 2017] and we finished second in the Premier League [in 2018],” he said.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I think we still have a chance to win that league because maybe they punish Man City with points and maybe we win that league and then they have to pay me the bonus and give me the medal.”

And Klopp also teased the idea of Liverpool being awarded at least two titles after coming second to City in 2019 and 2022.

He was asked during a Q&A with comedian John Bishop: “You leave this club having won the Premier League once.

“There could be a court decision that means you’ve won the Premier League three times…”

Klopp cheekily replied: “If you organise a bus parade, I’m in! How long it takes I don’t care.”



However, it’s unlikely that Liverpool would be awarded those two titles – even if Man City were stripped of titles – as they happened after the period where the alleged offences were committed.

The initial investigation came about after German outlet Der Spiegel published leaked financial documents from City in November 2018.

REAL MADRID could make a major change to their transfer dealings to accommodate Jose Mourinho’s request for a new central midfielder.

Los Blancos have historically avoided signing new players in January due to the inflated market prices, as well as clubs’ reluctance to lose their best players midway through the season.



But a report from Defensa Central suggests that Real could be about to make an overhaul to that long-standing policy following a mixed start to the season.

Real have won five of their seven league games to date, and were most recently beaten 2-1 by Atletico Madrid in an ill-tempered derby on September 20.



It is believed that a specific player has yet to be identified, but Real president Florentino Perez could approve a move into the market if Mourinho finds the right player.

They strengthened their midfield in the summer with the arrival of Bernardo Silva on a free transfer from Manchester City, complementing a stacked list of options which also includes Federico Valverde, Aureline Tchouameni, Eduardo Camavinga and Arda Guler.



The 15-time European champions were involved in a well-documented pursuit of Bernardo’s former Man City team-mate Rodri, who ultimately completed a summer move to Barcelona instead.

Whether Real sign a new midfielder will hinge on Thiago Pitarch’s development, with Mourinho eager to give the 19-year-old further opportunities to impress.

Pitarch made 16 appearances for Los Blancos last season, but was ruled out at the start of the season due to a ligament injury.

The Spanish giants’ have rarely made moves in January with Perez at the helm, with Emmanuel Adebayor and Thomas Gravesen being two of the most prominent exceptions.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Arguably their best January signing in recent years came when Marcelo arrived in January 2007, but Ramon Calderon was president at the time.

The Brazilian will go down as one of the club’s greatest-ever left-backs, making 548 appearances and scoring 38 goals, winning five Champions League titles in the process.

One of the highest-profile January flops came in 2009 when Julien Faubert arrived on loan from West Ham United, but made just two appearances for Los Blancos from the bench and failed to make a start.

For now, Mourinho’s main focus will be on Real’s next game against Villarreal at the Bernabeu on Saturday October 10, 2026.

Sports.title: Former Premier League wildman, 39, now ranked as a top 1 per cent PADEL star after making shock sporting switch

HATEM BEN ARFA has been known for causing a racquet on the football pitch and he is now doing that literally in the world of padel.

The Frenchman, 39, made a name for himself on these shores during an eventful four-year spell at Newcastle, but is now recognised for being one of the finest padel players on the other side of the Channel.



Ben Arfa is now ranked within the top 0.5 per cent of players in France, impressively placing him at 761st from 151,126 players.

He is not the only former French footballing star to play the sport, with the likes of Didier Deschamps, Patrick Vieira and Zinedine Zidane also listed in the French padel rankings of celebrities to play the sport.



A story from Le Parisien three years ago charted Ben Arfa’s eye-catching switch to padel, with referee Roland Mermillod shedding light on his dedication to the sport.

He said: “Hatem doesn’t do anything more than that. He plays almost every day.”



That dedication is all the more impressive in a chequered playing career when Ben Arfa’s undoubted playing talent was marred by moments of controversy.

He began his career with Lyon, before moving on to Marseille in 2008 after a training ground incident with Sebastian Squillaci.

Controversy was never far away from Ben Arfa, who had a training ground bust-up with then- Olympians manager Didier Deschamps.

An initial season-long loan move to St James’ Park followed in August 2010, which would turn into a permanent move five months later.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

After scoring on his full debut against Everton, an horrific leg break marred his first season, but showed glimpses of his undoubted talent in the following 2011/12 campaign.

He netted a superb individual goal in an FA Cup third round tie against Blackburn, before netting an equally impressive strike against Bolton Wanderers in a 2-0 victory.

But Ben Arfa made headlines for his exploits off the pitch following some heated clashes with Pardew, and received a driving ban.

Ben Arfa moved on to Hull City on loan in 2014, before returning to France with Nice a year later, ahead of spells with Paris Saint-Germain, Rennes, Valladolid, Bordeaux, and Lille.

His most recent moment of controversy came at Lille in 2022 with then manager Jocelyn Gourvennec and president Olivier Letang.



The former French star’s footballing exploits – both good and bad – appear to be in the past, but was reportedly close to rejoining Nice in January, according to a report by Nice-Matin.

That return never materialised though, and Ben Arfa will be eager to make further strides in the world of padel in the coming months.

Sports.title: Man City’s Premier League dominance will never be viewed the same with Aguero’s iconic goal now coming with an asterisk
Sports.content:
Next

ON May 13, 2012, Sergio Aguero delivered the most iconic moment in Premier League history.

The Manchester City striker jinked his way through the QPR defence in the 94th minute to score the final goal of the season – and pip neighbours United to the title on goal difference.



It sparked Martin Tyler’s infamous ‘Aguerooooooo’ commentary that has been replayed millions of times since those crazy, chaotic scenes at the Etihad Stadium.

And yet now that Prem title is set to come with an asterisk.



Then there is Steven Gerrard’s astonishing Anfield slip against Chelsea two years later, immortalised by cackling rival fans for more than a decade.

That was pure misery for the Scouse legend – and no longer to be taken at face value.



And don’t forget Jose Mourinho, who said finishing runners-up to Pep Guardiola’s side in 2017-18 was among his finest moments.

The self-styled Special One might now have a genuine right to that title bonus he claimed from the Old Trafford board.

Whatever punishment against City is eventually meted out by the Prem’s three-man independent commission, everything has been rendered differently by their verdict.

After a seven-year probe, legal bills stretching into the tens of millions of pounds and a private hearing that started 24 months ago, it seems that City, for all their claims of innocence, their indignation and fury, were bang to rights.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

What were Man City charged with? MAN CITY have been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges they were initially hit with. Those charges were upped to 130 and fit into the following six categories… Failing to give accurate financial information over sponsorship revenue, related parties and operating costs between 2009-10 and 2017/18. Total charges: 50

Failing to provide full details of managerial remuneration between 2009/10 and 2012/13. Total charges 8

Failing to provide full details of player remuneration between 2010/11 and 2015/16. Total charges 12

Failing to comply with Uefa Licencing and Financial Fair Play regulations between 2013/14 and 2017/18. Total charges 5

Breaching Premier League Profitability and Sustainability rules between 2015/16 and 2017/18. Total charges 25

Failing to co-operate with the Premier League investigation between 2018/19 and 2022/23. Total charges 30

Total charges: 130

They were breaking Prem rules, believing they were too big to be bound by any such conventions of legitimacy.

Doing what they wanted – because they did not care.

Even when they had got away with a plea deal warning from Uefa a decade ago.

While we now await the sanction, it will surely be devastating, even if the titles City won are not stripped from the club.

And, likewise, there can be no sympathy. Nor should there be.

When the anticipated 400-plus pages are finally published – which could be as soon as next week – it is clear that the decision by Prem chief executive Richard Masters to stick to his guns and keep the investigation going will be vindicated time and time again.



The reality is that, for all the anger coming from Etihad fans, which will now be overflowing, the Prem had no option but to pursue the case.

After all, the scale of the allegations was so great, so cavernous, that if nothing had been done it would have appeared Prem chiefs were content to operate with a rulebook that was more honoured in the breach than the observance.

Rival clubs simply did not believe a word City spoke.

Their motivations might have differed. There is no “red cartel” running football, however much some City fans might want to believe it.

But the established giants – not averse, at times, in both the distant and recent past of utilising their own armoury to secure their status – were never happy at being evicted by the Middle East interlopers.

Other clubs believed they were being deprived of their rightful dues, that City had gamed the system, played by a different set of regulations and gained their position as English football’s dominant force by blatant cheating.



For some, the chance to see City forced out of the top flight was, straightaway, an opportunity to make their own survival for another season or two more likely.

By taking on City’s legal aces, complete with their poison-tipped arguments, Masters and Co risked being as doomed as Hamlet in his final duel.

Adam Lewis KC, representing the Prem, had to prove “on the balance of probabilities” that City had deliberately, repeatedly and in full knowledge, set out to ride a coach and horses across the rulebook.

That they had been engaged in an orchestrated attempt to hide the true source of millions of pounds in income.



The crux of the claims was that upwards of £60m per season between 2009 and 2018 in sponsorship income, officially from Abu Dhabi-based companies, had in fact been paid directly by the club’s owners in the Gulf State.

That City had also, while insisting otherwise, allegedly paid a significant portion of the wages of former manager Roberto Mancini and senior players “off the books” – by using alternative sources to meet second contracts.

In short, City it was claimed had breached both Uefa and Prem financial control rules over a protracted period.

And gone out of their way to stymie the Prem investigation. That was always going to be the easiest part of the Prem case.



Especially given it was the offence for which the club were fined even after their successful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport against the initial two-year ban imposed by Uefa was upheld.

But to get a “conviction” on the other allegations required proving a conspiracy that went not just to the top of the club but included blue chip auditors and, effectively, the state of the United Arab Emirates.

That those email extracts, which City vehemently and consistently insisted were the result of “illegal hacking” and published “out of context” appeared damning was unquestioned.

But Lewis and his team had to convince the panel that not only did the emails suggest what some at City had been planning to do, but that they had actually done it.

Thinking about breaking the rules is not the same as breaking them.



The commission, though, unlike the majority of the three CAS judges in 2020, were convinced.

That means that while City can – and will – appeal against the sentence of the commission, they can do so only with the facts and findings stacked against them.

With every fan of every other club in the Prem now able to say: Guilty as charged.

RECOMMENDED STORIES



And wondering why, just a few months ago, Guardiola, Rodri, Bernardo Silva and others chose to leave.

City’s domination of the past decade was unquestioned. But, for all the Etihad bluster, it will never be viewed the same way.

Sports.title: Man City get new punishment verdict as three factors for guilty ruling appeal made clear
Sports.content:
Man City get new punishment verdict as three factors for guilty ruling appeal made clear

Manchester City have been handed new verdicts on what will follow them being found guilty of a significant number of financial charges

View 2 Images Manchester City's next steps regarding an appeal have been revealed (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Two legal experts have shared their thoughts on the next steps for Manchester City regarding their expected appeal and potential punishments. Earlier today, it emerged that the club had been found in breach of 114 Premier League financial regulations.

‌



City were initially charged in February 2023 with this outcome from their hearing against the Premier League just under two years ago. And there is expected to be further delays to any final solution with it understood that City will be appealing against the guilty verdict.

‌



Sports barrister at Church Court Chambers Yasin Patel has now offered his thoughts on the appeal while also making it clear that some clubs could take action.

‌



He said: "City's lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors - importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

Man City verdict LIVE: Premier League giants found guilty of 114 of 115 charges READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

"Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City's wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon."

‌



Ian Hargreaves, a partner at specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, has also discussed City's next moves following the latest development.

Hargreaves said: "The rumoured verdict is not the end of the story but the beginning of a new phase in what has become one of the most closely watched legal battles in global sport.

"The key questions this news raises are what sanction the panel considers proportionate and what guidance can be drawn from previous cases. There is a wide range of options, with a transfer ban at the more moderate end of the spectrum and expulsion from the league the most severe repercussion.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City released a statement of their own

"There is also the question of whether the panel's decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel's findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides."

"The outcome will also have wider implications for the balance of power in European football, although Premier League clubs will point out that these findings relate to historic conduct and not the league's current financial framework."

‌



A City statement read: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool are the sides to have been denied Premier League titles during the period in which City are judged to have secured an unfair advantage.

Article continues below

City are not back in action for another two weeks, with the extended international break stretching into October, and their first opponents upon return are Liverpool — arguably the club who have been denied the most silverware by City over the past decade.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel questions if Cole Palmer wants to play for England - 'It's hard to argue'
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has sensationally questioned whether Cole Palmer wants to play for England.

Palmer withdrew from the squad for the Nations League campaign and it is the FOURTH time he has pulled out after being called up by England. It comes just three months after Palmer was dropped from the World Cup and Tuchel’s warning is certain to cast doubt over the Chelsea star’s international future.

When it was put to Tuchel that it sounded like Palmer was not desperate to come away with on international duty, the England boss: “It’s hard to argue against what you’re saying. For sure it's a missed opportunity. It's another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities.

“I am his national team coach and I can only judge him on what he is delivering for the national team and he is just missing too many opportunities.”

‌



Man City must be relegated over 115 charges guilt - a points deduction is not enough READ MORE :

England face Spain in the Nations League on Saturday at Wembley on the back of five players pulling out of the original squad. Declan Rice, Tino Livramento, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo also pulled out.

But Tuchel was particularly brutal over Palmer who had completed all 90 minutes of Chelsea’s last four Premier League games and also had the summer off after not making the World Cup squad.

Tuchel said he understood the other withdrawals but said Palmer’s absence would not stick with him as he said those who reported up are now his priority in another swipe at the Chelsea forward’s chances. Morgan Gibbs-White cut short a holiday in Dubai to replace Palmer.

Tuchel added: “Every case is individual and if Declan calls me and explains to me…and I actually see him play v Brighton …I see straightaway on TV that something is off.

‌



“It leaves us with Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers, Morgan Gibbs-White and Eberechi Eze. All in camp. All desperate to be here. All available. And all ready to go, ready to stop a holiday after one day in Dubai.

“What sticks with me is the week that I have with the others. They (the absentees) lose that. That sticks. It sticks because we create something.

“We’re just not here for a week and say: ‘oh let’s play a six against six and now a nine against nine, lets do a little bit of foot volley and then we play.’

“We actually work off the field, on the field, about our principles, on how to be in. This brotherhood is so important and you miss out if you’re not there.”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel makes promise over England's 'Wonderwall' celebration as boss drops selection hint
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel makes promise over England's 'Wonderwall' celebration as boss drops selection hint

England take to the pitch for the first time since the World Cup on Saturday evening against Spain and the Three Lions will be hoping to give supporters something to celebrate at Wembley

View 4 Images Thomas Tuchel has given a hint over his plans vs Spain (Image: Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel says England plan to bring back a Wonderwall celebration at Wembley. England used the Oasis song as their World Cup anthem in the summer and the fans sang it after every win in the United States.

‌



The Three Lions face world champions Spain in the first game of their Nations League campaign on Saturday and Tuchel says he wants to bring back “beautiful” memories.

‌



England boss Tuchel said: “Do I think it will happen tomorrow? I think it will happen if we win. It's a big opportunity, and it's a big occasion, it's a beautiful match, in a new competition

‌



“Yes, of course, we will try and use the occasion to implement and to get the next win, and hopefully we play with a certain freedom that I felt that we played against France, for example.”

It will be England’s first game since the World Cup - where they suffered heartbreak against Argentina in the semifinal - and the fans really bought into the team.

Tuchel criticised the Wembley crowd for not being loud enough against Wales but fully expects the fans to be right behind them and it could set the mood for the rest of his reign in the build-up to Euro 2008.

Tuchel added: “I think the World Cup was outstanding in terms of atmosphere. I think we had an amazing performance against Wales, and I was not so happy with the atmosphere, so everyone killed me for that.

‌



“The stadium is the stadium, the crowds is the crowd, it can be sometimes in international, not tournament football. It can be difficult.

View 4 Images England's 'Wonderwall' celebration became a World Cup staple (Image: Getty Images)

“I want to just say we produced some top performances, especially against Wales, and it was still not what I thought is deserved for the players.

‌



“If you are 3-0 up after 15 minutes and of the crowd gets going in to every challenge I tell you we have a chance to be 5 or 6 nil up. I tell you, it helps so much.

“But if after 35 minutes you feel like 2,000 Wales supporters are singing and everybody else is like ‘ok when is the next goal coming?’ it’s just so different. That’s why it’s so beautiful and so difficult to play away.”

View 4 Images Kane looks set to start against Spain (Image: Getty Images)

‌



And while Tuchel is hoping that there will be more memorable post-match scenes, he has already admitted that there could be some new faces in the celebrations, havign suggested that it is unlikely any player will play every minute of the four games in ten days.

But Tuchel did suggest that England captain Kane - who is four caps away from equalling Peter Shilton’s record of 125 caps - would want to start them all even if he does not finish them.

Tuchel also hinted that he will keep largely the same starting XI through the new-look International window but says he will definitely make changes and usehis bench.

‌



When asked whether a player can play all the games, Tuchel said: “Maybe not all of them. Its not happening, I think. We will use our substitutes. Harry is desperate to start all four and there is a chance he will.

View 4 Images Kane is desperate to play against Spain (Image: Getty Images)

“This would actually be my mindset, to not make so many changes, to keep it going and to give the players we can rely on the trust and responsibility to take the next step and carry this team. Ideally.

Article continues below

“We have six or seven positions with regular starters but we must look at the reality. This is just my head. If you ask me after the game we may be having a completely different discussion and then we will travel to the Czech Republic and see. I would like to give players a regular start.

“That doesn’t mean they have to stay on the pitch for 90 minutes. It makes a big difference in our opinion if you play 70 or 90. From 70 on it makes a big difference. Up until 70mins its generally fine.”

Sports.title: 'Man City has gaslit its own fans by recklessly claiming innocence over 115 charges - I demand an explanation'
Sports.content:
"We can all be very calm because not one rule has been broken by Man City."

That's what we were told - or at least that's what the Manchester City top dogs told the players when the 115 charges were announced.

Now, we all look like mugs. Especially those of us that were naive enough to believe them.

For years the loyal City fanbase has heard every possible grumbling from the suits at the Etihad - essentially, this was a witch hunt. 'We're just too good, so they're trying to get us for it'.

‌



Well, congratulations City, you've gaslit your entire fanbase, and the stain of this will live a lot longer than the 48-hour reckless foray into the European Super League.

View 7 Images (L-R) Khaldoon Al Mubarak, former director of football Txiki Begiristain and CEO Ferran Soriano (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Man City release statement after being found GUILTY of Premier League charges READ MORE :

We've been here before. City fans were not new to it. Two years before the 115 charges were levelled at City by the Premier League, the club successfully overturned a two-year UEFA ban from the Champions League.

It took just five months for the Court of Arbitration for Sport to overturn that ban. Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said the UEFA investigation was a frustrating distraction, but it proved City had done nothing wrong.

‌



It's true. The club had been proved right, and its constant insistence of innocence was vindicated.

So, fast forward two years, and why shouldn't the fans believe them again? After all, the Premier League's 115 charges were based on the exact same leaked dossier that UEFA had used in its own probe.

View 7 Images Soriano and Al Mubarak have a lot of explaining to do to their own fans (Image: VINCE MIGNOTT/EPA-EFE/REX/Shutterstock)

The formula was identical; charges brought, City plead innocence. Except this time, the fans had the precedent to believe them.

‌



Football is incredibly tribal in this country. It's natural that fans back their own club - and equally natural for rival fans to assume guilt.

These 115 charges have been lingering over us fans for three-and-a-half years now. You'd struggle to find a single match in that time when rival fans didn't level the obvious 'we know what you are, we know what you are, you cheating b******s, we know what you are' chant at us.

So tedious. It's instantly responded by cheers and ironic celebrations from City fans. It was boring. So boring.

View 7 Images The club has consistently denied the charges levelled by the Premier League (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

‌



We had to contend with B-rate ex-professionals and boozed up fans calling into phone-in radio shows saying that City will inevitably be relegated out of the Football League at some point soon. Clearly this was nonsense. None of these people had any idea what they were talking about, because the case was heard behind closed doors.

Any sanction could only really result in a points deduction. Even in the worst case scenario for City, it would mean a single relegation to the Championship; this was a case brought by the Premier League specifically, not the FA or the EFL.

But that didn't stop the commentary by rival fans. Guilty. They didn't know a thing... but guilty.

View 7 Images Sanctions won't overshadow the best memories for fans - including reaching 100 points in 2017 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



A peak behind the curtain of Man City fans' social media, and we were cautiously optimistic. There's never smoke without fire, but everything we heard from the City camp was a confidence-booster.

Even immediately after the charges were brought in February 2023, the club said it was "surprised", "particularly given the extensive engagement and vast amount of detailed materials that the EPL has been provided with".

There's a vast amount of evidence for our case? Happy days. It even said there was a "comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" that supports innocence. It doesn't get more confident than that.

Then there was behind-the-scenes chats with the players - who, let's be honest, have the most to lose from relegation.

‌



View 7 Images Loyal fans remained cautiously optimistic about the outcome of the case (Image: NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Immediately after the charges were announced, CEO Ferran Soriano and then-sporting director Txiki Begiristain told the entire squad and backroom staff that there was nothing to worry about, according to former defender Aymeric Laporte.

He said: "When I was there and the news broke, the sporting director (Txiki Begiristain) and the CEO (Ferran Soriano) came and told all the players and staff that we can all be very calm because not one rule has been broken by Man City.

"They told us everything was fine so that’s why we all think City will be fine. I don’t think there will be any issues."

‌



View 7 Images The fans will be left heartbroken by any guilty verdicts (Image: Getty Images)

Then there was the chairman himself, Khaldoon Al Mubarak, who also comes out of this mess looking bad. He's consistently said he can't speak much about the case, but that he'll "say everything I've wanted to say" after the charges were settled.

So here we are, and we're ready to listen... because this is going to take some explaining.

But, despite the bitter taste this sorry charade has left in the mouth, it won't overshadow some of our most-memorable moments. Even if we're playing in the second tier of English football next season, nothing will take away Sergio Aguero's 90+4 finish to seal City's first Premier League title. Neither Ilkay Gundogan's brace to snatch the title away from Liverpool in the dying moments, nor Rodri smashing it home in Istanbul to win the club's first Champions League title. Those memories will be there forever, regardless, and the sorry fans from the days of 'typical City' will be eternally grateful.

‌



But, the club has some serious explaining to do.

Sports.title: Man City 115 charges timeline as damning Premier League guilty verdict reached
Sports.content:
Man City 115 charges timeline as damning Premier League guilty verdict reached

A look back on Manchester City's battle with the authorities after the club was found guilty of all but one of the Premier League's charges against them

View 3 Images Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak with the Champions League trophy (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

More than 15 years since Manchester City started winning trophies under Sheikh Mansour, the club has been found guilty of virtually every charge meted out by the Premier League. Starting with the 2011 FA Cup, the club's first major trophy in 35 years, City won eight trophies in the period covered by the case (2009-2018), including three Premier League titles, three League Cups and one Community Shield.

‌



The 2011-12 league title was the first of eight they have won overall. City's financial dealings have been under scrutiny since the mid-2010s when they clashed with UEFA on several occasions. Here's a recap of the allegations City have faced, dating back more than a decade.

‌



Clashing with UEFA

City were fined €60million (about £49m) and ordered to operate with a reduced Champions League squad in 2014 by European football's governing body for breaching Financial Fair Play (FFP) rules. Three years later, they received more than half of that figure back after complying with the sanction.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Der Spiegel allegations

In 2018, Der Spiegel published allegations from the Football Leaks website claiming that City inflated the value of sponsorship deals to circumvent FFP rules, prompting UEFA to launch another investigation.

That probe resulted in a two-year ban from European competitions, which was later overturned by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS). Meanwhile, the Premier League launched its own investigation into the club, resulting in the 115 charges being issued in February 2023, with City pleading their innocence.

‌



Can Man City appeal 114 guilty charges verdict? New timeline explained as deadline set READ MORE :

Treble glory

A few months later, City became just the second English club, after Manchester United, to win the Treble of Champions League, Premier League and FA Cup. More trophies followed and City made it four league titles in a row in 2024.

View 3 Images Manchester United fans display a banner referencing the Premier League's charges against City (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

But as the Sky Blues celebrated, rival clubs and fans questioned their success and grew increasingly frustrated about the wait for an outcome, especially as other clubs received points deductions for milder breaches of financial regulations.

‌



Pep departs as wait goes on

The independent hearing between City and the Premier League came and went but the wait for a verdict continued. The trophies kept coming, with City winning a domestic cup double last season, although they have lost their grip on the Premier League, while Pep Guardiola left the club in the summer.

View 3 Images Pep Guardiola led City to Champions League glory months after the charges emerged (Image: PA)

Verdict reached, but...

A verdict has finally been reached, with City found guilty of all but one of the charges. However, it's far from game over. It remains to be seen how City will be punished, while the club will almost certainly appeal, potentially leading to another lengthy wait for a final resolution to the most acrimonious case in Premier League history.

‌



Man City 115 charge timeline

May 2014: City were hit with a fine of around £49million, transfer restrictions and made to name a smaller Champions League squad than usual after being found guilty of breaching the European governing body's regulations in 2014.

April 2017: City were refunded around £33.4m of that fine after UEFA confirmed the club had complied with the sanctions imposed on them.

‌



November 2018: Der Spiegel publishes allegations from the Football Leaks website claiming City inflated the value of sponsorship deals to circumvent FFP rules.

March 2019: UEFA officially launches an investigation into the club over alleged FFP breaches.

May 2019: City criticise the UEFA probe and submit an appeal against the process.

‌



November 2019: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) dismisses City's early appeal, ruling it inadmissible.

February 2020: UEFA give City a two-year ban from European competitions and a fine of around £26m for "serious breaches" of FFP between 2012 and 2016.

July 2020: CAS overturns City's European ban on appeal, while the fine is reduced by more than half. CAS clear City of "disguising equity funds as sponsorship contributions" but maintain they "failed to cooperate with UEFA authorities."

‌



July 2021: High Court ruling confirms the Premier League is actively investigating City for alleged financial breaches.

April 2022: Der Spiegel releases further reports detailing the ongoing three-year Premier League investigation.

February 2023: The Premier League formally charges City with 115 alleged financial breaches, which the club denies.

Article continues below

September 2024: A 12-week-long independent hearing between the Premier League and City begins.

September 2026: It emerges that City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges, with the club set to appeal.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta has already given verdict on Man City’s 115 Premier League charges
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has already given verdict on Man City’s 115 Premier League charges

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 Premier League charges levelled at them and rival boss Mikel Arteta has regularly made his stance very clear

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has remained cagey on Man City's charges (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta previously assured that he saw no signs of wrongdoing at Manchester City before their guilty verdict. The eight-time Premier League champions were hit with 115 charges of breaching the league’s spending rules back in 2023.

‌



And reports on Friday have suggested that City have been found guilty of 114 of those charges. A punishment is not yet forthcoming, albeit a significant fine, points deduction and even expulsion from the Premier League have all been mentioned.

‌



The charges themselves relate to a period between 2009 and 2018. Current Arsenal boss Arteta was at the Etihad Stadium as an assistant to Pep Guardiola between July 2016 and December 2019.

‌



Asked back in 2023 when the initial charges were brought forwards, Arteta was tight-lipped. Asked for his response, the Spaniard said: “I’m not going to make any comment on that I’m sorry.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Arteta was then probed if he had seen or had any knowledge of any wrong-doing during his time with the club. Arteta simply replied: “No.”

The Arsenal boss was then asked about the charges once more the following year but was once again cagey. He said: “That’s something for the authorities to manage. It’s not for us.

"If they’re playing that means they can play and they are entitled to play. That’s it."

‌



Arteta eventually left Man City to return to Arsenal as he replaced Unai Emery. He has managed to get the club back on track and turned them into bonafide title challengers.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta spent three years at Manchester City (Image: Getty Images)

They went close to claiming the title in 2023. 2024 and 2025 but lost out to City on two occasions, while they were beaten to the punch by Liverpool in the latter of those seasons. Arsenal eventually got over the line last term as they finished seven points clear of City.

‌



From their perspective, City have already responded and claimed that the process relating to the charges is far from over. A club statement read: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

Sports.title: Fury: AJ is 'stepping stone' to Usyk trilogy
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury says Anthony Joshua is a "stepping stone" towards a trilogy fight with Oleksandr Usyk and vowed to knock out his British rival "inside seven rounds".

On Thursday, confirmation finally arrived that Fury and Joshua's long-awaited all-British heavyweight showdown will take place at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on Friday December 11.

Speaking for the first time since the announcement, Fury has predicted that he will inflict a one-sided defeat on Joshua to set up a third fight against Usyk, who defeated him twice in 2024 on points decisions.

"I'm just going to knock him [Joshua] out, 100 per cent," Fury said on the Furocity YouTube channel.

"I'm going to box the head off him and stop him inside six or seven rounds. I'm only using Joshua as a stepping stone, a warm-up to Usyk.

"Joshua, for me, is an old bum. A weightlifter. Too many weights, not enough speed. Too many weights, no cardio. So I'll cut through him like a hot knife through butter.

"I want Usyk. I want him in America, though, where I get a fair decision. I won the first two fights, and I'll definitely get a decision here, where it's fair.

"But, listen, now I want to use AJ as a heavy bag. Punch the **** out of him and then move on to Usyk. Give me a good warm-up before March next year."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Johnny Nelson shares his thoughts on Fury vs Joshua

Fury: I never believed I'd actually get AJ in ring - 'Christmas has come early'

Negotiations over the Fury vs Joshua fight had repeatedly hit stumbling blocks before this week's announcement and Fury insists he still has lingering doubts after Joshua turned down a face-off at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in April.

"He had his chance [or a face-off]. He was a little ****house at Tottenham the other month, whenever it was. Didn't want to get in the ring.

"We'll see. I always never ever believed I'd get him in the ring. So getting him in the ring now is like Christmas has come early for me.

"Honest to God. Like I can never ever see him or envision him sitting next to me at a press conference. It's going to be an onslaught.

"Tell you that now. A one-sided beatdown.

Sports.title: Brentford hold Schade contract talks as Arsenal, Liverpool track Germany winger
Sports.content:
Brentford have held initial talks with Kevin Schade about a new long-term contract in the wake of his excellent start to the campaign and increasing interest from bigger clubs including Arsenal and Liverpool.

The winger has scored three goals as Brentford's unbeaten start to the season has put them fourth in the Premier League from their opening five games, with two victories at home to Tottenham and Chelsea and three draws.

Schade has been tracked by several big Premier League clubs for some time, with Chelsea and Tottenham among his admirers, but Arsenal and Liverpool are thought to have been the keenest as the summer transfer window drew to a close.

The Germany international has entered the final two years of his current Brentford deal - signed when he joined from SC Freiburg for £20m in June 2023 - and the west London club are keen to give him improved terms.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at some of Brentford, Brighton and Bournemouth's biggest wins against the 'Big Six' after the trio have been dubbed the Premier League's Bermuda Triangle.

His three goals so far this term has taken his tally to 25 in 119 games plus a further nine assists and, while at Brentford, Schade has broken into the Germany side, starting Jurgen Klopp's first game in charge against the Netherlands last night.

Sports.title: Buttler ruled out of England's third ODI vs Sri Lanka
Sports.content:
Jos Buttler has been ruled out of England's third ODI against Sri Lanka, with Surrey's Dan Lawrence called into the squad.

An ECB spokesperson said: "Surrey batter Dan Lawrence has been called into the England Men's squad for Sunday's third Metro Bank ODI against Sri Lanka.

"Jos Buttler has been ruled out due to the hamstring injury he suffered in the second Metro Bank ODI at Headingley last night [Thursday] and will undergo further assessment."

Lawrence has been withdrawn from Surrey's County Championship fixture against Somerset and is set to train with England at The Oval on Saturday morning.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jos Buttler was forced to retire after a hamstring injury during England's second ODI against Sri Lanka .

Sri Lanka showed great fight to halt the hosts' chase in the second ODI and secure a 16-run victory at Headingley, levelling the three-match series at 1-1. Buttler played a decisive role in the hosts' chase before his injury ruled him out of the series decider.

Buttler had looked set to guide the hosts towards victory before pulling up in the 38th over with England 254-4. He was forced to retire hurt but returned to the crease in the 48th over in a final attempt to rescue the chase. Despite the injury, he went on to make 69 before being dismissed.

Will Jacks (52), Rehan Ahmed (0), Gus Atkinson (16) and Jamie Overton (2) also fell as the hosts' hopes faded. England managed just one four and one six from the 37th over onwards as Sri Lanka's bowlers tightened the pressure to seal a hard-fought win.

With the series finely poised at 1-1, the hosts must now regroup for the decider without Buttler, who played a central role in their second ODI chase.

Sports.title: Billam-Smith to fight Clarke on November 7 live on Sky Sports
Sports.content:
Chris Billam-Smith will fight Clarke on November 7, live on Sky Sports.

The British rivals clash in the headline event of Zuffa Boxing 12 at the Copper Box Arena in London.

Former world champion Billam-Smith is looking to fight his way back to the summit of the cruiserweight division, while Clarke launched himself into the upper echelons of the weight class with a stirring comeback victory over Jack Massey in June.

Billam-Smith headlined that event in Bournemouth when he won a fight of the year contender with Ryan Rozicki.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Rozicki was pulled out of the fight after the seventh round following an instant classic with Chris Billam-Smith

Those victories have put the two on a collision course.

Billam-Smith and Clarke have a past. A decade ago as amateur boxers, Clarke defeated Billam-Smith in the national elite championship finals.

That snuffed out Billam-Smith's hopes of a place on Team GB, while Clarke went on to box for Britain at the Olympic Games.

Now he wants revenge.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chev Clarke bounced back from being put down twice in the fourth round as he went on to stop Jack Massey in the seventh round of their cruiserweight classic

Billam-Smith did subsequently come into his own as a professional boxer. He won British, European and Commonwealth championships, before dethroning Lawrence Okolie on a memorable night at the Vitality stadium in his Bournemouth hometown to become the WBO cruiserweight world champion.

Regularly in exciting fights, he defended his title against Mateusz Masternak and Richard Riakporhe before losing a ferocious unification battle with Gilberto Ramirez.

Clarke has also featured in action-packed fights. He knocked out Ellis Zorro to win the British championship and challenged for the European title, when he was edged out by unbeaten champion Leonardo Mosquea.

Viddal Riley outpointed him at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium but Clarke restored his status when he twice rose from the canvas to take out Massey in his most recent fight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player American heavyweight Da'Mazion Vanhouter is 13-0, winning his last seven fights via knockout

Zuffa's newest signee, rising cruiserweight Lucas Roehrig, 9-0 (5), will fight Scotland's Connal McDonald, 5-1 (1), in an eight-rounder.

Scottish middleweight phenom Sam Hickey, 6-0 (3), and American heavyweight destroyer Da'Mazion Vanhouter, 13-0 (10) will face opponents to be named in eight-rounders. Vanhouter had an eye-opening performance on the Garcia vs Benn card earlier this month, demolishing Raphael Akpejiori in the first round.

British light-heavyweight contender Zach Parker will face unbeaten puncher Umar Dzambekov. Parker, 26-2 (18), a former British super-middleweight champion, makes his Zuffa Boxing debut following a controversial decision defeat last November to Olympic bronze medallist Joshua Buatsi.

Dzambekov (14-0, 10 KOs) is a southpaw knockout machine who grew up in Austria and now trains out of Los Angeles. He has stopped five of his last six foes, and in February, he delivered a crunching second-round KO over Ahmed Elbiali on Zuffa Boxing 03.

Additional information on the event will be announced in the coming weeks.

Fans are encouraged to register their interest early for the best chance to secure tickets via ZuffaBoxing.com.

Watch Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke on November 7 live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: Talk Of New York shines in Joel Stakes
Sports.content:
Talk Of New York was the chatter of Newmarket as he stared alongside Rebel’s Romance’s brother Fortitudine in a big-race double for Charlie Appleby on the Rowley Mile.

Always held in high regard and third in the St James's Palace Stakes behind Bow Echo and Gstaad, the son of Wootton Bassett was the 4-9 favourite for the Betway Joel Stakes, despite blotting his copybook at Goodwood last time out.

Always prominent in the group racing on the stands side, he moved powerfully to the lead under William Buick inside the final furlong, galloping out to a commanding four-and-three-quarter-length success.

Appleby, who is continuing in red-hot form, said: "On what he achieved in the St James's Palace you had to come here with confidence and you had to put a line through Goodwood, it was just one of those days and we've been there before.

"But his preparation coming into here looked good and it helped he won here in the spring. We always like to use the excuse of the dip if they get beat, but I would struggle to use that today!"

Connections will now consider supplementing Talk Of New York for one of the features of Qatar Racing British Champions Day, but it is next season where Appleby expects the colt to shine, when tasked with filling the lofty shoes of Notable Speech in the mile division.

"I'm not going to say yes to the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes, but you could take a look at it and there's the supplementary stage," continued Appleby.

"William and I spoke last week and we could have waited to see what the ground was like in France for the Prix Daniel Wildenstein, but William was confident and said if we run in the Joel and win well, the QEII is then an option. We'll see how he comes out of this.

"I think a bit of ease in the ground wouldn't do him any harm as he's a decent-sized horse who hits the ground hard. I'm not saying I will go to this year's Breeders' Cup with him, but I'm very much working back from next year's Breeders' Cup."

A little over half and hour later Appleby's afternoon got even better as after being backed into 15-8 favouritism, Fortitudine made it three from three in the Betway Godolphin Stakes.

Having made all to enhance his growing reputation with a first Listed strike, he could now follow in the footsteps of his illustrious sibling and head to Dubai after a short break.

Appleby said: "It was always our plan to go out there and make it and what he's happy doing is going out there and galloping.

"He learned to race at Kempton and we went out and made the running today and what I was impressed with was half a mile out you could see them coming at him and you could see him lower and quicken again, he might have even quickened twice actually.

"We're all very relaxed with this horse and he keeps coming out and doing it for us. He's down in a small little yard at home because he's not the biggest and most robust and likes that individual care and attention.

"If there is one thing in his bag, he can gallop and maintain it. We'll put him away for a bit now and maybe take him out to Dubai for the City of Gold over the slick mile and a half. William keeps reverting back to his brother and he enjoyed it out there so it might be something we look towards."

Pensando A Te sparks Classic dreams for Marco Botti

Pensando A Te got up in the very last stride for Marco Botti and Silvestre de Sousa to deny Light Of Dawn victory in the Betway Rockfel Stakes at Newmarket.

The Karl Burke-trained Light Of Dawn was the 5-2 favourite for the Group Two contest after winning the Group Three Prestige Stakes at Goodwood last month, with John and Thady Gosden's previously unbeaten filly Spirited Gesture rated her biggest threat.

Pensando A Te, who finished second to the reopposing Speed Of Sound on her Yarmouth debut before going one better at Ascot, was sent off at 15-2 in the hands of De Sousa, who after a slow start settled his mount at the rear of the nine-runner field, seemingly intent to keep his powder dry for a late run.

The front-running Speed Of Sound and Light Of Dawn were the two vying for the lead hitting the rising ground heading inside the last of seven furlongs, but no sooner had Light Of Dawn won that protracted battle to grab the lead, Pensando A Te came with a flying late run to get up by a short head.

Image: Pensando A Te ridden by Silvestre De Sousa before the Betway Rockfel Stakes

Botti said: "It's always nice when you have a two-year-old who does well at the back-end of the season. I thought we were maybe rushing her on a little bit, but we always thought we had a nice filly.

"We were confident when she ran first time out and she ran a good race and she's progressed nicely since then. At Ascot I thought she did it nicely in a small field and today stepping up to seven furlongs the plan was to get her settled and come with a late run.

"I didn't think she had got there and my first impression was we got beat. She's a nice filly for next year."

The Newmarket-based Italian will spend the winter months dreaming of a 1000 Guineas bid with his new star filly, quoted at 20-1 shot by Coral for Classic glory.

Light Of Dawn, who carries the Wathnan Racing colours, just held on for second from the fast-finishing Ruby Moon.

Wathnan's racing adviser Richard Brown said: "She's run a blinder and James [Doyle] said she wasn't enjoying the ground, so all credit to her for nearly pulling it off and it was a big run.

"We'll put her away now and there's a chance she gets the mile next year without it being certain. That's the road we'll go down and in my mind I would maybe be thinking France [Guineas]."

Sports.title: 'They changed the plan' - Hamilton left frustrated by Ferrari tactics
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton expressed frustration with Ferrari's approach to Q3 after qualifying sixth for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, saying "they changed the plan".

Hamilton questioned why the team completed only one run of multiple laps at the end of the final knockout stage rather than go out earlier for initial laps, as Mercedes, McLaren and Red Bull with Max Verstappen had done.

The seven-time world champion said his final laps were compromised by having no 'tow' from a car in front to aid straight-line speed down Baku's long main straight. Team-mate Charles Leclerc did have a tow, from Hamilton, by dint of the fact it was the Monegasque's turn to go out second in final qualifying.

Leclerc qualified second behind dominant Mercedes polesitter George Russell, who topped qualifying by a season-high margin of eight tenths of a second.

Reflecting on his own session, Hamilton told Sky Sports F1: "It was a pretty bad qualifying once again. It's not for the lack of trying.

"Q1 and Q2 were pretty ok. At least Q1 was pretty decent, Q2 we struggled a little bit more, and then as we went into Q3 they changed the plan.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

"Instead of doing two runs we ended up waiting and then because I was ahead of Charles, I had nobody ahead of me on a tow so that was worth quite a chunk in itself.

"But, either way, we couldn't compete with the Mercedes. They are just outright so much quicker on the straights than us. They did a great job."

Three of the five cars in front of Hamilton on the grid - Russell and McLaren duo Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris - for Saturday's race at 1pm run Mercedes engines.

"I think it's going to be hard to overtake a Mercedes tomorrow," added Hamilton.

"Keeping up with a Mercedes engine on the straight will be tough but I'll give it everything I've got."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok is joined by George Russell to watch back his pole-setting lap for the Azerbaijan GP.

Speaking in Ferrari's post-qualifying press release, team principal Frederic Vasseur said: "We made some significant changes to the set-up and to our approach, and they paid off today.

"George has been very strong since the first lap of FP1, but Charles did a good job to put the car on the front row.

"On Lewis' side, it was difficult to get a tow because the different run plans made it complicated to synchronise with the other cars. He also brushed the wall on his first lap in Q3, which compromised that attempt, but he recovered well to finish sixth despite not having a tow on his final lap."

'We know we have a good race car' - Leclerc hopes for strong Saturday race

Leclerc, who claimed Ferrari's first front-row since the Hungarian Grand Prix in July, was pleased with his lap but admitted the gap to Russell was "a lot more than what we expected" despite a challenging Thursday.

"Honestly, it was quite a good lap," he added. "Lewis was three-four seconds, I think, in front, and I managed to do a good lap at the end.

"But when I see the gap to George, maybe the lap wasn't good enough."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater breaks down the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, including why the race takes place on a Saturday, while doing his best Craig David impression!

But Leclerc offered a more optimistic assessment of what he could potentially do from the front row after encouraging long-run pace in practice.

"We'll try, and we'll do our best," said Leclerc. "Whether that'll be enough, only time will tell.

"But we know that we have a good race car, more often than not better in the race than in qualifying, and I hope that it will be the case again this weekend."

Vasseur, whose team have claimed no podium finishes in the last four races, added: "Tyre degradation is expected to be very low, which could make track position particularly important.

"We are in a position to score good points with both cars, even if Baku is always unpredictable."
