Sports.title: Sainz hit with grid drop and penalty points for second yellow flag infringement in Baku | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Carlos Sainz Jnr has lost his best grid position of the season to date after being penalised for his second yellow flag infringement of the day in Baku.

The Williams driver avoided a grid drop for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags in final practice. However stewards hit him with a five-place grid drop when he repeated the offence in qualifying and added two penalty points to his licence, putting him on a total of four.

Sainz was reprimanded for his infringement in qualifying as the stewards ruled the yellow flag only appeared briefly during his lap. However Sainz passed multiple yellow flags during Q3 and failed to slow sufficiently.

Stewards’ verdict on Sainz’s final practice infringement

The stewards did not issue a grid drop to Sainz over his infringement in practice after taking into account how briefly the yellow flag was displayed for.

“A single yellow was displayed in marshalling sector six shortly before [Sainz] entered the sector,” the stewards ruled. “Sainz explained that, approaching turn four, he briefly noticed a light signal in his peripheral vision but was not certain that it was yellow. He therefore asked the team by radio whether a yellow flag was being displayed.

“The onboard video also showed that a yellow warning light was flashing on Sainz’s steering wheel, indicating the yellow sector. Sainz explained that in the circumstances he had not been able to pay attention to this warning.

“Approaching turn four, Sainz braked slightly earlier than on the reference lap, but subsequently applied less brake pressure. At the exit of turn four he accelerated more moderately than on the reference lap. Overall, he lost approximately 0.10 seconds in the relevant sector.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“From the exit of turn four Sainz was able to see the green light marking the end of the yellow sector. Sainz acknowledged that, having seen the green light, he should have understood that he was still travelling within a yellow sector. Nevertheless, on the straight approaching the green light he accelerated up to the limiter while still within the yellow sector.

“The stewards considered the fact that the single yellow was displayed only shortly before Sainz entered marshalling sector six as a mitigating circumstance. However, taking into account the visible yellow indication, the warning displayed on the steering wheel, the telemetry and, in particular, Sainz’s acceleration while still within the yellow sector after the green light had become visible, the stewards were not satisfied that Sainz had sufficiently reduced speed and exercised the required caution for a single yellow.

“The stewards therefore determine that Sainz failed to sufficiently reduce speed under the single yellow.

“The standard penalty under the Penalty Guidelines for such an infringement is a drop of five grid positions. However, the stewards considered that there were mitigating circumstances, in particular the very short period between the single yellow being displayed and Sainz entering the relevant marshalling sector. The stewards also considered the penalties applied in comparable cases, where a driving reprimand has consistently been imposed in circumstances warranting mitigation from the standard penalty. The stewards therefore considered a driving reprimand appropriate and consistent with those precedents.”

Stewards’ verdict on Sainz’s qualifying infringement

The stewards did not accept Sainz’s explanation for his second infringement.

“Single yellow flags were displayed in marshalling sectors four and five, in particular after turn two and on the approach to turn thee,” they noted. “The Yellow indications were clearly visible and Sainz had also received a radio warning from the team: “Yellow ahead, lift.” Sainz confirmed at the hearing that he was aware of the yellow Flag situation.

“SAI explained that he intended to demonstrate a reduction in speed across the yellow area as a whole. He stated that he did not consider it necessary to reduce speed on the straight and instead intended to demonstrate his response when approaching and exiting turn three. He considered this to be a “global lift” covering the consecutive Yellow sectors. He further explained that the car which had originally caused the yellow was no longer in the run-off area and that he expected the yellow flags to be withdrawn.

“The stewards did not accept this interpretation. Where consecutive marshalling sectors are subject to yellow flag conditions, a driver must demonstrate a significant reaction to reduce speed in each individual yellow marshalling sector. A reduction in a subsequent sector cannot retrospectively satisfy the requirement applicable to the preceding Yellow sector. The obligation is also not dependent on the driver’s own assessment of whether the original hazard remains present within a particular part of the Yellow sector.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The telemetry clearly showed that Sainz’s reaction to the Yellow occurred only in Marshalling Sector 5. There was no meaningful reduction in speed in marshalling sector four which could realistically be attributed to a response to the Yellow. Indeed, Sainz recorded his fastest time of the session in marshalling sector four.

“The stewards therefore did not accept that the subsequent lift in marshalling sector five constituted a sufficient “global” response covering both sectors. This is distinguishable from cases where the telemetry demonstrates a significant response to the Yellow even though the overall sector time reduction is relatively small. In the present case, Sainz was aware of the Yellow, had received an explicit warning from the team, the yellow indications were clearly visible and the telemetry established that he did not demonstrate the required reaction in marshalling sector four.

“The stewards therefore determine that Sainz failed to sufficiently reduce speed under the Single Yellow Flag in marshalling sector four.

“The standard penalty under the Penalty Guidelines for this infringement during qualifying is a drop of five grid positions.”

Sports.title: Antonelli “very mad” with himself after crashing out in first round of qualifying | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli was frustrated with himself after crashing out of qualifying for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The championship leader hit the wall at the inside of turn one during Q1. He tried to drive his car back to the pits but his race engineer Peter Bonnington told him to stop as the suspension damage was too extensive for them to repair during the session.

Speaking after the session Antonelli said he was caught out by how quickly the grip levels increased at the track during the session.

“The grip was coming up very quickly lap-by-lap,” he told Sky. “Obviously I turned in and suddenly I had a lot more front-end compared to the lap before and I touched the wall.

“So it was mistake from my side. Very unnecessary, to be fair. I’m very mad about it and we’ll try to do better tomorrow.”

Antonelli missed a significant proportion of the first and second practice sessions yesterday due to a hydraulic problem. While Antonelli is set to start tomorrow’s race from 16th on the grid his team mate George Russell claimed pole position for the race.

“The car has been very strong this weekend, so George has been doing incredibly well,” said Antonelli. “We’ll try our best tomorrow to recover as many places as possible.”

Sports.title: Russell dominates Baku qualifying for pole after Antonelli crashes in Q1 | 2026 Azerbaijan GP qualifying report
Sports.content:
George Russell took pole position for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in dominant fashion.

His best lap of 1’42.526 was over eight tenths of a second quicker than anyone else could manage. He claimed pole position by the biggest margin for over three years

However his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli will start only 16th after he crashed out in the first round of qualifying.

The championship leader already had a time on the board when he clipped the barrier on the inside of turn one. The contact immediately broke his front-left suspension, and although Antonelli tried to drag his car back to the pits, race engineer Peter Bonnington persuaded him the suspension was so significant that the team wouldn’t be able to fix it in time and he should stop.

Compounding Antonelli’s misery, the time he had already set proved quick enough to secure him a place in Q2.

Russell’s bid for pole position briefly looked under threat from the McLaren drivers in Q3. However Lando Norris locked up heavily at turn three on his final lap and went into the run-off area. That also scuppered Max Verstappen’s final attempt to set a time, leaving him eighth on the grid.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Charles Leclerc produced his usual top-drawer performance at Baku to join Russell on the front row of the grid. Oscar Piastri, who set the quickest time at one stage in Q3, took third. Isack Hadjar out-qualified Verstappen on his return from injury.

Norris’s error left him fifth on the grid ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Both Alpine drivers reached Q3 but Franco Colapinto went off at turn 15 and ended up tenth, while Pierre Gasly took seventh ahead of Verstappen.

Carlos Sainz Jnr made good use of Williams’ upgrade, putting his car in Q3 for the first time this year. He will start ninth ahead of Colapinto.

Oliver Bearman narrowly failed to claim the final place in Q3 after Colapinto beat his time. Esteban Ocon also dropped out in Q2 in the other Haas. Alexander Albon was frustrated at his failure to join his team mate in the final 10 and dropped out along with the two Racing Bulls.

There was no great surprise that neither of the Aston Martins nor Cadillacs were able to beat Antonelli’s time in Q1. However the elimination of both Audis following their major upgrade was unexpected.

Sports.title: Verstappen leads close final practice session in Baku ahead of Russell and Hamilton | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen denied George Russell a clean sweep of all three practice sessions for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

But there was little to choose between the three quickest teams at the end of the final hour of running before qualifying.

The Red Bull, Mercedes and Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari were covered by little more than a tenth of a second.

Drivers found the soft tyres were capable of producing multiple quick laps. Verstappen improved his fastest time repeatedly over a 12-lap run on softs at the end of the session, but skidded into the turn 15 run-off area during his final attempt.

His last run nosed him ahead of Russell’s Mercedes, which had set the pace for much of the session. Russell and team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli, who was fourth-quickest, ducked back into the pits and switched to the medium compound before the session ended, while others continued to improve.

Charles Leclerc was half a second slower than Hamilton after going off at turn seven. Russell also came to a stop there during the session.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Pierre Gasly underlined Alpine’s potential again by setting the sixth-fastest time. That put him ahead of both McLaren drivers.

The two Red Bull drivers were separated by 1.2 seconds. Isack Hadjar complained of being repeatedly stuck in traffic on his way to the ninth-fastest time. “Unfortunately I don’t control all the cars,” replied his race engineer Richard Wood.

Franco Colapinto completed the top 10. Sergio Perez put his Cadillac in 16th place but was unhappy to see Arvid Lindblad overtake him by cutting across the inside of turn 15, which he reported to the stewards. Both Racing Bulls ended the session in the bottom five places.

Aston Martin’s tough weekend continued. The team told Lance Stroll to park up after just eight laps after he clipped the wall at the inside of turn one.

Although many drivers explored the track’s run-off areas the session ran without interruption, except for a brief Virtual Safety Car period to allow marshals to move a fallen branch.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Why swapping Ocon for Camara makes sense for Haas | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 could have one fewer race-winner on the grid in 2027 as Esteban Ocon has given the strongest indication yet he won’t remain at Haas.

Ocon is a mid driver at best. His race win in Hungary was not to do with skill and in a poor car, a mid driver cannot shine. The fact that Bearman is untroubled by Ocon’s ability is plain to see.

From a Haas perspective, keeping Ocon is a neutral equation. He’s not bringing in anything and having someone else in the car would make little to no difference to them from a sporting standpoint, it if having a Ferrari academy driver in the car gets them cheaper parts, why wouldn’t you?

Camara would be obvious for them given his current visibility across the F2 standings and the media. Couple that with his corporate backing and the fanaticism of Brazilian fans with wallets, he is a more attractive choice than a Mercedes journeyman with little in the way of an affiliation package.

Performance comes first, allegedly, but you can’t ignore financial performance. Besides, they’re not going to get Tsolov, Mini or Dunne so why not?

Sports.title: Spotlight: Scheckter plans appeal over court’s demand he pay £1.5m tax bill | Brief
Sports.content:
Jody Scheckter has vowed to fight on after losing a court battle over a £1.5 million tax bill.

The 1979 Formula 1 world champion closed his organic farm business in Hampshire two years ago but faces a demand for £1,457,634 from His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs.

A court ordered Scheckter to pay the bill last week. However he told The Telegraph he believes he did not break the law and will appeal against the decision. The 76-year-old added illness prevented him from attending much of the two-week tribunal hearing and he struggled to hear some of the questions.

He told the paper: “My wife said ‘You should have paid it long ago’ She’s right. Except, you know… I blame my mother, she always told me: ‘You’ve got to fight for what’s right’. And I absolutely believed I was doing the right thing.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Invites Dana White Into Anthony Joshua Fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury says he removed a clause barring Dana White from his fight with Anthony Joshua. He says Joshua’s contract had the same restriction. Fury has made his choice public, leaving Joshua to answer an uncomfortable question: does he want White kept away from the event?

“I want him involved. Two baldies together,” Fury joked in an interview, as Dev Sahni reported. The contracts have not been made public, so Fury’s description of Joshua’s terms remains his account.

White’s involvement has already irritated Joshua’s promoter, Eddie Hearn. Fury knows that. His joke puts the issue in front of fans and invites them to see any objection from Joshua’s side as promoter politics getting in the way of a fight.

That is useful ground for Fury. If negotiations stall, he can say he welcomed everyone while Joshua’s side insisted on keeping White out. It gives Fury a simple explanation for a complicated delay, even though nobody has established that White’s role is what is holding up the fight.

It also puts Joshua in a difficult position. Matchroom helped make him a huge British attraction, and Hearn has every reason to protect his place in the promotion. But if Joshua wants White excluded too, fans deserve to hear that from Joshua. Fury’s version makes the restriction sound like Hearn guarding his territory.

There is another question Fury has left unanswered: what would White actually do? Neither boxer needs him to negotiate on his behalf. Wanting White “involved” sounds like a concession until someone defines the job Fury wants him to have.

Fury has found a line that will get people talking. A clear date, venue and agreement between both camps would do more for this fight than another argument over who gets a microphone.

Sports.title: Ricardo Sandoval Risks Two Titles Against Sergio Mendoza
Sports.content:
Ricardo Sandoval prepared for months to fight Oscar Collazo, a compact southpaw moving up to flyweight. With Collazo injured, Sandoval now has just over two weeks to adjust to Sergio Mendoza, a taller challenger with 23 knockouts who wants his WBA and WBC titles on October 10 in Chicago.

The change matters in the ring. Sandoval, listed at 5’6″, was preparing to face a much shorter fighter. Mendoza is listed at roughly 5’8″. The champion must adjust his distance and timing for an opponent who presents a different target and may make him work harder to get inside.

“I’m very excited to still be fighting in Chicago and to have the opportunity to defend my titles for the first time,” Sandoval said in the Golden Boy and Most Valuable Promotions announcement. Mendoza offered a more urgent message: “I’m going to leave my soul in the ring to become world champion.”

Sandoval (27-2, 18 KOs) has lost the unification fight that gave this date its appeal, yet he still has two belts to defend. Mendoza (27-1, 23 KOs) gets a second world title chance only months after Thanongsak Simsri stopped him in the second round of their April fight in Japan. That defeat raises a question about Mendoza’s ability to withstand the champion’s offense. It also gives him reason to seize this opportunity quickly.

Sandoval’s danger is fighting as though Mendoza is an obstacle between him and a rescheduled Collazo bout. If he rushes forward looking to make a statement, he gives a taller puncher chances to catch him coming in. A measured start would let Sandoval test Mendoza’s power and find the distance he did not spend camp preparing for.

Their flyweight title fight is the DAZN co-feature to Floyd Schofield III against Lucas Bahdi for the WBA lightweight title at Wintrust Arena.

Sports.title: Chris Billam-Smith Risks His Comeback Against Chev Clarke
Sports.content:
Chris Billam-Smith has a chance to avenge two amateur losses to Chev Clarke on November 7. The danger is that Clarke’s best punches may come exactly where Billam-Smith likes to fight: up close.

Their 12-round cruiserweight bout will headline Zuffa Boxing 12 at London’s Copper Box Arena. Billam-Smith (22-2, 14 KOs) brings the world title experience. Clarke (12-2, 9 KOs) brings the amateur wins and the confidence of a fighter who has already beaten him twice.

Billam-Smith tends to make fights physical. He leans on opponents, works along the ropes and keeps punching when the exchanges get ugly. That served him in June against Ryan Rozicki, who did not come out for the eighth round after a punishing fight. Clarke’s win over Jack Massey on the same Bournemouth card showed a different kind of danger. Dropped twice in the fourth, Clarke recovered and stopped Massey in the seventh.

Billam-Smith cannot assume that crowding Clarke will make him safe. Clarke can fire short counters in those exchanges, and he showed against Massey that hurting him does not necessarily finish the job. But the knockdowns also give Billam-Smith an obvious target. If Massey could catch Clarke cleanly twice in one round, Billam-Smith has reason to test his chin early.

There is a question about what the Bournemouth fights took out of both men. Billam-Smith absorbed plenty from Rozicki; Clarke had to climb off the canvas twice. Neither gets a gentle return. For Billam-Smith, that comes after years of demanding cruiserweight fights and a world title loss to Gilberto Ramirez.

Clarke’s amateur edge gives this fight its history, but Billam-Smith has built the stronger professional career. He has won a world title and learned how to fight through difficult rounds. Clarke can change the direction of his career by beating him. Billam-Smith has far more to lose if a fighter he once struggled to beat stops his climb back toward another title shot.

Sky Sports will show the fight in the UK and Ireland; Paramount+ will stream it in the United States and Canada.

This fight is an elimination match between two aging cruiserweights running out of road. Clarke is thirty-five, entered the professional ranks late after the Tokyo Olympics, and has struggled to build real momentum toward the elite level. The two amateur wins over Billam-Smith happened a lifetime ago under a completely different scoring format.

In the professional ring, Clarke has looked vulnerable, particularly when Jack Massey put him on the canvas twice in June. Clarke survived because Massey got reckless, but banking on that kind of miraculous escape against top-tier punchers is suicide. A third professional loss buries Clarke on domestic undercards for the remainder of his days.

Billam-Smith is playing with fire by taking this fight. At thirty-six, his physical prime is fading fast. The beating he endured against Ryan Rozicki sent him directly to a hospital bed, proving that every victory now requires him to leave a piece of himself behind. He took heavy punishment from Gilberto Ramirez, endured a grueling scrap with Brandon Glanton, and took endless headshots from Rozicki.

Billam-Smith wanted Jai Opetaia, but settling for Clarke presents maximum risk with minimal reward. Losing to a domestic rival he is supposed to outwork destroys his credibility as a serious world title challenger. The stylistic matchup favors pure attrition over boxing finesse. Billam-Smith does not have the foot speed to keep Clarke on the outside, which guarantees a brutal battle in the pocket.

Clarke possesses power in the inside short spaces, which is precisely where Billam-Smith chooses to fight. If Clarke catches Billam-Smith clean early, the miles on Billam-Smith will show up instantly. Billam-Smith has the superior professional seasoning over twelve rounds. He knows how to drag opponents into deep waters, lean his weight on their shoulders, and grind them down along the ropes.

Sports.title: Johnny Fisher Weighs 243 Pounds for Michael Pirotton Fight at Zuffa Boxing 11
Sports.content:
Fisher headlines Saturday’s Copper Box Arena card, live on Paramount+ in the US and Sky Sports in the UK.

Johnny Fisher tipped the scales at 243 pounds ahead of his heavyweight clash with Michael Pirotton at London’s Copper Box Arena on Saturday, September 26. Belgium’s Pirotton weighed 240.6 pounds for their scheduled 10-round main event at Zuffa Boxing 11.

Fisher was 2.4 pounds heavier. Paramount+ will broadcast the event in the US, with Sky Sports carrying it in the UK. The event starts at 2 pm ET / 7 pm UK.

The Romford heavyweight enters at 14-1 with 12 knockouts after signing with Dana White’s promotion. Saturday will mark his third appearance at the Copper Box, where he also suffered his only professional defeat against Dave Allen.

Fisher had edged Allen by split decision in their first meeting before Allen stopped him in the rematch. He has since returned to winning ways, stopping Ivan Balaz in four rounds.

His move to Zuffa brings an immediate headline slot.

“The most exciting chapter of my professional career begins,” Fisher said when announcing his signing. “Thank you to Dana White, Nick Khan, and the Zuffa Boxing team for this opportunity. Everything has led to this point. Bull Army, get ready to assemble. Bosh!”

Richards and Kalajdzic Make Weight

Craig Richards registered 174.2 pounds for his 10-round light heavyweight bout against Radivoje Kalajdzic, who weighed 174.5 pounds. Both came in below the 175-pound limit.

Two middleweight bouts are scheduled for 10 rounds each. Lee Cutler weighed 159.5 pounds, with Louis Greene at 159.1, while Cesar Mateo Tapia hit 159.9 pounds against Leo Ruiz’s 159.2.

Kayla Allen and Edina Kiss will contest six rounds, weighing 142.9 pounds and 142 pounds, respectively. Alex MacMillan registered 149.9 pounds for his six-round meeting with Guillaume Azagier, who came in at 151.6.

Those bouts complete the six-fight main card.

Three Bouts on the Prelims

Rogelio Romero weighed 199.2 pounds ahead of his eight-round cruiserweight contest with Aurel Ignat, who registered 199.6 pounds.

Alexis de la Cerda and Cain Lewis both made the featherweight limit for their eight-rounder. De la Cerda came in at 125.4 pounds, with Lewis slightly heavier at 125.6.

Fred Pullen faces Leonardo Faretina over four rounds at lightweight. Pullen weighed 131.4 pounds, while Faretina registered 132.7, completing the nine-bout London bill.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Calls Shakur Stevenson’s Pacquiao Pursuit Easy Money
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley sees Shakur Stevenson’s pursuit of Manny Pacquiao as a soft move. With plenty of active fighters available, Shakur has picked a 47-year-old for the proposed co-feature on the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua card.

“Ain’t nobody waiting on no damn Manny Pacquiao and you to fight, boy,” Bradley said in a video on his channel. He challenged Zuffa Boxing’s interest in the matchup, too: “Y’all talking about y’all supposed to be changing boxing? This ain’t changing boxing. This downplaying and downgrading boxing.”

Bradley first fought Pacquiao in 2012, when Manny was 33. Stevenson would face a far older fighter who has not recorded an official win since beating Keith Thurman in 2019. Putting Pacquiao’s name on Shakur’s record would be a commercial prize. It would say much less about Shakur’s place among today’s best fighters.

A Fury–Joshua stadium card would put Stevenson in front of viewers who rarely watch him. That opportunity comes with a trap. If he controls the distance and wins a quiet decision, a crowd waiting for Pacquiao’s old bursts of action may turn on him. If Shakur stops Pacquiao, many will see the result through the lens of Manny’s age. Winning the fight and winning over that audience are different jobs.

Stevenson also holds the WBO light welterweight title he took from Teofimo Lopez in January. Bradley pointed to Raymond Muratalla and O’Shaquie Foster while questioning why Shakur is pursuing Pacquiao. A catchweight attraction would take time away from a title defense, although the WBO has not approved this proposed fight or granted Stevenson an exception.

Bradley went further, claiming Floyd Mayweather wants Shakur to beat Pacquiao before Gervonta Davis gets the opportunity. That is Bradley’s speculation. His stronger point concerns Shakur’s own career: a famous opponent cannot give him the same credibility as beating a top fighter in his prime.

Pacquiao–Stevenson remains in talks for the proposed Fury–Joshua card in Cardiff. Bout agreements had not been delivered when the latest report was published.

Turki Alalshikh built his entire reputation among boxing purists on eliminating cherry-picks, forcing unifications, and making the fights the old promotional machinery spent a decade sabotaging. For Riyadh Season and Netflix to rubber-stamp an official, sanctioned bout between a prime pound-for-pound champion and an elderly senator looks like a total betrayal of that brand. It lowers the bar to YouTube celebrity boxing standards. Purists will openly question how the same organizers who put together elite 50-50 matchups can suddenly justify an exploitative nostalgia stunt on the biggest British stadium card of the year.

Turki Alalshikh built his entire reputation among boxing purists on eliminating cherry-picks, forcing unifications, and making the fights the old promotional machinery spent a decade sabotaging. For Riyadh Season and Netflix to rubber-stamp an official, sanctioned bout between a prime pound-for-pound champion and an elderly senator looks like a total betrayal of that brand. It lowers the bar to YouTube celebrity boxing standards. Purists will openly question how the same organizers who put together elite 50-50 matchups can suddenly justify an exploitative nostalgia stunt on the biggest British stadium card of the year.

Putting this fight as the co-feature in Cardiff sets a stylistic trap for everyone involved. Those stadium fans want blood, violence, and dramatic exchanges to warm them up for Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Instead, they will watch Shakur do what he always does: use elite footwork, control distance from twenty feet away, and tap his way to a quiet, low-output decision against an icon whose forty-seven-year-old legs cannot track him down.

If Shakur refuses to engage and cruises to a boring points win, eighty thousand spectators will boo him mercilessly. If he turns aggressive and stops Pacquiao, fans will feel disgusted watching a faded legend get battered by someone nearly two decades younger. It produces a scenario where nobody wins, the sport loses credibility, and the fans leave feeling cheated by a spectacle disguised as competition.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Questions Hamzah Sheeraz’s Title Exit
Sports.content:
Frank Warren won the purse bid for Hamzah Sheeraz’s defense against Janibek Alimkhanuly. Days later, Sheeraz gave up the WBO super middleweight title. Warren’s response raises a question Sheeraz’s next fight will have to answer: what was the belt worth if he would not defend it against this challenger?

“Very, very disappointed,” Warren said in an interview this week. “It was a purse bid. We bid the highest amount of money for it.” Queensberry’s winning bid was $1,001,809, with Sheeraz due roughly $750,000 under the purse split. Warren said to iFL TV his team had worked to put Sheeraz in position to win the title.

Sheeraz mentioned Alimkhanuly’s previous failed drug test in objecting to the WBO’s order. He has grounds to question the sanctioning body’s decision. Still, surrendering the belt after Queensberry won the bid leaves him open to another question: what fight is worth giving up a guaranteed title defense?

Alimkhanuly would have been a serious test. Sheeraz had trouble controlling the mobile Simon Zachenhuber in July and kept his title by majority decision, with one judge scoring the fight level. Against Alimkhanuly, he would have faced a southpaw with greater power and a stronger claim to world class standing.

Warren also criticized the advice Sheeraz is receiving, then said Queensberry still has a contract with him. If Sheeraz is approaching his final fight under that deal and intends to leave, Warren has little incentive to arrange an easy farewell. A dangerous opponent would give Queensberry a fight to sell and give Sheeraz another chance to prove himself. Warren has announced no such plan, but his frustration makes the next matchmaking decision worth watching.

A champion brings a belt to the table when pursuing Canelo Alvarez or another major fight. Sheeraz no longer has that bargaining chip. If his team has a better opportunity ready, it can make the decision look shrewd. Until then, fans have seen him leave a difficult fight and a world title behind.

Fans never buy noble moral stances when a fighter surrenders a title to avoid an absolute nightmare. If Janibek were a feather-fisted fringe contender or an overmatched mandatory, Sheeraz walking away over money or a past testing issue might pass the smell test. When the mandatory opponent happens to be an avoided Kazakh wrecking ball with an elite amateur pedigree, the narrative completely crumbles.

Janibek represents the worst possible opponent profile in professional boxing: high risk, modest commercial value, and desperate hunger. He has been frozen out of massive unification bouts for years precisely because champions know the danger he brings. He saw Sheeraz holding that WBO belt as his golden ticket to finally force the sport to take him seriously and secure the life-changing purses he has been chasing. Facing a motivated, heavy-handed southpaw who knows his entire career trajectory hinges on dismantling you is a terrifying proposition.

Sheeraz clearly did the math and panicked. Taking Janibek for seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars offered terrible risk-to-reward math, especially after Simon Zachenhuber exposed how vulnerable Sheeraz looks when opponents start landing clean counters. Getting knocked out on home soil by Janibek permanently erases the mystique Queensberry spent years building.

The public sees right through the sudden ethical concerns. Turning down a dangerous fight against a prime killer while simultaneously campaigning to share the ring with Canelo Alvarez—who served a well-documented suspension for clenbuterol—makes the excuse look laughably dishonest. Sheeraz wanted the prestige of calling himself a world champion, but when the real tax for holding that strap arrived at the purse bid, he chose self-preservation over genuine greatness.

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins Faces Cardiff Payday Reality
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins says he’ll fight Keyshawn Davis in Wales. He also wants the money to remain the same as when the bout was pitched for Madison Square Garden. If Pacquiao–Shakur joins Fury–Joshua in Cardiff, that demand becomes much harder to satisfy.

Hitchins says he has accepted the Davis fight and that Keyshawn told him he was ready to sign. He dislikes the proposed move overseas but would make the trip for the opportunity. The opponent isn’t his sticking point. The terms might be.

“As long as the pay is the same, I’m cool,” Hitchins told Sean Zittel and Radio Raheem.

The original plan, by Hitchins’s account, put him and Davis in the co-feature beneath Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in New York. Cardiff changes the audience and the setting. A possible Manny Pacquiao–Shakur Stevenson fight changes the card’s pecking order as well. If that bout is added, Hitchins–Davis would likely sit beneath two much bigger attractions.

Hitchins has every right to ask for the purse he wants. Promoters have to decide what the fight adds at that price. Two skilled Americans meeting at welterweight is an excellent matchup for boxing followers, but Hitchins’s patient style may be a tough sell to a stadium crowd waiting for Fury and Joshua. Twelve rounds of careful jabbing and clinching would put pressure on the event’s pace, especially if his bout runs close to the headliners.

Madison Square Garden would have given Hitchins familiar surroundings and supporters in the building. In Cardiff, he would need to win over a crowd with little reason to favor either American. Davis may have the more crowd pleasing combinations, though he still has to land them against a boxer who excels at controlling distance.

None of this means Hitchins is refusing Wales or that his purse is holding up the deal. No figures have been disclosed, and Pacquiao–Shakur has not been finalized. The offer Hitchins liked in New York may look different on a crowded Cardiff bill. He has accepted the opponent. Now he needs the terms to work.

Hitchins holding out for co-feature money while sitting in the number three slot shows a complete failure to grasp how Zuffa, TKO, and Netflix operate.

Dana White and TKO do not overpay undercard fighters who bring zero ticket sales or subscriptions. They run a business built on leverage. When a card features heavyweight giants like Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua alongside a pairing like Manny Pacquiao and Shakur Stevenson, every dollar is already allocated to the top of the marquee. Those headliners drive the subscriptions and pack eighty thousand seats in Cardiff. The third fight on the bill is there to fill airtime, not eat up premium budget.

Hitchins is confusing his personal ambition with actual market value. Fighters slotted third on a mega broadcast do not get multimillion-dollar packages. If he demands the same guarantee he was pitched when he thought he was the primary co-feature in New York, Zuffa and the organizers will simply look past him. Keyshawn wants the fight, but Keyshawn also has promotional backing and mainstream interest.

If Hitchins digs his heels in over money, matchmakers can easily replace him with another welterweight or junior welterweight hungry for global exposure on Netflix. By overplaying his hand, Hitchins risks sitting at home watching Keyshawn fight someone else under the brightest lights in the sport.

Matchmakers have an endless line of hungry contenders ready to take Hitchins’ spot for half the money just to get on a global Netflix stage. If Hitchins walks away over purse demands, nobody is shedding a tear, and the promoters will not hesitate to pivot to a replacement who comes to throw leather.

Keyshawn comes out ahead regardless. If Hitchins drops out, Keyshawn gets matched with an aggressive, fan-friendly welterweight or junior welterweight whom he can likely dismantle in style. Looking explosive on a bill featuring Tyson Fury, Anthony Joshua, Manny Pacquiao, and Shakur Stevenson does infinitely more for Keyshawn’s market value than chasing Hitchins around the ring for twelve rounds of clinches and jabs.

For Hitchins, walking away would be career self-sabotage. His style has never drawn mainstream attention or moved live gates. He needs marquee dance partners to stay relevant. Accepting smaller money to fight Keyshawn in Wales is the necessary cost of entry to unlock the division’s real moneymakers.

Beating Keyshawn is Hitchins’ only path to force his way into conversations with the big money names at welterweight. If Hitchins prices himself out now, he shuts the door on all of them [Ryan Garcia, Devin Haney, Teofimo Lopez and Rolando Romero]. He gets left in the cold, relegated to low-profile headline slots on small cards. Taking the fight, taking the pay cut, and taking the trip to Wales is his only real lottery ticket.

Sports.title: Fundora and Hadribeaj Give Fans Little to Talk About
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora promised to burn down Las Vegas. Ermal Hadribeaj promised a hard fight. Both sounded ready during Thursday’s virtual press conference, but the first media push for their October 17 title fight gave casual fans little reason to stop scrolling. That is a problem for a card whose main event already needs an introduction.

Fundora said he intends to extend his three-fight knockout streak. Hadribeaj spoke about the work that earned him a shot at the WBC super welterweight title and what becoming Albania’s first world champion would mean to him. Those stakes are real. Neither man, though, gave the press conference a line that made the matchup feel urgent.

“We’re only focused on this fight. We know that we can’t overlook anyone. We focus on the work and take it one fight at a time,” Fundora said during Thursday’s virtual press conference.

That is sensible preparation from a champion. It is a tough sales pitch. Hadribeaj was equally respectful, calling Fundora “a great guy” and recalling that they met three years ago. His most interesting answer came when he rejected the obvious advice to attack Fundora’s body. He said others have tried it and suggested he has worked on specific answers, but kept those details to himself.

The rest of the card has the same problem. Jermall Charlo was once a name that drew attention on its own. Long stretches out of the ring have cost him that pull, and a bout with Koen Mazoudier offers little to restore it before the opening bell. Their fight had been scheduled for July in Australia before Charlo’s trip fell through; moving it to Las Vegas has given the card a former champion, but not a matchup many fans were asking to see.

Brandon Figueroa’s title defense is harder to understand. He stopped Nick Ball in the final round to win the WBA featherweight belt, a result that should have set up another fight with immediate appeal. Instead, he faces 35-year-old Tomoki Kameda, who lost to IBF champion Angelo Leo in 2025. Kameda is ranked by the WBA, so this is a legitimate title defense. Still, Leo is the opponent who would give fans a clear answer about where Figueroa stands among the featherweight champions.

Fundora and Hadribeaj may produce an excellent fight. Figueroa usually makes opponents work, and Charlo’s return will interest those who have followed him for years. But Thursday was a chance to make people care before October 17. The fighters gave the promoter very little to work with, while the matchmaking left the card’s biggest questions unanswered.

Ghana News.title: 2027 AFCONQ: Ghana under pressure as Gambia beat Somalia 2-1
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s task of qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations has become more difficult after The Gambia secured a 2-1 victory over Somalia in the other Group C fixture.

The result leaves Ghana bottom of the group after the opening round of matches, following Thursday’s 2-0 defeat to Côte d’Ivoire in Bouaké.

Ebrima Colley gave The Gambia the lead before Bilal Njie restored parity for Somalia. Mohammed Badamosi then struck the decisive goal to hand the Scorpions all three points.

The result means Ghana now face an early test of their AFCON qualification campaign when they host The Gambia on Tuesday.

With the Black Stars already three points behind both Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia, a positive result has taken on added importance as Carlos Queiroz looks to avoid another difficult start.

Ghana endured a disastrous opening to the 2025 AFCON qualifiers, collecting just one point from their first two matches before eventually finishing the campaign without a win and missing out on the tournament.

Ghana News.title: Eastern NPP Women’s Organiser calls on AG, Police to secure bail for Salomey Baffoe
Ghana News.content:
The Eastern Regional Women’s Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Regina Bempong, is calling on the Attorney-General and the Police Criminal Investigations Department to secure bail for Senior Nursing Officer, Salomey Awiti Baffoe, who is being held in connection with the “Ghana Jollof” case.

According to her, Mrs Baffoe’s continued detention is unjustified, particularly as she is a mother of three and faces a misdemeanor charge.

Mr Baffoe was remanded by the Adentan Circuit Court on September 17, 2026, on a charge of abetment. Her bail application was rejected by the High Court in Accra on Thursday, September 24.

In a statement, Madam Bempong argued that the concerns over possible interference with electronic evidence should not be a basis for keeping Madam Baffour in custody.

She said the police have already seized her two mobile phones and, according to the police, accessed them.

Madam Bempong also maintained that the alleged offence is bailable and that Mrs Baffoe is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

She is therefore urging the Attorney-General and the Police CID to facilitate her release on reasonable conditions while investigations continue.

The Eastern Regional NPP Women’s Organiser is also appealing to the Chief Justice to urgently consider a petition filed by Madam Baffoe's lawyer, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, seeking to have the Court of Appeal sit on the matter concerning her liberty.

Madam Bempong has further called on women’s groups, the Ghana Registered Nurses and Midwives Association (GRNMA), FIDA and civil society organisations to speak up on the case.

Ghana News.title: Poverty, illiteracy driving acceptance of vote-buying among women – Damongo Queen Mother
Ghana News.content:
Queen Mother of the Damongo Traditional Area, Alijata Haruna, has attributed the acceptance of vote-buying among some women in the Savannah Region to poverty, illiteracy and limited employment opportunities.

Speaking at the “Democracy Is Not For Sale” forum in Damongo, organised by JoyNews on Friday, September 25, she said economic hardship makes some women more willing to accept money and other items offered by political actors during election periods.

She was responding to a question about why some voters regard cash received during elections as a normal gesture, despite concerns that such inducements could influence their voting decisions.

According to Alijata Haruna, the immediate economic needs of some women can make it difficult for them to reject such offers.

“I think one of the issues or the fundamental issue is about the poverty level of the women and then also the illiteracy rate. Over here [in Savannah Region] we have high illiteracy rate of women. So I think all those cloths and the hundred cedis to persuade me to vote for him or her, I don't think that I should refuse because I need it, because I really need it.

So definitely that is some of the fundamental factors that contribute to those things. It's about our illiteracy rates and also the poverty level of women and employment issues.”

She said addressing the underlying socio-economic conditions affecting women would be important in tackling the acceptance of vote-buying.

The “Democracy Is Not For Sale” forum forms part of efforts to encourage public discussion on electoral integrity and the factors that can undermine the democratic process.

Ghana News.content:
The JoyNews' Democracy Is Not For Sale forum has moved to Damongo in the Savannah Region, bringing together stakeholders and residents to discuss the growing influence of money in Ghana’s democratic process.

Ghana News.title: GNFS launches 2026/27 National Anti-Bushfire campaign in Atebubu, records 62.8% reduction in bushfire cases
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) has officially launched its 2026/27 National Anti-Bushfire Campaign in Atebubu, in the Bono East Region, with a strong call for collective action to protect the environment and secure a greener Ghana.

The event, held under the theme "Bushfire Prevention: A Collective Action for Sustainable Environmental Development and a Greener Ghana," brought together a cross-section of stakeholders, including the Bono East Regional Minister, Francis Owusu Antwi, traditional leaders, farmers, students, security services, and the general public.

Among the dignitaries present were the Omanhene of the Atebubu Traditional Area, Ohempon Dr. Yeboah Asiamah; the Omanhene of the Dwan Traditional Area, Okoforbour Awase Afura III; the President of the Bono East Regional House of Chiefs and Bassamanhene, Nana Owusu Ansah; and the Municipal Chief Executive for Atebubu, Masaudu Thomas Ayaaba.

The campaign is designed to be nationwide, covering all 16 regions of Ghana. Activities lined up include community durbars, school outreach programmes, radio sensitisation, the creation of fire belts, and the establishment of rapid-response patrols.

Community fire volunteers are also set to receive improved tools and resources to enable them to act as first responders in their localities.

Addressing the gathering, the Chief Fire Officer of the GNFS, CFO Daniella Mawusi Ntow Sarpong, emphasised that bushfire prevention is a collective responsibility that requires every stakeholder to come together as a team.

She reported that through collective efforts, there has been a significant reduction in bushfire incidents across the country.

According to her, “631 bushfire cases were recorded between January and August 2025, while only 235 cases were recorded within the same period in 2026”.

This, she noted, represents a 62.8 percent reduction, which she attributed to strong collaborative work by all stakeholders.

The Bono East Regional Minister, Hon. Francis Owusu Antwi, in his remarks, emphasised the dire consequences of bushfires, including their ability to weaken the human environment.

He reaffirmed the government's full commitment to environmental protection through various policies, including the restoration of degraded lands.

"A greener Ghana is essential, and we must all work to help achieve that," he stated.

The Omanhene of the Atebubu Traditional Area, Ohempon Dr. Yeboah Asiamah, on his part, thanked the authorities for their efforts and pledged that Nananom would continue to contribute their quota towards the success of the campaign.

He, however, cautioned the public against actions that deliberately cause bushfires, noting that culprits should be punished to serve as a deterrent to others.

Stakeholders at the event appealed to the public and corporate organisations for logistical support and protective gear to assist firefighters in their work.

The launch in Atebubu signals the beginning of a nationwide push to reduce bushfires, protect farmlands, and preserve Ghana's natural environment for future generations.

Ghana News.title: I’ll vote for a female president; women are less likely to steal from the state – Okyeame Kwame
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian rapper and developmental activist Kwame Nsiah-Apau, popularly known by his stage name Okyeame Kwame, aka the Rap Doctor, has shared his opinion on women taking up leadership roles in governance.

Known for his feminism, the musician has been a strong supporter of women, consistently empowering them to break barriers and take up responsibilities alongside their male counterparts in order to change the narrative of vulnerability in society.

In a recent interview with Nikki Samonas on Joy Prime’s Changes show, he was asked whether he would vote for and advocate for a female party flagbearer to win a presidential contest and take over the government. He confidently said he would gladly do so.

According to him, this is because he considers women to be more empathetic and less likely to engage in the misuse of public funds compared to male presidents.

“If that woman and the man are both equally qualified and they’re equally responsible, I’ll vote for the woman because women usually, not all the time have a bit more empathy and they’re less likely to steal from the state than men,” he said.

However, he said this cannot be generalized, as there is evidence of cases where some female leaders have been involved in the misuse of state resources.

Aside from that, he strongly believes and is convinced that women are naturally caring and possess a motherly instinct to look after people. As such, he believes they are capable of managing the affairs of a nation if given the opportunity to serve as president.

For him, men have a tendency to care more about things than people, which makes him confident that a female president would be capable of leading the country effectively.

“…women come with a lot of love, empathy, sympathy, nurture; they have that motherly thing where they care more about people. Men are inclined to care more about things as Jordan Peterson said. So, I think a women president will be dope,” he emphasized.

His support for women has also led to the release of his new song, titled ‘Big Up’, which he says is dedicated to celebrating women who have contributed to Ghana’s growth in various ways. According to him, these women have not received sufficient recognition for their contributions to the country.

“In the third song of the song ‘Big Up’, I mentioned some five women; Susanna Al-Hassan who was the first female Minister of State in the whole of Africa who also supported Nkrumah during independence, Naa Dedei Ashikishan who was one of the business women in Ghana. Her face is on the 50 pesewas coin; Theodosia Okoh who was an artiste, Mabel Danquah and Ama Nkrumah. These women during the struggle for independence, supported. Some of them went to jail, lost their jobs, they had studied and put their hearts behind the struggle for independence and the beginning of Ghana. But I don’t think that these women are celebrated well enough. There are more of them but I mentioned five in my song.”

Given their enormous contributions to the country’s growth, he suggested that the lives and achievements of such women be studied in schools and that some prominent streets in the country be named after them as meaningful ways of recognizing their contributions.

“I want to see all of them in Social Studies books, I want students to write exams about them. I want young girls to know that we don’t only have the founding fathers, but there are also founding mothers. I want prominent streets named after some of them. I want them to have their own roundabout; the founding mothers roundabout,” he suggested.

He admonished society to promote and celebrate women in the same way men are celebrated, in order to create balance and encourage men to embrace their feminine side, thereby creating more room for empathy.

Ghana News.title: More public education needed to stop vote-buying – Savannah Region MP
Ghana News.content:
Savannah Regional Minister Salisu Be-Awuribe has called for stronger public education to help tackle vote buying, saying an informed electorate must play a leading role in resisting attempts to influence voters with money.

According to him, educating citizens about the value of their votes and encouraging them to challenge electoral inducements could help protect Ghana’s democratic process from the growing influence of money.

Speaking to JoyNews at the ‘Democracy Is Not For Sale’ programme in Damongo, Mr Be-Awuribe said the public must not remain passive in the face of vote buying.

“When the public is well educated and they themselves rise up to the challenge, then we may be far from being in the situation that we are in,” he said on Sepetember 25.

He said the responsibility for tackling vote buying should not rest solely with politicians and law enforcement agencies, stressing that citizens themselves have an important role to play in rejecting attempts to influence their electoral choices with money.

Mr Be-Awuribe commended civil society organisations and media houses for bringing the issue to public attention and contributing to discussions on the impact of money on electoral processes.

Mr Be-Awuribe further called on citizens to reject attempts by individuals to influence electoral outcomes through financial inducements, stressing that the public must take an active role in confronting vote buying.

“The public should revolt against them and know that their conscience cannot be bought,” he said.

Mr Be-Awuribe maintained that sustained public education and citizen participation are crucial to safeguarding the integrity of Ghana’s electoral processes.

Ghana News.title: Absa Bank commissions new head office, commits to strengthening operations in Ghana
Ghana News.content:
Vice President, Prof Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang

Absa Bank Ghana has commissioned its new state-of-the-art head office in Accra, marking a major investment in its operations and signalling the bank’s commitment to its long-term growth in Ghana’s financial services sector.

The new facility, known as Absa Place, was officially commissioned on Friday, September 25, with Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang and senior officials from the Bank of Ghana, Absa Group and other stakeholders in attendance.

Speaking at the ceremony, the Vice President said the value of the investment should go beyond the modern infrastructure and translate into stronger services and greater opportunities for businesses and customers.

She urged Absa Bank Ghana to expand access to finance for women-owned businesses and young entrepreneurs, while developing practical financial solutions for businesses operating in agriculture, manufacturing and trade.

“Expand access to finance for women-owned businesses and young entrepreneurs and develop practical solutions for businesses in agriculture, manufacturing, and trade,” she said.

Prof. Opoku-Agyemang also encouraged the bank to leverage technology to deepen financial inclusion, while ensuring that customers who require personalised support are not excluded as financial services become increasingly digital.

She further called for stronger cybersecurity and information security, stressing the need to protect customers’ funds, personal information and transactions.

“The Bank of Ghana’s renewed focus on cyber and information security is therefore timely. Innovations must continue, but so must investment in the systems, the safeguards, and people required to protect customers and preserve confidence in our financial system,” she said.

BoG Urges Stronger Resilience

Second Deputy Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Matilda Asante Asiedu, said the commissioning of Absa Place should represent more than the completion of a corporate building.

She pointed out the investment must contribute to stronger governance, operational resilience, sound decision-making and sustained customer confidence.

Matilda Asante Asiedu

According to her, the rapid evolution of digital platforms, payment systems and changing customer expectations has created new opportunities for the banking sector, but also introduced risks that financial institutions must effectively manage.

She stressed that innovation must be accompanied by appropriate controls, security, data protection and sound risk management.

“As financial institutions grow more dependent on technology and interconnected systems, operational resilience, security, data protection, and sound risk management become ever more critical,” she said.

Ms Asante Asiedu said the new facility should provide Absa Ghana with a more resilient operating environment, facilitate collaboration and support reliable operations and quality service delivery.

She also reminded Absa of its responsibilities as a systemically important bank, noting that its financial and operational strength has implications for businesses, employees, counterparties and confidence in the wider financial ecosystem.

She urged the bank to maintain strong risk management, adequate liquidity, regulatory compliance and responsible conduct.

Absa Pledges Responsible Growth

The Managing Director of Absa Bank Ghana, Dr Edward Botchway, said the bank’s board would continue to provide the stewardship and oversight needed to ensure the institution remains strong, well governed and responsible.

He said the completion of Absa Place also comes with a responsibility to ensure that the investment delivers value to customers and partners.

“Our customers and partners also deserve to benefit from every investment that we celebrate. As we celebrate the completion of Absa Place, our responsibility is to ensure that the work undertaken in this building justifies the confidence, effort and resources invested in its creation,” he said.

Dr Botchway said the bank would continue to focus on sustainable growth, effective customer service and contributing meaningfully to Ghana’s development.

The commissioning of Absa Place marks another milestone in Absa Ghana’s operations as the bank positions its infrastructure to support its future activities in Ghana’s evolving financial services sector.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
