World.title: Estonia launches joint study to map optimal electricity mix by 2027
World.content:
Estonia's Chamber of Commerce, major energy companies and government have launched a joint effort to determine the most cost‑efficient mix of electricity generation, storage and cross‑border connections needed to meet the country's rising power demand.

The analysis will be completed by the end of February 2027, the chamber announced.

The analysis seeks an answer to the question of which portfolio of production, storage and connection capacities is optimal for Estonia at different consumption levels and what investments this requires.

The Chamber of Commerce and Industry emphasizes that the analysis will be carried out based on the principles of intellectual honesty, freedom from ideology, impartiality and transparency. "All technologies are assessed on the same basis, and the result is not directed by predetermined technological or worldview preferences. All assumptions and constraints affecting the analysis are clearly set out and justified," the chamber's statement says.

The process is structured so that the input and decision‑making rights of companies supporting the project are clearly separated. The companies supporting the project and Elering belong to an advisory council that provides sectoral input and feedback, but does not decide on the assumptions and inputs used in the model. These decisions are made by a steering committee consisting of representatives of the state, academia and the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, which also approves the terms of reference, methodology, input data and constraints.

Public discussion expected

All core elements of the analysis — the terms of reference, methodology, inputs, results and conclusions — will be made public so that public discussion can take place.

Interim results of the project will not be commented on during the analysis. The project results will be presented to the public once the analysis is complete.

The analysis is funded by the companies participating in the project. The project is supported by Eesti Energia/Enefit, Utilitas, Alexela, VKG, Evecon, Baltic Energy Partners, Saare Wind and Fermi Energia, as well as electricity consumers Maag Food and Lemeks. Elering participates in the advisory council as the system operator.

The steering committee includes Einari Kisel (Ministry of Climate), Ahti Kuningas (Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications), Raoul Lättemäe (Ministry of Finance), Erkki Raasuke (EIS), Evelin Pärn‑Lee (Competition Authority), Jaak Aaviksoo (Estonian Academy of Sciences), Hannes Agabus (TalTech), Ivo Palu (Estonian Electrical Power Engineering Society), Uku Varblane (Foresight Centre), and Mait Palts and Raivo Vasnu (Estonian Chamber of Commerce and Industry).

The project is led by foreign‑investment consultant and former Minister of Entrepreneurship and Foreign Trade Anne Sulling.

The analysis will be completed at the end of February 2027, before the parliamentary elections, so that the results can be used by the new government in shaping energy‑policy decisions.

The initiative grew out of a report published in April 2026 by Anne Sulling and Erkki Raasuke, which examined under what conditions international investors would be willing to invest in large energy‑infrastructure projects in Estonia.

One of the report's central recommendations was to calculate the optimal portfolio of electricity production, storage and external connections for Estonia, in order to provide the state with an analytical basis and investors with the necessary foresight.

Elering is conducting a separate study

At the same time, Elering and Tallinn University of Technology have begun preparing future scenarios for Estonia's energy system, in order to assess the impact of different energy‑policy and technological choices on electricity prices and security of supply. This analysis will be completed by the end of 2027.

In the course of the work, Elering will create an electricity‑market model that compares possible development paths for Estonia's energy system up to 2050. The model should help assess how different choices affect electricity prices and system reliability. Tallinn University of Technology will prepare European energy‑system development trajectories and possible scenarios for Estonia.

The analysis will take into account network tariffs, the renewable‑energy charge, the cost of ensuring security of supply, the cost of balancing the system, and the need to reinforce electricity and gas networks up to 2050. The analysis does not include possible changes to state taxes and excise duties.

Elering is conducting the analysis as an independent system operator.

Scenario development and consultations will begin in autumn 2026. European development trajectories and Estonian scenarios will be discussed with stakeholders from September 2026 to February 2027. The scenarios to be modelled will be approved in February 2027, and the report on competitive energy prices will be completed by the end of 2027.

World.title: International nightlife conference to be held in Tallinn in October
World.content:
The international night culture conference "Dance Floor of Democracy" will take place at Tallinn's HALL club October 9, bringing together European night culture leaders, city officials, researchers and artists.

The conference will focus on how night culture can become a natural part of a city's identity and democratic urban space. "Clubs are places where the different faces of a city — different communities, generations and people from different backgrounds — share the same space and find something in common," said Maren Niemeyer, director of the Goethe-Institut in Tallinn. "Yet night culture venues are still primarily regarded as entertainment establishments rather than cultural spaces deserving conscious support from society and policymakers."

"DJs and producers are music curators and artists who guide dancers in discovering music — just as museum curators and artists guide us into the world of paintings and sculptures. A well-curated dance floor is just as necessary for a city as a museum, sports center or park: it creates a physical space where people can come together, share experiences and meet people they do not yet know," said HALL founder and conference co-organizer Elena Natale.

"The idea behind the conference is to bring together the people who create and organize nightlife and shape it in cities and to ask what conditions night culture needs to remain vibrant and develop alongside the city and its communities," said conference project manager Jaan Ulst.

The conference program will examine night culture from three perspectives: how cities, clubs and communities can work together to create a vibrant night culture ecosystem, how what happens in club spaces shapes the community and the city around them and how to make the dance floor an integral part of democratic urban space.

Speakers sharing their experiences will include Amsterdam night mayor Freek Wallagh; Micol Didi, responsible for project support and communications at the Vienna Club Commission; Martin Fueller, dean of the Tresor Academy of Subcultural Understanding; Kate Howard, night-time economy adviser to Galway City Council; Gabija Liaugminaitė, project manager at the Vilnius Night Office; and Benoît Rousseau, director of music and dance at Gaîté Lyrique. Artists and curators will be represented by, among others, DJ and Motto Sono Records founder Miia Magia and HALL artist program director Micaela Saraceno.

Following the conference, ERSO and techno will meet at HALL: musicians from the Estonian National Symphony Orchestra will perform Kenn-Eerik Kannike's debut album "Computations," arranged for classical instruments by Karl Tipp. After the concert, the evening will continue with a club night featuring DJs Chloe Lula (Tresor, Berlin), Miia Magia (Motto Sono Records, HE.SHE.THEY., Parabel Agency, Helsinki) and Ciara May (Cultúr/Riot, Galway).

The conference will take place October 9 at HALL (Peetri 6) in Tallinn. Attendance is free, but advance registration is required.

World.title: Estonia's only artichoke farmer sees bright future for local crop
World.content:
Estonia's only dedicated artichoke grower says this summer's conditions were ideal for the crop, now thriving after years of testing different varieties and growing methods.

Artifarm owner Andreas Kiik said he first got the idea to try growing artichokes in Estonia after trying them on a trip to Italy. While early efforts were largely a flop, years of trial and error eventually led to success in the local climate.

"We started experimenting eight years ago, and eventually got to the point where, with the right varieties and growing methods, they grow very well here," he said.

Artichokes thrive in moisture and moderate temperatures. This year's summer in Estonia was particularly favorable, and Kiik hopes the Mediterranean crop will start bringing in some income.

Fresh Estonian-grown artichokes. Source: ERR

"It would be great if we could cover the growing costs, but next year should be even better," he added.

While the tender, edible heart accounts for only about 30–40 percent of the plant, Kiik's Lääne County operation uses the rest as well.

"We just made pasta from the outer leaves, but they can also be used to make a good alcoholic drink or tea," he explained, noting that the stalks can be pickled just like cucumbers.

Most of Kiik's customers are currently restaurants and small eateries, but some people also buy artichokes from him for themselves.

"Those who order generally know exactly what they want," he said, adding that many are regular customers.

World.title: Defense official: Russia's neighbors have stepped up responses to air threats
World.content:
Due to Russia's war of aggression in Ukraine, more and more drones and even cruise missiles have ended up in neighboring countries, which is why the Baltic states and Poland have strengthened measures for responding to air threats, said Gert Kaju, head of the Ministry of Defense's defense readiness department.

The side effects of Russia's aggression are increasingly being felt in countries adjacent to the war zone; for example, 39 drones have entered Moldovan airspace this year, Kaju said on Friday at the weekly briefing held at the Ministry of Defense.

"In addition, drones have been shot down in Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and also Romania. And Russian cruise missiles have also ended up in third countries — they have either flown through that airspace or somehow veered into it," he described.

"In response to this, the procedure for deploying air‑defense assets has been made faster, primarily in Poland and also in the direction of the Baltic states — meaning the chain of command has been simplified and accelerated in order to respond to this air threat," Kaju said.

According to the overview presented by the Ministry of Defense representative, Russia continues long‑range strikes on Ukraine's critical infrastructure, hitting residential buildings, industrial enterprises, administrative buildings and transport infrastructure in at least 14 oblasts over the past week.

"According to Ukrainian data, Russia has launched circa 1,900 jet‑powered drones in September, of which Ukraine claims to have destroyed circa 60 percent," he noted. "Due to these attacks, Ukraine has lost nearly 90 percent of its steel‑production capacity."

Ukrainian strikes against energy infrastructure

With its long‑range strikes, Ukraine hit oil‑refining plants in various Russian regions during the previous week of the war, including in Moscow, Yaroslavl and Samara oblasts. As a result of the strikes, Russia's oil‑refining capacity has suffered additional losses; Russia is losing production capacity, Kaju said.

"In addition to infrastructure related to oil refining, Ukraine continues to strike Russia's logistics centers, including in the Moscow region," Kaju added. "As for medium‑range strikes, here Ukraine's drone units have focused primarily on airfields in Crimea and Rostov oblast, as well as areas related to drone storage and launch sites, and also additional energy facilities in Crimea."

According to Kahju, more than 400 different energy facilities in Crimea have been hit since early July, and in the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea Ukraine has managed to put more than 300 vessels out of action.

Fighting continues in Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia and Kharkiv oblasts

Speaking about what is happening on the front line, Kaju said that the most intense fighting is still taking place in Donetsk oblast, in the direction of Pokrovsk and Kostyantynivka, as well as in the direction of Lyman. Following these in intensity are Zaporizhzhia and Kharkiv oblast.

Ukraine has carried out counterattacks primarily in Kharkiv oblast, including in the direction of Kupiansk, and in Donetsk oblast, where Ukraine's focus is primarily on the Lyman direction.

"Russia's combat losses are 1,500 soldiers per day, and therefore we can say that Russia's weekly losses are over ten thousand soldiers," Kaju stated.

Russia's threats and propaganda continue

Kaju also spoke about how Russia continues rhetoric in which it blames everyone else for what is happening in Ukraine, including Ukraine and the Western world, with Moscow claiming that the Western world is using this situation to generally escalate relations with Russia.

"Russia also continues pressuring countries that support Ukraine, so that they would abandon supporting Ukraine," he said. "As an example, we can point out the situation where the Russian Foreign Ministry summoned the chargé d'affaires of the United Kingdom in Moscow and issued an official protest against London's further increase of arms deliveries to Ukraine. At the political and communicative level, Russia continues to spread its worn‑out narrative," Kaju described.

"In addition to the fighting and the air threat described above in neighboring countries, hybrid activity has increasingly come into view in third countries — whether direct acts of sabotage, various types of information operations or other such activity. That is, companies involved in supporting Ukraine are threatened, attempts are made to attack them or force them to stop their activities," the Ministry of Defense official said.

"All of this is part of Russia's narrative, where their goal is to create fear and uncertainty on the other side, because creating fear and uncertainty is one part of Russia's deterrence policy, trying through this to show that Russia is a large and threatening force," he explained.

"Our response to this must be, on the one hand, that we monitor it, respond to these steps with our own steps, and in the case of incidents it is also important to attribute the event to its initiator," Kaju emphasized.

"So in summary — one thing is the war in Ukraine, but on the other hand its effects are increasingly felt in neighboring countries, primarily through the hybrid activities described above. Our task is to monitor and respond to them according to the nature of the threat," Kaju said.

World.title: Prosecutors launch criminal probe into Maardu football match-fixing case
World.content:
The Estonian Football Association (EJK) filed a complaint over the incident after opening a disciplinary investigation.

The EJK has also banned three people connected with the club from football activities. A match between FC Tallinn and Maardu earlier this month was abandoned with around 12 minutes' regular time to go after Maardu conceded three goals in seven minutes, as well as giving away a penalty.

The EJK launched its disciplinary investigation a couple of weeks ago into possible breaches of its disciplinary regulations. The provisions cover breaches of integrity principles, direct or indirect involvement in betting, the pre-arrangement of the course or outcome of a match, and the obligation to report such activity.

"During the investigation, the EJK is cooperating with international football organizations, while Maardu Linnameeskond has also indicated its willingness to cooperate. Based on the material gathered, the EJK filed a criminal complaint with the prosecutor's office," the association said on September 10, immediately after the match.

On the same day the EJK banned Deniss Kovtun, Artjom Volkov and Vladislav Tšurilkin from all football-related activities for the duration of the disciplinary investigation. The Disciplinary and Ethics Committee will review the sanction upon receipt of additional information or once the investigation has concluded.

On Friday, September 25, the prosecutor's office announced that criminal proceedings had been launched following the EJK's complaint.

"The complaint submitted by the Estonian Football Association has raised suspicions that the results of football matches may have been manipulated for financial gain," Northern District Prosecutor Siret Vaher-Torni said. "The validity of the circumstances presented to the prosecutor's office and the roles of those potentially involved will be established in the criminal proceedings that have been launched."

Maardu Linnameeskond announced on Tuesday, September 22, that it was suspending its participation in the league and had also halted training.

Founded in 1997, the club has played under its current name since 2016. In 2019, it was promoted to the Meistriliiga, the top flight for the first and, to date, only time in its history, but finished last and was relegated back to the Esiliiga.

The Esiliiga match between FC Tallinn and Maardu Linnameeskond on Thursday, September 10 was abandoned in the 78th minute over suspected betting fraud, after Maardu conceded three goals in seven minutes and gave away a penalty. The Estonian Football Association has banned three people connected with Maardu from football-related activities for the duration of a disciplinary investigation, with the club suspected of pre-arranging the match and breaching integrity rules. Two matches in Estonian football have previously been called off over betting suspicions — one in the top division in 2013 and another in the Esiliiga in 2016 .

World.title: Iraqi PM calls on US firms to seize investment opportunities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called on US companies on Wednesday to seize investment opportunities available in Iraq, particularly in the petrochemicals, glass, and phosphate industries, as well as the gas and clean energy sectors.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting in New York with a delegation from the US Chamber of Commerce, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister stated that Iraq has considerable natural resources, human resources, and a key geographical position, all of which serve as necessary foundations for successful partnerships. He explained that the government is seeking to use these resources to promote economic development and increase investment possibilities.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the government’s commitment to providing support for businesses and investors, such as granting ownership of land for investment projects in accordance with Iraqi laws, as well as access to tax and customs exemptions for up to ten years.

Iraq is working on infrastructure and transportation projects, notably the strategic project of the Development Road, which will improve Iraq’s position as a corridor connecting the East and West, according to al-Zaidi.

The prime minister affirmed that the government looks forward to establishing factories and setting up projects to diversify the economy and create job opportunities.

Al-Zaidi also asked members of the US Chamber of Commerce and specialized firms to attend the Baghdad Energy Conference and capitalize on the prospects offered in the country. He added that Iraq aspires to establish economic partnerships based on collaboration, mutual interest, and long-term investment.

World.title: Iraqi PM, US president discuss partnerships, regional stability
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met with US President Donald Trump in New York on Tuesday on the sideline of his participation in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

The two leaders discussed bilateral relations and approaches to strengthen cooperation and partnership between the two countries across political, economic, and investment sectors, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The two sides also reviewed the latest developments in the region, as well as the joint efforts undertaken by Iraq and the United States to enhance regional and international security and stability.

The discussion takes place ahead of a crucial September 30 milestone, which marks a shift in Washington-Baghdad ties toward long-term economic collaboration as the US prepares to end its coalition military mission in Iraq.

Amid continuing negotiations between Iraq and US officials, including a recent meeting between al-Zaidi and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Washington pressured Baghdad on its obligations to place weapons possessed by armed factions under state supervision.

In addition to their exclusive bilateral discussion, al-Zaidi attended President Trump’s larger gathering that included leaders from important regional powers, including Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Jordan, Egypt, and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) nations.

The larger gathering addressed strategies to coordinate post-war arrangements, protect global commerce supply lines, and develop diplomatic frameworks for Middle Eastern stability.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets Iranian president in New York
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met on Wednesday with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in New York on the sidelines of their participation in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

According to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the meeting addressed developments in the region and the necessity of working together to handle difficulties in ways that promote security and stability.

The two leaders also addressed approaches to keep the region from spiraling into a cycle of escalation, tensions, and crises.

During a meeting on Wednesday with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein emphasized the importance of defusing regional tensions through dialogue.

The meeting addressed bilateral relations and regional developments, as well as the importance of continued coordination between the two countries to respond to current challenges and support diplomatic efforts aimed at enhancing regional stability.

Hussein also stressed the significance of continued diplomatic efforts among the parties involved to defuse tension and prevent escalation.

Araghchi outlined the discussions that began between Iran and the United States, sponsored by an intermediary, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly meetings in New York. These discussions attempt to de-escalate the situation and find approaches to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for navigation.

The two ministers also discussed the outcomes of the meeting involving the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, Iraq, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Egypt, and Turkey—attended by US President Donald Trump—as well as how regional and international relationships might help efforts for de-escalation.

World.title: Iraq’s Gulf Cup 27 match against Oman ends in 1-1 draw
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi and Omani national teams drew 1-1 on Wednesday in the opening match of the 27th Gulf Cup held at Prince Abdullah Al-Faisal Sports City Stadium in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

Iraq launched a strong attack, causing Oman to make a defensive mistake. Zaid Ismail took advantage of the rebound and set it up for Mohammed Qasim, who fired a rocket shot with his left foot into the near corner, giving the “Lions of Mesopotamia” an early lead in the sixth minute.

The Omani team’s performance improved, and their level rose during the second half. After a decisive and skillful pass from Ahmed al-Kaabi, Nasser al-Rawahi scored the equalizer brilliantly from a close range, winning the “Man of the Match” award in recognition of his outstanding performance.

In a candid evaluation, Australian coach Graham Arnold, who manages the Iraqi national team, acknowledged that the team’s performance fell short of expectations. He pointed out that the rushed preparations had hindered the implementation of their tactical plan.

The Iraqi team only had one training session before the tournament compared to six for the Omani team.

“We were not the better side, and we must work harder in the coming matches to secure the win,” Arnold said.

The manager of the Oman team, Tarik Sektioui, expressed his great pride in his team, describing the squad as “fighters” for their ability to recover from an early setback and snatch a vital opening point against the defending champions.

World.title: Turkey to hand over military base to enhance Iraqi sovereignty
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan announced on Wednesday that Turkish forces will gradually hand over the Bashiqa-Zelikan base to the Iraqi government.

According to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the handover process will take place in accordance with an agreed-upon mechanism and timeline amid the progress Iraq has achieved through security measures.

During their meeting on the sideline of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, the two leaders agreed to deepen security cooperation in negotiations in which Iraqi and Turkish authorities discussed strategic relations.

Additionally, al-Zaidi and Erdogan agreed to completely expand the Iraqi state’s authority in Sinjar and to eliminate the presence of banned foreign armed groups.

Turkey established a military base in Bashiqa, near Mosul, in December 2015, initially deploying around 600 soldiers to train local forces to combat ISIS terrorist groups.

The deployment of Turkish soldiers without formal consent from Iraq has been a longstanding point of contention, often regarded as a violation of Iraq’s sovereignty and a strain on the relationship between Ankara and Baghdad.

As part of the agreement, Iraq agreed to restore state authority in Sinjar and remove or disarm foreign armed groups and militias that Turkey sees as security risks.

World.title: Iraq to raise gas production at Nahr Bin Umar to 300 million cubic feet
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil revealed on Monday that it is planning to increase associated gas recovery at the Nahr Bin Umar field to 300 million cubic feet per day.

Deputy Minister for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber chaired a meeting to review associated gas recovery plans and projects at the Nahr Bin Umar field in the southern province of Basra.

The meeting was attended by representatives from the South Gas Company (SGC) and the project operator, Halfaya Gas Company, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The meeting focused on the development plan to enhance associated gas recovery, aiming for a target of 300 million standard cubic feet per day.

The plan will be implemented in two phases, each with a capacity of 150 million standard cubic feet per day.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil said earlier that the Bin Umar gas project will produce between 500 and 600 tons of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Saber mentioned earlier that the project, which will minimize gas flaring and support the country’s electricity grid, is planned to be operational by the end of April.

Saber confirmed the news while inspecting the project’s final connection point in mid-April.

The project will produce 70 million standard cubic feet per day of raw gas, between 500 and 600 tons of LPG for home consumption, around 80 million standard cubic feet per day of dry gas for power plants, and more than 1,800 barrels per day of condensates.

The initiative is an important step toward increasing gas utilization, preventing gas flaring, and strengthening the country’s electricity grid.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit 3 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed on Tuesday that oil exports for August reached approximately 70 million barrels, with daily shipments exceeding three million barrels.

In a televised interview, Khudair explained that the deals the ministry reached to transport oil through the Turkish port of Ceyhan raised the volumes to 600,000 barrels per day, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Iraq’s oil exports fluctuated during September 2026, amid ongoing geopolitical tensions related to the Middle East war and Baghdad’s efforts to diversify its export routes.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that exports started at three million barrels per day at the beginning of September but have since gradually declined to about 2.4 million barrels per day at present.

Despite a decline in Iraqi oil exports during September, the figures still surpassed the average daily exports in August, which were approximately 2.35 million barrels per day. This increase was bolstered by enhanced shipping traffic and a decrease in shipping disruptions in the Gulf over the past few weeks.

In early September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

The prime minister indicated that it is important to improve infrastructure and export capacity to meet the expected rise in output.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

Al-Zaidi directed an increase in output from oil fields in the Kurdistan region of Iraq and the expansion of exploration activities to achieve the plan’s objectives and reach a production capacity of 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

World.title: Iraq’s exports hit $19.55 billion in Q1 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Figures released by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) showed that the country’s exports reached $19.55 billion in the first quarter of 2026, compared to imports of $10.27 billion.

Hydrocarbons continued to account for the significant bulk of Iraq’s exports, exposing the country to larger global energy dynamics.

Iraq’s crude oil exports totaled $18.64 billion, petroleum products $762.2 million, and other exports $148.5 million.

The state sector’s imports totaled $1.35 billion, and the private sector’s imports reached $8.92 billion, according to the National Iraqi News Agency (NINA).

Iraq’s trade balance indicated a surplus of $10.82 billion, according to figures from the CBI that compare exports with imports.

The country’s exports during the first quarter of 2026 are lower than those of the fourth quarter of 2025, which stood at $21.62 billion.

Iraq’s export capacity during the first quarter of 2026 experienced significant headwinds due to rigorous OPEC+ production limits and interruptions related to maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: In a first, waste plastic mixed with bitumen in pilot test section of NH-44
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a first for the road sector, govt has used waste plastic as a wet mix with bitumen to lay a bituminous highway stretch, a move that is likely to reduce imports of the key construction material while addressing the growing problem of plastic waste.

On Thursday, a pilot test section was laid on the main carriageway of NH-44 in Jhansi. Officials associated with the pilot said the technology has potential to reduce conventional bitumen consumption by around 4%, lowering demand for a material that India largely imports to meet domestic requirements. They added that the modified bitumen could cost around 20% less than conventional bitumen.

The waste plastic wet-process technology for producing premium-quality Waste Plastic Modified Bitumen (W-PMB 76-10) has been developed by IIT (BHU), Varanasi, under a research programme funded by the ministry of road transport and highways.

The performance of the pilot stretch will be monitored by IIT (BHU) to assess its long-term engineering performance and field suitability, officials said.

India generates around 25,000 tonne of plastic waste every day. Until now, waste plastic has been used in road construction only as a dry mix with aggregates while laying the bituminous layer. The new method mixes processed waste plastic directly with bitumen before it is laid, making it the first such pilot on a national highway.





Officials said the technology offers multiple benefits, including the value-added reuse of waste plastic through a scientifically controlled process and improved rut resistance of bituminous mixes under high ambient temperatures and heavy axle loads.

âLaboratory evaluations have shown that LDPE-modified bitumen provides better resistance to moisture damage and greater resistance to rutting at high temperatures. The modified binder increases the stiffness and high-temperature performance of asphalt, helping pavements withstand permanent deformation under heavy traffic loads and extreme temperatures,â an official said.

World.title: 2022 Rajouri IED blast: Police file chargesheet against 4
World.content:
JAMMU: J&K Police have filed a chargesheet against four terrorists, including a Pakistan-based

handler, in a 2022 IED blast case.

Two migrant labourers were injured in the explosion below Jaganaloo bridge in Rajouri district on April 19 that year.

World.title: 'Mafia ruled UP, Yogi govt eliminated it': Amit Shah highlights political stability, policy implementation under BJP govt
World.content:
NOIDA: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Friday said the BJP government had eliminated the mafia from Uttar Pradesh, creating a conducive atmosphere for investment in the state.

Addressing the UP International Trade Show 2026, Shah recalled the situation in the state before the BJP came to power in 2017 and said the Yogi Adityanath government had taken steps to eliminate mafia elements across Uttar Pradesh.

"There was a time when the mafia ruled UP. In 2017, the BJP formed the government here, with Yogi Adityanath assuming the role of Chief Minister. The Yogi government has successfully eliminated the mafia across the state, and this has created a conducive atmosphere for investment..." Shah said.

He also highlighted political stability under Prime Minister Narendra Modi and said policy continuity and implementation had helped transform India into a global manufacturing hub.

"Political stability has become a hallmark of our leader, PM Modi. By earning the public's trust over 3 consecutive terms as Prime Minister, he has not only formulated policies but also ensured their consistent implementation on the ground, he said.

Shah added that "PM Modi has also demonstrated great dynamism in refining existing policies and formulating new ones based on experience, thereby transforming India into an attractive global manufacturing hub."





The Union home minister recalled that in 2013, the Uttar Pradesh government had organised a conference to attract industrial investment to the state, but the event had to be held in Delhi due to the law-and-order situation in Lucknow.

"In 2013, UP govt organised a conference to attract industrial investment to the state... At that time, it had to be held in Delhi. When the media raised questions about this, UP officials frankly admitted that the law-and-order situation in Lucknow was such that no investor was willing to come there.

That is why they had to move the event to Delhi," Shah said.

He contrasted the situation with the present and credited the change to the "double-engine" government.

"But look at the situation today: That very same Uttar Pradesh has become free from fear, a hub for investment, and an engine of national growth. This transformation is the magic of the 'double-engine' government," he said.

Shah said the transformation had enabled Uttar Pradesh to set an ambitious target of becoming a USD 1 trillion economy.

"It is precisely because of this transformation that Uttar Pradesh can now set the ambitious goal of becoming a 1-trillion-dollar economy," he said.

Shah contrasted the present situation in Uttar Pradesh with the period when the Samajwadi Party and Bahujan Samaj Party governed the state, and highlighted the emergence of new industrial and manufacturing sectors.

"There was a time when the SP and BSP ruled here. A 'crime industry' was thriving...

Look at the situation today, 10 years later. In place of the illegal pistol industry, a defence corridor has been established; vehicle manufacturing has replaced vehicle theft; and a medical device park is coming up where the chain-snatching 'industry' once existed. This is a massive transformation," Shah said.

He said Uttar Pradesh, which earlier lacked confidence to host an investment summit in Lucknow, had now emerged as a major destination for investors.

"The very UP that once lacked the confidence to host an investment summit in Lucknow has now become a major hub for attracting investment... After the Yogi government took office, the BJP administration completely eradicated the hooliganism that prevailed during the SP-BSP era..." he said.

, in view of the red alert issued by the

Dhami directed officials to maintain heightened vigilance in districts under red and orange alerts, continuously monitor vulnerable areas and ensure that all arrangements for relief and rescue operations are in place in advance in case of any emergency. He also directed that district emergency operation centres remain active and weather warnings be disseminated immediately at the local level.

Disaster management and rehabilitation minister Madan Kaushik also spoke to Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman and took stock of the weather situation and preparedness across the state.

He directed officials to closely monitor the weather and remain fully prepared to deal with any eventuality.

Following the chief ministerâs directions, Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman held a meeting with all 13 districts on Friday and instructed them to remain on alert mode.

According to the weather department forecast, on September 26, red alerts have been issued for five districts, orange alerts for five districts and yellow alerts for three districts.





On September 27, red alerts have been issued for four districts, orange alerts for four districts and yellow alerts for five districts.

On September 26, Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Champawat, Nainital and Udham Singh Nagar are under a red alert, while Dehradun, Pauri Garhwal, Rudraprayag, Chamoli and Almora are under an orange alert. Haridwar, Uttarkashi and Tehri Garhwal are under a yellow alert.

People living near rivers, streams and seasonal water channels should be regularly alerted and prevented from approaching riverbanks or entering fast-flowing waters.

Special monitoring has also been ordered along the Char Dham routes, major tourist destinations and other vulnerable areas to ensure the safety of pilgrims and tourists. All arrangements should be kept ready in advance so that relief and rescue operations can begin with minimum response time in case of an emergency.

World.title: Op Drishti: AFMS conducts 220 eye surgeries in underground OT at shelling-prone zone along LoC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Over 220 sight-restoring surgeries were conducted by Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS) surgeons during the 10th edition of first-of-its-kind mega eye surgical camp, held under Operation Drishti, at an underground operation theatre in a shelling-prone zone at Tangdhar in Kupwara along the Line of Control in J&K on Friday and Saturday.

Most interventions were cataract surgeries, along with selective retinal procedures and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery. Patients from Khawarpora, Tangdar, Tadd, Bagbela, Yangdar and neighbouring hamlets came after screening and a broadcast on Radio Rooh-e-Karnah, with the Indian Army guiding each one from arrival to recovery.

World.title: 5 ways India is kicking car safety into top gear with Bharat NCAP 2.0: What buyers need to know

Current Bharat NCAP phase remains valid until Sept 30, 2027, with proposed introduction of Bharat NCAP 2.0 from Oct 2027

The bottom line

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Bharat NCAP 2.0, planned for October 2027, will look beyond what happens when a car crashes. The proposed system will examine the entire safety chain: from how a vehicle helps avoid a collision to how well it protects occupants, pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and what happens after an accident.Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari announced the proposed timeline at the SIAM Annual Convention in September 2026. The second phase is being planned as the first phase of Bharat New Car Assessment Programme, or Bharat NCAP, approaches the end of its current cycle.According to the ministry of road transport and highwaysâ draft AIS-197 Revision 1, the first phase of Bharat NCAP began on October 1, 2023 and is valid until September 30, 2027. The draft revision has been prepared as the framework for Bharat NCAP 2.0.The proposed changes could make the safety rating a much broader measure of a carâs performance, not just in a crash, but before, during and after one.Bharat NCAP is Indiaâs own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. It was formally launched by the ministry of road transport and highways in August 2023 and became operational from October 1, 2023.The programme applies to type-approved passenger vehicles in the M1 category with a gross vehicle weight of less than 3.5 tonnes. It is voluntary, which means manufacturers can offer eligible vehicles for assessment.The programme is anchored by the Central Institute of Road Transport (CIRT), while testing is carried out through designated agencies with the required infrastructure.At its core, Bharat NCAP gives car buyers a common safety benchmark. A vehicle must already meet mandatory regulatory requirements to be sold in India. Bharat NCAP goes a step further by putting eligible vehicles through specified tests and awarding them a rating of between one and five stars.The idea is fairly simple: instead of looking only at a carâs price, design or features, buyers get an additional reference point to understand how the vehicle performs in standardised safety tests.The government has also positioned the programme as a way to encourage manufacturers to improve vehicle safety and strengthen the safety standards of cars made in India.The existing programme broadly assesses three areas:Vehicles are subjected to prescribed crash tests and other assessments. Their performance across these parameters is then used to arrive at the overall star rating.The current framework includes a 64 kmph offset frontal impact test, a 50 kmph side movable deformable barrier test and a pole side impact test, among other checks prescribed under AIS-197.The assessment therefore goes beyond simply asking whether the passenger compartment remains intact.Adult Occupant Protection examines the risk of injury to adults in different crash conditions and seating positions. Child Occupant Protection looks at the protection offered to younger passengers, including the use and installation of child restraint systems.Safety Assist Technologies, meanwhile, covers technologies designed to help prevent crashes or reduce their severity.A car may offer different levels of protection to adults and children, so Bharat NCAP evaluates the two separately.The adult assessment focuses on occupant protection during prescribed crash scenarios, while the child assessment considers how effectively younger occupants are protected and how child restraint systems work within the vehicle.This also means that a carâs overall star rating is not simply a score from one crash test. It reflects performance across several safety parameters.For consumers, the individual scores can therefore provide more information than looking at the star rating alone.Bharat NCAP is anchored by CIRT, with testing carried out through designated testing agencies that have the required facilities.The wider automotive testing ecosystem includes agencies such as the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT).Manufacturers submit eligible vehicles for assessment under the programme. The existing framework specifies procedures around the variant selected for testing, including provisions concerning the base variant of a model.That distinction matters when reading a Bharat NCAP result. A rating should not automatically be assumed to apply to every variant of a model unless the official assessment covers those variants.Bharat NCAP ratings range from one to five stars. A higher rating indicates stronger performance under the programmeâs prescribed assessment criteria.But a five-star rating is not a guarantee that occupants will escape injury in every real-world crash. NCAP testing is conducted under standardised conditions and is intended to provide a basis for comparing vehicle safety performance.It is also important to distinguish Bharat NCAP from the mandatory certification requirements for selling a vehicle in India.Bharat NCAP is voluntary and is designed to provide consumers with additional information beyond the mandatory regulatory framework. A vehicle being tested or rated under Bharat NCAP should therefore not be confused with regulatory approval.Since its launch, Bharat NCAP has increasingly become part of the safety conversation around new car launches. The ratings have also become a factor in how manufacturers present their vehicles to consumers, particularly as safety becomes a more visible consideration in the passenger-vehicle market.This is where the proposed second phase takes a much wider approach.The draft AIS-197 Revision 1 divides Bharat NCAP 2.0 into five safety verticals:The change is significant because the current system focuses mainly on occupant protection and safety-assist technologies, while the proposed framework looks at the complete safety chain.The draft framework uses a 100-point assessment structure, with Crash Protection accounting for 55% of the assessment. The remaining weightage covers the other safety areas.In other words, the crash itself will still be a major part of the rating, but it will no longer be the only part of the safety story.Bharat NCAP 2.0 proposes expanding the Crash Protection assessment to five mandatory crash tests:Adult and child occupant protection will continue to be assessed separately.The addition of full-width frontal and rear-impact tests means the proposed system will examine crash scenarios beyond the core tests in the existing framework.That gives the second phase a wider testing footprint and allows different types of impacts to form part of the overall safety assessment.One of the biggest differences in Bharat NCAP 2.0 is that the programme is designed to look at what happens before a crash as well.Crash Avoidance is one of the five proposed verticals. It focuses on technologies and vehicle characteristics that can help prevent a collision or reduce its severity.Safe Driving is another proposed category, widening the assessment beyond the vehicleâs passive protection features.Together, these categories shift the focus from simply asking, âHow well does this car perform when it crashes?â to a broader question: âHow does this vehicle contribute to safety across different stages of a road incident?âBharat NCAP 2.0 also proposes a separate Vulnerable Road User Protection category. This brings pedestrians and other vulnerable road users more directly into the safety assessment.Post-Crash Safety is one of the five proposed assessment areas. Minister Gadkari described Bharat NCAP 2.0 as covering the entire safety chain, including post-crash evacuation and care. âWe are going to evaluate the entire crash chain,â Gadkari said, adding that new technologies developed globally as well as by startups would be considered under the programme.This means the assessment is intended to extend beyond the instant of impact and examine safety considerations in the period immediately after a crash.It adds another layer to the programmeâs approach: avoiding the crash where possible, protecting people during the impact, and addressing safety after the collision.For buyers, Bharat NCAP offers an additional way to compare cars beyond mandatory safety requirements.A consumer can look at a vehicleâs overall rating as well as its adult and child protection performance and the safety technologies considered in the assessment.The rating is not meant to replace other factors involved in buying a car. Price, size, fuel efficiency, features, driving requirements and other considerations remain relevant, but the proposed 2.0 framework would expand that information further.Buyers could eventually have a broader picture of how a car performs across crash protection, crash avoidance, safe driving, vulnerable-road-user protection and post-crash safety.Bharat NCAP is one part of a much larger road-safety challenge, focusing on the structure of vehicles. Vehicle design and safety technology can influence the outcome of a crash, but they cannot address every reason why accidents happen.The ministry has identified several factors associated with road crashes, including speeding, mobile-phone use, drunken driving, wrong-side driving, lane indiscipline, jumping red lights and failure to use helmets and seat belts. Vehicle condition, road conditions and weather can also play a role.Government data recorded 1,68,491 road accident fatalities in 2022.Bharat NCAP therefore addresses one part of this wider equation: the safety performance of vehicles. Its proposed second phase would broaden that role by looking at what a vehicle can do to help avoid crashes, how it protects people when a crash occurs, how it protects vulnerable road users and what happens afterwards.The current Bharat NCAP phase remains valid until September 30, 2027. The government has proposed introducing Bharat NCAP 2.0 from October 2027, with the draft AIS-197 Revision 1 serving as the framework for the next phase.The proposed transition would take Indiaâs vehicle safety-rating system from a relatively focused crash and occupant-protection programme to a broader safety assessment.The familiar one-to-five-star rating would remain the consumer-facing language of vehicle safety, but the assessment behind it is set to become much more comprehensive.The bigger shift is in the question Bharat NCAP is trying to answer. Instead of looking only at how a car performs when it is involved in a crash, the proposed system would examine the vehicleâs safety journey from avoiding a collision to protecting occupants and vulnerable road users, and supporting safety after the crash.That could give Indian car buyers a wider set of safety information to consider when choosing their next vehicle.

World.title: Salem Mayor, councillors start indefinite sit-in against Corporation Commissioner
World.content:
Salem Corporation Mayor A. Ramachandran and 20 DMK councillors began their indefinite sit-in against Salem Corporation Commissioner Lalitaditya Neelam on Friday (September 25).

The Mayor alleged that the Corporation Commissioner did not send the resolutions passed in the council meetings to the State government.

Speaking to reporters, Mr. Ramachandran said the decision to privatise the drinking water supply in Salem Corporation should be cancelled. From the British era, it was the Salem Corporation that supplied water to the public, and it should continue. If a private company started supplying water, charges would be increased threefold.

Also, the transfer of land, worth ₹1,000-crore, for free for a waste-to-energy project should be dropped. If the plant was established, waste from five districts would be dumped in Salem, which would pollute land, air and water.

As the Commissioner did not send the resolution passed against this project, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay announced it in the Assembly under the 110 rule, the Mayor added.

He also demanded action against those who entered the council meeting hall during the last meeting. Also, tenders were being given without knowledge of the Mayor and the councillors, he alleged.

“The Commissioner, who is going for inspection in my ward 6, did not inform me. So, departmental action should be taken against the Commissioner. Until our demands are met, we will continue our protest,” the Mayor added.

Since many councillors had gone to the the by-election campaign, all councillors were not present. But all of them, including those from the AIADMK, supported the protest, the Mayor clarified.

Police personnel were deployed to the Salem Corporation office to avoid any untoward incidents.

People coming into the corporation office will be allowed in after checking, sources said.

World.title: Expand scope of ward funds, say councillors
World.content:
Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) councillors sought to expand the scope of works covered under the first phase of the Ward Development Fund, at the council meeting on Friday.

Standing Committee Chairperson C. Velu said the councillors were asked to use the ₹30 lakh allocated for pre-monsoon works such as improving roads, cleaning storm-water drains, purchasing boats, building retaining walls, and installing CCTV cameras.

He asked whether the allocation was additional or would be drawn from the existing funds. If the councillors were restricted to using the fund only for the works listed, they would be unable to attend to other maintenance requirements, he said.

GCC Commissioner G.S. Sameeran said pre-monsoon works were given priority, and that councillors could identify locations that require immediate attention.

Thiru.Vi.Ka Nagar councillor Siva. Raajashekaran said they were unable to undertake even minor works such as welding because of the restrictions on the funds.

Deputy Mayor M. Magesh Kumaar and many councillors demanded that a revised circular be issued on the usage of funds.

Standing Committee (Revenue) Chairperson Sarbajaya Das said zonal officials had told councillors that the funds could be used only for monsoon-related works, and sought a circular clarifying the position.

Mr. Sameeran said the funds could be used for works other than monsoon preparedness and agreed to issue a circular to this effect.

Remarks draw flak

Valasaravakkam Ward Committee Chairperson V. Rajan criticised certain remarks allegedly made by Minister for Public Works Department (PWD) Aadhav Arjuna in the Assembly during the recent Budget session on the functioning of elected representatives and DMK mayors in municipal corporations.

Mr. Rajan said councillors and committee chairpersons were not receiving adequate funds and were not being invited to meetings held by Ministers at Ripon Buildings or to inaugurations across the city.

Mayor R. Priya asked Mr. Rajan to “become an MLA and pose this question in the Assembly”. DMK floor leader R. Ramalingam said the Minister should explain his remarks at a council meeting. The Mayor said she could grant permission for this.

T. Nagar BJP councillor Uma Anandan said officials of the Electricity Board, Metrowater, and the GCC did not cooperate with the councillors, and that the role of councillors was becoming redundant.

Valasaravakkam councillor S. Bharathi sought clarity on the monitoring of storm-water drain connections. Referring to the ongoing work to lay new drains on Arcot Road, she asked whether the underground high-tension cables were being properly shifted or whether drains were being laid over them.

The Mayor said the work had been awarded to Narayana Constructions and that the underground cables were being shifted during excavations. Damaged or severed cables, if any, were being replaced before the work proceeded, she said.

Ms. Bharathi, however, alleged that she had submitted photographs showing lack of progress, and called for an inspection. Mr. Sameeran said the pictures had been taken during construction and that the location had since been revamped, and the high-tension cables relocated.

Four contracts awarded

Tondiarpet Ward Committee chairperson Nethaji U. Ganesan said four contracts had been awarded in the past four months, including works for desilting drains and repairing damaged roads, at 34% and 36% below the estimated amounts.

Mr. Ganesan questioned the quality of such works and alleged that officials were not monitoring them regularly. He added that motor repair works were being delayed.

The Mayor asked the Commissioner to examine whether a cap — with a limit of around 15% — could be fixed on bids below the estimated cost, depending on the nature of the work.

World.title: Chennai Corporation moves to curb pet abandonment with ₹10,000 penalty
World.content:
Starting Friday, the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) will collect a fine of ₹10,000 from pet owners who abandon licensed dogs and cats. It passed a resolution to this effect at the council meeting on Friday.

The fine was reduced from ₹25,000 to ₹10,000 following councillors’ objections.

The GCC will also launch a facility for registering complaints about missing pets. Owners will not be penalised if they registered a complaint and the animals were subsequently rescued by the Corporation. A total of 40 dogs abandoned by their owners were rescued by NGOs in the past few weeks. An official said the penalty was expected to deter residents from abandoning pets.

Scanners will be provided for all 40 vehicles used in dog-catching operations, with 320 dog catchers, to identify the owners of dogs and cats and penalise violators.

The Corporation has also begun collecting a fine of ₹5,000 for unlicensed pets and ₹500 for pets found unleashed. An official said the civic body had collected ₹7 lakh so far.

Over 1 lakh dogs vaccinated

The GCC has administered anti-rabies vaccines and ectoparasiticides to 1,00,378 stray dogs between August 11 and September 25, a press release said. Thirty teams have been deployed since August 11, with each team expected to vaccinate about 100 dogs a day. About 3,000 dogs are vaccinated daily, with 10 teams operating simultaneously in three zones, the release added.

The campaign has so far covered Tiruvottiyur, Manali, Madhavaram, Tondiarpet, Royapuram, Ambattur, Anna Nagar and Alandur zones in 41 days. Drives in Kodambakkam, Thiru.Vi.Ka Nagar and Perungudi will be completed over the next 34 working days, the release said.

World.title: Philanthropist receives Sankara Ratna Award for contribution to eye care
World.content:
Sankara Nethralaya conferred the Sankara Ratna Award 2025 on philanthropist Prasad Reddy Katamreddy, president and CEO, Twisted X Inc., Texas, and a member of the Board of Advisers, Sankara Nethralaya U.SA, at a function here on Friday.

The award was presented by former Vice-President M. Venkaiah Naidu, in recognition of Mr. Katamreddy’s support to Sankara Nethralaya, including a $550,000 contribution towards a Mobile Eye Surgical Unit.

The unit is intended to extend eye-care and surgical services to underserved communities across Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Karnataka.

Mr. Naidu said preventing blindness required sustained efforts from both the government and the private sector. He stressed the need to take eye-care services closer to rural communities through mobile facilities.

He also urged greater awareness of posthumous eye donation and support for institutions working to address corneal blindness.

Mr. Katamreddy also reaffirmed his and his wife Shobha Reddy’s commitment to philanthropy and supporting communities in need.

The Sankara Ratna Award was instituted in 2002, the silver jubilee year of Sankara Nethralaya.

World.title: 1,671 km of stormwater drains being desilted: Chennai Mayor
World.content:
Greater Chennai Corporation Mayor R. Priya told the council that desilting of 1,671 km of stormwater drains was under way at an estimated cost of ₹22.46 crore, in response to a question from MDMK councillor P. Subramani (Ward 139) on monsoon preparedness.

She said ₹10 crore had been allocated at ₹5 lakh per ward for monsoon precautionary works. Another ₹22 crore had been earmarked for patching and resurfacing damaged roads, while ₹26.53 crore had been proposed for hiring 150 100-horsepower pumps and 500 tractor-mounted pumps for low-lying areas.

The Mayor said ₹4.65 crore had been allocated to engage temporary personnel to operate pumps and water tanks. A drone survey costing ₹15 lakh was also being undertaken to verify desilting works and ensure that removed silt and garbage were cleared.

She added that mosquito-control workers had been deployed, adequate quantities of larvicides stocked and fogging carried out in vulnerable areas. Pamphlets on disease prevention during the rainy season would also be distributed, with health inspectors tasked with creating awareness.

World.title: Rani Channamma University officials held over fraud allegations
World.content:
The Belagavi police have arrested three officials of Rani Channamma University in connection with an alleged financial misappropriation of more than ₹32 lakh, involving employees’ Provident Fund (PF) and National Pension System (NPS) contributions.

Assistant Registrar H.M. Murigesh, First Division Assistant Sandeep Burli, and Mahesh Viresh Wali have been arrested. Investigators are looking for another accused, Ramu Hanchinal, who is absconding. This follows a complaint filed by RCU officials after an internal inquiry.

According to the complaint, PF amounts deducted from the salaries of employees appointed under the consolidated-pay system were allegedly not deposited into their respective accounts. Instead, the accused allegedly diverted funds to their personal bank and NPS accounts.

Under the arrangement, 10% of the employees’ salaries were deducted as their contribution, while the university was required to make an equal 10% contribution. The complaint alleges that amounts exceeding the prescribed contribution were diverted to accounts linked to the accused.

The complaint has also alleged irregularities in transactions involving various allowances and income-tax payments, resulting in financial losses to both the university and its employees.

The complaint was filed at the police station in Kakati on September 8. Officers began investigating the alleged irregularities. The three arrested officials were reportedly apprehended from the Varur area near Hubballi and produced before a court. The court has remanded them in 14 days of judicial custody.

Police Commissioner Prakash Nikam told reporters that investigators had accumulated enough evidence against the accused to apprehend them. The investigation is continuing, with officials examining financial records, documents and transactions to establish the extent of the alleged misappropriation.

Police sources said that the accused Ramu Hanchinal is currently employed at Bagalkot University. Efforts are under way to trace and apprehend him.

World.title: Railways to run 102 festival special trips via Solapur division
World.content:
The Central Railway’s Solapur Division will operate 102 festival special train trips, including 64 services between Kolhapur and Kalaburagi, to meet the additional passenger rush during the Dasara and Deepavali festive season.

The special services will be operated between Mumbai and Chennai, Mumbai and Latur, and Kolhapur and Kalaburagi between October 10 and November 24, according to a revised press release issued by the Solapur Division on Friday.

On the Kolhapur-Kalaburagi route, 64 special trips will be operated daily except on Fridays from October 10 to November 15. Train No. 01451 will leave Kolhapur at 6.10 a.m. and reach Kalaburagi at 4.10 p.m. the same day. The return train, No. 01452, will leave Kalaburagi at 6.10 p.m. and reach Kolhapur at 5.40 a.m. the next day.

The train will stop at Hatkanangale, Jayasingpur, Miraj Junction, Arag, Belanki, Sulgare, Kavathe Mahankal, Langarpeth, Dhalgaon, Mhasoba Dongargaon, Javale, Wasud, Sangola, Pandharpur, Modnimb, Kurduwadi Junction, Solapur and Kalaburagi Junction.

The Kolhapur-Kalaburagi special will comprise four AC III-tier, six Sleeper Class, six General Second Class and two luggage-cum-brake vans, totalling 18 ICF coaches.

On the CSMT Mumbai-Chennai Beach route, 12 weekly special trips will be operated. Train No. 01015 will leave CSMT Mumbai at 12.35 a.m. every Wednesday from October 14 to November 18 and reach Chennai Beach at 11.30 p.m. the same day. The return train, No. 01016, will leave Chennai Beach at 4 a.m. every Thursday from October 15 to November 19 and reach CSMT Mumbai at 4 a.m. the following day.

These trains will halt at Dadar, Thane, Kalyan, Lonavala, Pune, Daund, Kurduwadi, Solapur, Kalaburagi, Wadi, Krishna, Raichur, Mantralayam Road, Adoni, Guntakal, Gooty, Tadipatri, Yerraguntla, Cuddapah, Razampeta, Renigunta, Arakkonam and Perambur. They will have 22 LHB coaches, including two AC II-tier, two AC III-tier and two luggage-cum-generator-cum-brake vans.

Another 26 special trips will be operated between CSMT Mumbai and Latur every Tuesday and Thursday from October 13 to November 24. Train No. 01105 will leave CSMT Mumbai at 12.35 a.m. and reach Latur at 11.40 a.m. the same day. Train No. 01106 will leave Latur at 4.30 p.m. and reach CSMT Mumbai at 4.10 a.m. the next day.

These trains will halt at Dadar, Thane, Kalyan, Lonavala, Pune, Uruli, Daund, Bhigwan, Jeur, Kurduwadi, Barshi Town, Dharashiv and Harangul. The service will comprise four AC III-tier, 11 Sleeper Class, five General Second Class and two luggage-cum-brake vans, totalling 22 ICF coaches.

Reservations for the festival special trains, which will run on special charges, will open on September 27 at all computerised reservation centres and through the IRCTC website and RailOne app.

Passengers have been advised to travel with valid tickets and make use of the additional services during the festive season. Detailed timings at intermediate stations can be checked through the Indian Railways enquiry system, RailOne app and NTES app.

World.title: Tambaram police seize 12 kg of ganja, arrest five in special drive
World.content:
Tambaram City Police seized 12 kg of ganja and arrested five persons in separate operations conducted as part of a special drive against narcotic drugs on Friday.

Selaiyur police arrested Manikantan, 28, of Palayamkottai in Tirunelveli district, and Adarsh, 24, of Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, near the MCC flyover at East Tambaram railway station. Police seized 5.3 kg of ganja and a mobile phone from them.

In a separate operation, the Guduvanchery Prohibition Enforcement Wing (PEW) team arrested Manabhanjan Padhi, 47, of Ganjam district in Odisha, at Kamarajapuram Lake Bund. A total of ₹5 kg of ganja, ₹1 lakh in cash, a mobile phone and a scooter were seized from him.

The Pallikaranai PEW team arrested Shaik Ali, 20, of West Godavari district in Andhra Pradesh, near the East Tambaram railway grounds and seized 1.25 kg of ganja and a mobile phone. Tambaram police arrested Shanjai, 20, of Thiruneermalai, Kadapperi, at Kuppamedu on Kiskintha Road and seized 450 grams of ganja.

Cases were registered against the accused under various provisions of the NDPS Act.

World.title: Any attempt to divert Pakistan’s water to be treated as act of war, India ‘must make no mistake about it’: PM at UNGA
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday said that any attempt by India to divert Pakistan’s share of water would be treated as an “act of war”.

“Any attempt to stop, impede or divert Pakistan’s share of the waters will be treated as an act of war. India must make no mistake about it,” he said during a speech at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, where he called attention to the neighbouring country’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance.

In his address, the prime minister highlighted India’s abeyance of the IWT since last year, stressing that it had no legal basis.

He highlighted that the country’s claims and actions regarding the treaty had been rejected by UN experts as well as by the Permanent Court of Arbitration, leaving Pakistan “vindicated beyond any ray of doubt” in its position.

“Water must never be weaponised. Rivers should nourish nations, not divide them,” he stressed, calling the Indus river system the “lifeblood” of the entire region.

PM Shehbaz also addressed last year’s brief military conflict with India, which followed a terror attack in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam that New Delhi blamed on Islamabad without any evidence.

“Our brave and valiant armed forces, under the courageous leadership of Field Marshal Asim Munir, responded with precision and professionalism,” he said.

He once again praised US President Donald Trump’s “resolute and visionary leadership” in brokering a ceasefire between the two countries in May 2025, stressing that it saved “hundreds of millions of lives”.

“Who knows the extent of devastation that could have taken place had President Trump not stepped in at this critical moment with clarity of thought and action?” he questioned.

“We must therefore ensure that South Asia never reaches this precipice ever again,” he said. This, however, the premier added, required a fair resolution of the Kashmir dispute.

“For eight decades, the Kashmiri people have waited for the United Nations to fulfill its solemn commitment of a free and impartial plebiscite,” he pointed out, adding that they had endured “illegal occupation, arbitrary detention, extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, sexual violence and collective punishment” for generations.

He declared that Pakistan would continue to extend its full diplomatic, political and moral support to Kashmiris until they were granted their right to self-determination, terming Kashmir “Pakistan’s jugular vein”.

Pakistan’s peace efforts

During his address, the prime minister also addressed the conflict in the Gulf region and wider Middle East, highlighting the loss of lives, economic suffering and pressure faced by critical maritime routes, particularly the Strait of Hormuz.

“At this critical moment, Pakistan chose to act swiftly. Through concerted efforts, Pakistan brought Washington and Tehran under one roof in Islamabad,” PM Shehbaz said, referring to the Islamabad Talks that resulted in the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding by the United States and Iran in June.

In this regard, he appreciated Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, whose “relentless efforts helped create space for diplomacy under exceptionally difficult and challenging circumstances”. He also extended his appreciation to Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar for his role in the process.

“Amid the roar of missiles, drones and guns, the voice for diplomacy must echo even louder and stronger,” the premier stated.

“The Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab are arteries of the global economy. They must remain open, connecting nations, not becoming choke points of confrontation.”

He also condemned, “in the strongest possible terms”, the recent attacks by the Houthis against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, calling them “deplorable”. He expressed Pakistan’s complete solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

He also highlighted the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed by Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia as a reflection of Pakistan’s commitment to peace.

“This alliance is not directed against any country; it is a collective commitment for defence, stability and peace in the region, and nothing more,” he stressed.

PM Shehbaz also restated Pakistan’s support for Palestine, expressing his concern for ongoing Israeli violence in Gaza and the West Bank as well as its continued aggression against Lebanon and Syria. In particular, he noted that the forcible eviction of Palestinians in the West Bank “clearly reflects Israel’s genocidal agenda”.

“Pakistan believes that the only just and lasting solution is the creation of an independent, sovereign, viable and contiguous State of Palestine, based on pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital,” he reaffirmed.

The premier also termed terrorism a grave threat to international peace and security, emphasising that Pakistan had sacrificed “almost 100,000 precious lives” and suffered economic losses of over $150 billion in combating terrorism.

He added that Afghan territory continued to be exploited by the TTP and the BLA. These foreign-funded groups operated from sanctuaries in Afghanistan intending to destabilise Pakistan, he said.

He called on Afghan authorities to halt all such attacks, fulfill their international commitments and take “verifiable, decisive action to ensure that Afghan soil is never again used against Pakistan or any other country”.

The premier briefly touched on the rise of Islamophobia in his speech, specifically calling attention to “RSS-driven Hinddutva ideology” that he said was fanning religious hatred. He stressed that this hatred must have “no place in this world”.

He also praised UN peacekeeping as “one of the strongest expressions” of collective security, noting Pakistani men and women’s role in protecting civilians and helping countries emerge from conflict.

On the topic of Pakistan’s economic revival, he said that the government had restored macroeconomic stability and was moving towards sustainable and inclusive growth. He highlighted Pakistan’s close relations with China, including the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), and paid tribute to Chinese President Xi Jinping for spearheading initiatives for global development, security, civilisation and governance.

PM Shehbaz additionally called on developed countries to honour their climate-finance commitments and ensure support for adaptation and resilience, stressing that Pakistan repeatedly bore consequences for climate change despite contributing less than one per cent of global emissions.

“The theme of this session calls upon us to restore trust,” he said. “But trust cannot be restored by words alone. It must be earned through action.”

He called for the UN to become stronger and more effective, stressing that reform must reflect “the interests and aspirations of the overwhelming majority of member states, not the ambitions of a select few”.

“We have chosen dialogue over confrontation. We have chosen cooperation over coercion. We have chosen peace over war,” the premier said in his concluding remarks. “Let this 81st General Assembly make it a unanimous choice.”

World.title: Petrol price raised by Rs2.02 per litre, high-speed diesel rate reduced by Rs3.59
World.content:
The government on Friday increased the price of petrol by Rs2.02 per litre, but reduced that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.59 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs391.30 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs408.53 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable from Sept 26 (Saturday) to Sept 28 (Monday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Pakistani, Saudi, Turkish military chiefs meet to discuss ways to assist Riyadh under Makkah defence pact
World.content:
Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan held military chiefs of staff talks on Friday with the objective to explore ways to assist Riyadh under the Makkah Defence Alliance.

The Turkish defence ministry published photographs of the three military officials in uniform, stating that the meeting had taken place, without disclosing where.

However, Turkiye’s Defence Ministry earlier said its Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu would travel to Saudi Arabia for the meeting.

The meeting took place against the backdrop of the kingdom being dragged into fresh fighting between the Houthis and the Yemeni government, with the former declaring a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and targeting its ships in the Red Sea. In recent weeks, Houthis have also carried out attacks in Saudi Arabia.

Earlier, the Foreign Office (FO) in Islamabad had shared that the three countries were mulling a military chiefs’ meeting to consider ways to assist Riyadh under the Makkah pact.

The FO statement came after Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held a discussion on the defence pact with Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan bin Abdullah and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

In the statement, the FO noted that the tripartite agreement, signed on Aug 7, stipulated that an attack against any one of its parties should be considered an attack against all parties.
