World.title: DPWH projects flagged by Gatchalian in 2027 proposed budget
World.content:
Senator Win Gatchalian spots projects without station limits or bridge IDs, duplicated projects, and projects without coordinates in the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of Public Works and Highways

MANILA, Philippines – Senator Win Gatchalian flagged 7,107 projects worth P251.81 billion in the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).

Among the red flags Gatchalian raised during the Senate budget hearing on Friday, September 25, were:

Projects without station limits or bridge IDs: P83.67 billion for 2,570 projects

Duplicated projects: P3.94 billion for 189 projects

Projects reappearing from the 2026 General Appropriations Act in the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP): P20.79 billion for 258 projects

Projects without coordinates: P83.50 billion for 3,543 projects

Lump-sum projects: P14.79 billion for 56 projects

Overlapping or fragmented projects: P63.19 billion for 533 projects

Unspecified work scope: P1.52 billion for 62 projects

Conflicting types of work: P386.25 million for 20 projects

Given the sheer volume of projects handled by the agency, DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon said they presume regularity in the proposals submitted by regional and district offices.

Dizon said the DPWH would review the projects flagged by Gatchalian. He also pointed out that the projects included in the NEP came with a certificate of implementability.

The document, signed by a district engineer, certifies that a proposed project has no duplicate, has not received previous funding, and does not overlap with another project.

If the review finds problems with the flagged projects, Dizon said the DPWH would file cases against the concerned district engineers.

At the same time, Dizon acknowledged that some of the projects flagged by Gatchalian could be explained.

Gatchalian also flagged multi-billion-peso projects in the 2026 budget proposal.

In 2025, it was revealed that DPWH officials had connived with contractors and lawmakers to corrupt public funds. – Rappler.com

World.title: Eldrew Yulo continues to prove boundless potential with Asian Games bronze
World.content:
SWING. Eldrew Yulo in action for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games.

After his older brother Carlos captured back-to-back golds in floor exercise and vault, Eldrew Yulo also shines in his first Asian Games stint as he bags the bronze in horizontal bar

MANILA, Philippines – Winning is a family affair for Eldrew and Carlos Yulo.

After his older brother Carlos captured back-to-back artistic gymnastics golds in floor exercise and vault, Eldrew also shone in the 2026 Asian Games as he bagged the bronze in horizontal bar at the Nagoya General Gymnasium in Japan on Friday, September 25.

The younger Yulo completed the podium after a tiebreaker with Kazakhstan’s Milad Karimi, scoring 13.666 points to conclude his first Asian Games stint in style.

EMOTIONS. The Philippines’ Karl Jahrel Eldrew Yulo bursts into tears after winning the bronze medal in the men’s horizontal bar in the artistic gymnastics competition of the 2026 Asian Games.

Yulo and Karimi posted similar scores, but the Filipino clinched the bronze with a higher execution of 8.566 against the 7.766 of the veteran Kazakh, who is a former Asian champion in the apparatus.

Tian Hao won convincingly with 14.7 points as he secured another gold medal for China, which dominated the competition and ruled five of the eight events in men’s artistic gymnastics.

Japan’s Shinnosuke Oka settled for silver anew with 14.033 points — the gold once again eluding him following runner-up finishes in the team, individual all-around, and parallel bars.

The Asian Games medal is yet another testament to the boundless potential of Yulo, who just turned 18 in January and is competing in his first year as a senior gymnast.

And his rookie year has been fruitful.

Yulo won gold and bronze medals in floor exercise and a bronze in horizontal bar in the FIG World Cup Series as well as a floor exercise bronze in the Asian Artistic Gymnastics Championships in China in June.

If the Asian Games is any indication, Yulo is just getting started. – Rappler.com

World.title: Mary Jane Veloso finally free after 16 years
World.content:
IN TEARS. Former overseas Filipino worker Mary Jane Veloso cries as she shows to the media the absolute pardon order, during a press conference at the Correctional Institution for Women in Mandaluyong City on September 25, 2026.

Veloso, who was sentenced to death in Indonesia in 2010 for drug trafficking, is given absolute pardon by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

MANILA, Philippines – After more than a decade in detention, Mary Jane Veloso, the woman who suffered in jail after she was allegedly tricked by recruiters into becoming a drug mule, is finally walking free.

The former overseas Filipino worker and human trafficking victim was released from the Correctional Institution for Women (CIW) in Mandaluyong City on Friday night, September 25.

This comes a day after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. granted her absolute pardon on Thursday, September 24.

Bureau of Corrections Director General Gregorio Catapang Jr. handed Mary Jane Veloso a copy of the President’s absolute pardon and presented her official release order from the CIW on Friday night.

Play Video

In a statement, the bureau said Veloso will be endorsed to the local government unit of her residence in Nueva Ecija “as part of the government’s reintegration,” which includes “access [to] programs and services designed to support her transition back into the community.”

“This only proves that there are really second chances, and we are happy that Veloso can now enjoy her newfound freedom with her family,” Catapang said.

Veloso, who was sentenced to death in Indonesia in 2010 for drug trafficking, was given an absolute pardon by the President. This extinguished her criminal liability.

In 2010, Veloso was supposed to fly to Malaysia to work as an overseas Filipino worker, but was instead rerouted to Yogyakarta, Indonesia, where her recruiters gave her a new suitcase.

Indonesian authorities found that the bag contained a stash of heroin, which Veloso claimed she unknowingly brought with her. Even after she was sentenced to death due to drug trafficking, Veloso and her lawyers from the National Union of People’s Lawyers maintained that she was innocent and was only allegedly tricked by her recruiters into being their drug mule.

Veloso was scheduled for execution in 2015, but then-president Benigno Aquino III broke protocol at the last minute and called then-Indonesian foreign minister Retno Marsudi to turn Veloso into a state witness. (LOOK BACK: Aquino, Del Rosario, and the phone call that saved Mary Jane Veloso’s life)

In 2024, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto entered into an agreement with the Philippine government to transfer Veloso to the country. Indonesia also gave Marcos the discretion to grant Veloso clemency.

She arrived in the Philippines in December 2024 and had been detained at CIW since then.

Veloso’s recruiter Cristina Sergio and accomplice Julius Lacanilao are currently detained after they were found guilty of illegal recruitment in 2020. In June, Veloso took the witness stand and personally testified in the human trafficking and illegal recruitment case against her recruiters. – Rappler.com

World.title: Gilas Women fall short of Asian Games 3×3 gold vs hot-shooting Japan
World.content:
SQUAD. Gilas Women in action in the women's 3x3 basketball competition in the 2026 Asian Games.

Kacey dela Rosa puts Gilas Women on her back, but Japan proves too much to handle, pulling away for the convincing win behind its hot shooting to deal the Philippines its only loss in the Asian Games

MANILA, Philippines – Gilas Women fell short of the Philippines’ third gold medal in the 2026 Asian Games after a stinging 21-11 loss to host Japan in the women’s 3×3 basketball final at the Kinjo Futo Station Square Venue in Nagoya on Friday, September 25.

Kacey dela Rosa put the the Filipinas on her back with 6 points, 3 rebounds, and 3 blocks, but the Japanese proved too much to handle, pulling away for the convincing win behind their hot shooting from beyond the arc.

Yuki Hirashita and Sakura Horiuchi fired 9 and 8 points, respectively, and each sank three two-pointers — the two taking turns in torching the Philippines.

Dela Rosa kept Gilas Women within striking distance with a bucket that cut their deficit to 8-12 before Japan closed out the win on a 9-3 run with 30 seconds to spare.

Hirashita scattered 5 points during that stretch, including the two-pointer that sealed the victory for Japan.

Amyah Espano put up 3 points and 3 rebounds in the silver finish, Kennan Ka added 2 points and 4 rebounds, while Maria Pasilang contributed 4 rebounds.

Despite the heartbreaking ending as they absorbed their only loss in the tournament, Gilas Women delivered the Philippines its first-ever 3×3 basketball medal in the Asian Games.

Meanwhile, Gilas Men missed out on the bronze after a 21-10 defeat to Iran.

Doy Dungo churned out 4 points, Luis Pablo tallied 3 points and 2 rebounds, Nic Cabañero had 2 points and 1 rebound, while Koji Buenaflor chimed in 1 point for the Philippines.

It was a disappointing result for Gilas Men after they won their first four games only to drop their last two matches, losing to South Korea in the semifinals and then to Iran. – Rappler.com

World.title: Marcos suspends excise taxes on LPG, kerosene anew
World.content:
The tax relief does not extend to gasoline and diesel, as Finance Secretary Frederick Go says this would 'not be progressive' because higher-income consumers who use more of the two fuels would capture more of the benefit

MANILA, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered the full suspension of excise taxes on liquid petroleum gas (LPG) and kerosene as high global oil prices continue to hit the wallets of Filipino consumers; the relief, however, does not extend to gasoline or diesel.

Marcos issued Executive Order No. 125 on Friday, September 25, following a recommendation from the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC). The order will take effect immediately upon publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation.

The suspension covers LPG, except when used as a raw material for petrochemical production or for motive power, and kerosene, except when used as aviation fuel. Gasoline and diesel, which have seen successive sharp price increases in recent weeks, were not included in the tax break.

The relief can last a maximum of three months, but may end earlier if the one-month average price of Dubai crude falls below the $80-per-barrel level.

The move came after the Department of Energy (DOE) certified that one-month average Dubai crude price had reached $99.41 per barrel, well above the $80-per-barrel threshold required for the government to suspend fuel excise taxes. The DBCC subsequently recommended full suspension.

The DBCC and DOE are also required to review the measure every month and may recommend whether the suspension should continue, be modified, or ended.

Finance Secretary Frederick Go earlier told senators that suspending excise taxes on gasoline and diesel would “not be progressive,” given that wealthier consumers use more of the two fuels and would capture a larger share of the benefit. The government could also lose about P12 billion in tax revenues each month if the break was extended to gasoline and diesel.

The government previously suspended excise taxes on LPG and kerosene for three months beginning in April after Dubai crude similarly breached the trigger threshold. Gasoline and diesel were also excluded from that earlier round.

The Department of Finance previously estimated that suspending excise taxes for LPG and kerosene for the maximum three-month period would cost the government around P4.1 billion in foregone revenues. – Rappler.com

World.title: Kazakhstan Continues to Investigate Mangystau Military Tragedy, Five Officials Detained
World.content:
ASTANA – Five military officials have been detained as part of a pretrial investigation into the deaths of service members during a military exercise in the Mangystau Region, Deputy Interior Minister Sanzhar Adilov said at a Sept. 25 government commission meeting in Aktau.

The meeting reviewed the progress of the investigation and measures to support the families of the deceased service members and those affected by the tragedy. Adilov said the Military Investigative Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs is conducting a pretrial investigation into the deaths.

“Five officials have been detained and placed in the temporary detention facility in Aktau: the chief of staff and first deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Naval Forces of the Armed Forces, two commanders of military units, the commander of a marine infantry company and the commander of the boat,” Adilov said.

He added that investigative and procedural measures are continuing, including the necessary examinations. Investigators will provide a legal assessment of the actions of all persons involved and establish the full circle of suspects.

Aid to families to be distributed transparently

Chair of the government commission Kanat Bozumbayev said the state would fully meet its obligations to support the families of the deceased service members. Legally guaranteed payments will be made without delays, while responsible specialists will be assigned to each family to provide ongoing individual support.

The commission also thanked members of the Kazakhstan Khalyk Kenesi, Kurultai deputies, political parties, entrepreneurs, and other citizens for their support. Funds raised through a special fund have reached the required level, and the fundraising campaign has been closed.

A special commission headed by Bekmurat Zhusipov, a member of the Kazakhstan Khalyk Kenesi and chair of the Mangystau Regional Public Council, has been established to ensure transparent and targeted distribution of the funds among the families and the affected service members. Law enforcement and state bodies have been instructed to ensure strict oversight of the use of the funds.

Defense Ministry pledges accountability

Defense Minister Lieutenant General of Aviation Dauren Kosanov expressed condolences to the families of the deceased service members and said those responsible would face punishment under the law.

“We remain in constant contact with the families of the deceased and provide them with all necessary assistance and support,” he said.

The government commission continues to oversee both the investigation and assistance to the affected families. All circumstances and causes of the incident are being established, with those responsible to be held accountable in accordance with the law.

World.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Raise Oil Refining Capacity to Nearly 30 Million Tonnes by 2031
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan plans to increase the combined capacity of its three existing oil refineries from 17.5 million to 28.8 million tonnes per year as the government moves to meet growing domestic demand for petroleum products and considers construction of a fourth refinery.

The plans were discussed at a Sept. 23 government meeting chaired by Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov on the implementation of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s instructions to modernize existing refineries and assess the construction of a fourth facility.

Existing refineries to undergo expansion

KazMunayGas Chairman Askhat Khasenov reported on the status and timelines of refinery expansion projects. According to him, the capacity of the Shymkent Refinery is planned to double from 6 million to 12 million tonnes of oil per year by 2030, while the Pavlodar Petrochemical Plant is expected to increase capacity from 6 million to 9 million tonnes by 2031.

At the Atyrau Refinery, an efficiency improvement project is scheduled for completion in 2027, increasing capacity from 5.5 million to 6.1 million tonnes annually.

The Shymkent refinery expansion will also require upgrades to oil transportation infrastructure, including increasing the capacity of the Kenkiyak–Atyrau and Kenkiyak–Kumkol main oil pipelines and the Tekesu station. A Shymkent–Almaty petroleum products pipeline with capacity of up to 3.5 million tonnes per year is also planned.

Fourth refinery under consideration

Deputy Energy Minister Kairkhan Tutkyshbayev reported on work to assess the construction of a fourth refinery. According to the Energy Ministry, Kazakhstan’s long-term demand for oil refining capacity could reach around 40 million tonnes per year.

Bektenov instructed the government to complete a comprehensive assessment and make final decisions on the fourth refinery by the end of this year. The assessment is expected to determine the facility’s optimal capacity, configuration, feedstock base, location and economic model.

Officials were also instructed to closely monitor the expansion projects, prevent delays and ensure the timely commissioning of new facilities, with further attention to increasing the depth of oil processing.

Government links refining investment to fuel prices

Bektenov said the expansion of refining capacity is closely linked to the economic conditions of the domestic fuel market.

“Increasing oil refining capacity is directly linked to the attractiveness of fuel prices on the domestic market. In the current situation, when gasoline and diesel prices in Kazakhstan are twice as low as in neighboring countries, investments in oil refining are economically unfeasible. Therefore, we need to actively continue market liberalization. This is a matter of economic security,” Bektenov said.

The government said the refinery expansion projects are intended to strengthen Kazakhstan’s ability to meet domestic demand for petroleum products over the medium and long term.

World.title: Kazakhstan, China Advance $440 Million Robotics Localization Project
World.content:
ALMATY – Kazakhstan and Chinese robotics manufacturer UBTech Robotics are advancing a $440 million project to localize robotics production in Kazakhstan, with plans covering manufacturing, research and development, programming and the creation of new jobs.

The project was announced on the sidelines of the Kazakhstan–China Investment Forum, which opened Sept. 25 at Koktobe Hall in Almaty and brought together more than 600 delegates, including representatives of Chinese corporations, Kazakh businesses, government bodies and development institutions.

According to Yerlan Nabiyev, Nero Group CEO, the cooperation with UBTech Robotics began after an initial meeting in November last year, held on the recommendation of Almaty’s city administration.

UBTech Robotics, a Chinese technology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Shenzhen, specializes in humanoid and educational robotics. Nabiyev said a subsequent agreement on cooperation was signed during a Kazakhstan–China forum in July in the presence of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.

“We have already started implementing the project to localize robotics production here in Kazakhstan on the territory of a special economic zone,” Nabiyev told The Astana Times.

Project to cover production, R&D and programming

The initial investment is estimated at nearly $440 million. According to Nabiyev, the project is designed to go beyond assembling finished products and will include research and development, research activities, programming and manufacturing facilities.

“This is an initial stage, which primarily involves localization not only of the production component. It is also R&D, research, programming, substantial job creation and, of course, production facilities,” he said.

Nabiyev said the project is intended to develop practical applications for robotics across different sectors rather than focus primarily on entertainment.

“Our goal is for robots not to replace people. Our goal is for robots to be assistants to people,” he said.

“We are now primarily focused not on entertainment content involving robots, but on their application first of all in education and services, of which there are many, practically in all sectors, in manufacturing — robots in logistics, robots for production purposes and so on,” Nabiyev added.

Robotics to expand educational opportunities

Nabiyev also highlighted the social dimension of the project, including the development of educational robotics in Kazakhstan. According to him, Nero Group currently employs more than 200 people and has expertise in electronics manufacturing, circuit boards and specialized technologies. The company expects its workforce to grow substantially as the robotics business expands.

He added that the company is preparing to include robotics in Kazakhstan’s national register of domestic manufacturers, with the relevant technological operations and share of local content to be reflected in the registration.

Nabiyev also said educational robotics production is expected to begin in October, with an initial target of supplying nearly 30 schools in Almaty by the end of the year.

Kazakhstan–China investment ties expand

The robotics project is part of broader efforts to deepen investment cooperation between Kazakhstan and China. The Kazakhstan–China Investment Forum, organized by Kazakh Invest with the support of the Investment Committee of the Foreign Ministry, is bringing together more than 300 companies, according to Kazakh Invest Chairman Sultangali Kinzhaкulov.

“Today we are reaching a level of high-quality investment cooperation: leading investors are coming to the country, building plants, establishing production and manufacturing products with high added value,” Kinzhaкulov told The Astana Times.

He noted that the forum is being held in this format for the first time and brings together investors that are operating in Kazakhstan or planning to enter the market. Nearly 50 commercial documents are expected to be exchanged during the forum, alongside an exhibition and B2B matchmaking meetings.

The Kazakhstan-China Investment Forum was attended by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, who opened the event and outlined key priorities for expanding investment and economic cooperation between the two countries.

World.title: Tokayev Calls for New Investment Model as Kazakhstan, China Deepen Economic Partnership
World.content:
ALMATY – Kazakhstan and China should move from individual investment projects toward integrated production ecosystems, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said Sept. 25 at the Kazakhstan-China Investment Forum in Almaty, outlining transport, industry, critical minerals, digitalization and agriculture as key areas for deeper cooperation.

More than 600 delegates, including Chinese corporations, Kazakh businesses, government bodies and development institutions, took part in the forum. Participants also observed a minute of silence in memory of the service members who died in the Mangystau Region.

Opening the forum, Tokayev said that Chinese investment in Kazakhstan has exceeded $29 billion, while more than 9,000 enterprises with Chinese participation operate in the country. The two governments are working to increase bilateral trade to $100 billion.

“China is the main trading partner of Kazakhstan. Following the results of last year, trade turnover approached a record level of $50 billion,” Tokayev said.

He noted that the ratification of the agreement on the promotion and mutual protection of investments had strengthened the legal foundation for cooperation, while the visa-free regime was helping expand business ties.

“Under conditions of profound transformation of the global economy, Kazakhstan and China are capable of offering a modern and effective model of constructive cooperation based on mutual trust, openness and common long-term interests,” Tokayev said.

Middle Corridor remains a strategic priority

Transport and logistics featured prominently in Tokayev’s address as Kazakhstan seeks to strengthen its role between Chinese and European markets.

“Together with international partners, we are increasing railway capacity, expanding highways and seaports, developing cargo aviation and border infrastructure. From Lianyungang to Aktau, a network of logistics hubs has been formed, connecting the Chinese coast with the Caspian Sea,” he said.

“A new important link in the logistics network will be the Kazakh-Chinese terminal in Chengdu, where the General Consulate of Kazakhstan is planned to open. We consider the development of the Middle Corridor, which is forming a modern configuration of transport links between Asia and Europe, a priority task,” Tokayev added.

Wang Haiyan, deputy director of the Institute of Russian and Eurasian Studies and director of the Center for Kazakhstan Studies at East China Normal University, said transport and logistics remain among the areas of greatest interest to Chinese investors.

“More than half of overland transportation between China and Europe passes through Kazakhstan,” Wang said in an interview with The Astana Times, highlighting that the third cross-border railway and infrastructure supporting the Middle Corridor could further strengthen Kazakhstan’s position as a logistics hub.

From individual projects to production ecosystems

Tokayev said industrial cooperation already includes a portfolio of 260 major joint projects worth more than $62 billion.

“Together with Chinese enterprises, an automotive cluster is developing in Almaty, silicon production is being created in the Karagandy Region, and projects are being implemented in metallurgy, petrochemicals and energy-storage systems,” he said.

He also highlighted projects by Lihua, Fufeng and Dalian Hesheng Holdings involving cotton-textile production and the deep processing of corn and grain.

“This is a good foundation for moving our partnership to a new level – from implementing individual investment projects to forming full-fledged production ecosystems with joint access to the markets of Central Asian countries, the Eurasian Economic Union, the South Caucasus and Europe,” Tokayev said.

He proposed launching the Kazakh-Chinese program “Common History Destiny. Designed and Made in Both China and Kazakhstan,” with the government tasked with forming a pool of promising projects together with Chinese partners.

Wang said the shift reflects growing Chinese interest in moving beyond raw-material acquisition toward processing and deeper industrial value chains.

Critical minerals and digitalization open new opportunities

Tokayev identified the mining and metallurgical complex as another priority, noting Kazakhstan’s reserves of uranium, copper, gold, coal, critical minerals and rare-earth metals. Tokayev also highlighted digitalization, smart cities and satellite technologies.

“Kazakhstan is open to cooperation with all leading technological centers of the world,” he said.

Wang identified digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence as emerging areas for investment, including smart cities, intelligent transport, 5G and 6G infrastructure and digital logistics. She also pointed to renewable energy and water-saving agricultural technologies as areas with further potential.

Forum proposed as annual investment dialogue

Tokayev said the forum should become a permanent platform for direct interaction between the two countries’ business communities.

“I propose holding it annually in September under the name Almaty Investment Dialogue Kazakhstan–China,” he said.

Around 300 companies are participating in the forum, including investors already operating in Kazakhstan and those planning to enter the market.

The forum underscores Kazakhstan’s effort to turn its growing economic ties with China into deeper industrial, technological and logistics cooperation, with joint production and access to wider Eurasian markets becoming an increasingly important focus.

Ten agreements signed during the forum

In the presence of Tokayev, representatives exchanged 10 signed agreements covering industrial production, renewable energy, investment financing, automotive manufacturing and urban development.

Among them are agreements on an electrolytic aluminum plant and an accompanying wind power facility in the Abai Region, a 450-megawatt portfolio of wind power projects in the Akmola Region, and the joint development of an energy project involving Samruk-Energy, China Energy Overseas Investment and SANY Renewable Energy.

Other agreements provide for the creation of a specialized investment fund at the Astana International Financial Center, financing arrangements between Development Bank of Kazakhstan and China Construction Bank’s Astana branch, as well as projects in automotive manufacturing, chemical production and real estate.

World.title: Kazakhstan Launches Direct Flights From Almaty to Chongqing
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan’s low-cost airline FlyArystan has launched regular flights on a new route connecting Almaty with Chongqing, expanding Kazakhstan’s air connectivity with China.

The new service began on Sept. 23 and will operate twice a week, on Wednesdays and Saturdays, using Airbus A320neo aircraft, according to the Civil Aviation Committee of the Ministry of Transport.

The new service will become FlyArystan’s fifth destination in China, complementing its existing routes to Urumqi, Yining (Kulja) and Xi’an. The launch of the new route is expected to strengthen air connectivity between Kazakhstan and China and contribute to the development of trade, business, investment, tourism and cultural ties between the two countries.

The Civil Aviation Committee continues to work on expanding Kazakhstan’s international flight network and increasing the number of international routes.

World.title: News Digest: Foreign Media on Kazakhstan’s Political Reform, AI Push and Investment Potential
World.content:
ASTANA – The Astana Times has selected articles from global media outlets covering Kazakhstan. This week’s foreign media digest covers constitutional reform, the country’s drive to become a regional AI hub, nuclear energy cooperation, investment opportunities and Astana’s new airport project.

Kazakhstan’s new political era: Constitutional reform

EU Reporter published an article examining Kazakhstan’s post-referendum political reforms, focusing on the new Constitution, the newly elected 145-member Kurultai, the creation of the vice-presidency and People’s Council, and how these institutional changes are being linked to broader economic, technological and EU cooperation.

“Constitutional reform is not only about institutions. Its significance lies in how effectively they serve citizens, strengthen governance and contribute to the country’s development,” reads the article.

Inside Kazakhstan’s push to become a regional AI centre

Al Jazeera published an article on Sept. 21 about Kazakhstan’s rapid push to become a regional AI hub, covering its government-backed digitalisation drive, development of local AI technologies and talent, and the environmental and human-rights concerns accompanying that expansion.

One of the article’s notable examples is how Kazakhstan’s AI sector is opening new career opportunities for women. Valeria Tio, managing director of Astana Hub, said a woman who had worked as a barista at the hub found a job as a developer after one year of studying through its Tomorrow School programme, calling it “a real social elevator.” The program has trained 500 people in 18 months, while new cohorts are now being opened across 12 regions of Kazakhstan.

Kazakhstan, UK discuss cooperation in peaceful use of nuclear energy

Kazakhstan and the UK discussed prospects for cooperation in the peaceful use of nuclear energy during a meeting between the Agency of Kazakhstan for Atomic Energy, Deputy Chairman Timur Zhantikin and Lord John Alderdice, the UK Prime Minister’s Trade Envoy for Central Asia, reported Trend on Sept. 22.

“The meeting discussed current issues and prospects for developing Kazakhstan-UK cooperation in the peaceful use of nuclear energy,” the agency said.

Kazakhstan: A nation set to capitalise from its vast natural resources and investor appeal

Credendo released an article on Sept. 24 about Kazakhstan’s economic and investment outlook, highlighting its abundant natural resources, strong macroeconomic fundamentals and strategic position, as well as efforts to diversify through the Middle Corridor, critical minerals, infrastructure, digitalisation and AI.

“Kazakhstan is endowed with substantial commodity wealth, including oil, gas, uranium and critical minerals, leading to strong trade and investment commitments in transport and digital infrastructure, logistics, energy and critical minerals. Moreover, Astana is trading its resources against access to technologies,” reads the article.

Changi Airports to participate in construction of new airport in Kazakhstan’s Astana

Singapore’s Changi Airports International (CAI), a subsidiary of Changi Airport Group, will be involved in the construction of a new airport in Astana, according to the Astana akimat, reported Trend on Sept. 23.

The Astana akimat, Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Transport and CAI have signed a Framework Cooperation Agreement aimed at developing a long-term strategic partnership in the field of airport infrastructure in the capital.

Under the agreement, the parties reached formal arrangements in two main areas: cooperation on the construction of a new airport in Astana and the development of the existing Astana International Airport.

World.title: India, Kazakhstan Seek to Turn Strategic Partnership Into Deeper Trade and Investment Ties
World.content:
ASTANA – India and Kazakhstan should translate their strong political partnership into deeper trade, investment, digital and energy cooperation, participants said at the India-Kazakhstan Strategic Dialogue on Sept. 24.

During the India-Kazakhstan: Anchoring Regional Stability and Economic Integration in a Multilateral World session, speakers highlighted the gap between close political ties and relatively modest bilateral trade.

Indian Ambassador to Kazakhstan Sailas Thangal said the countries need to address structural barriers limiting economic cooperation, including connectivity, logistics, customs procedures, payment mechanisms, market access and regulatory issues.

“Business delegations and exhibitions alone are not enough to enhance our bilateral trade and commerce,” he said, calling for concrete measures to turn existing potential into commercial partnerships.

“India and Kazakhstan have the trust, we have the complementarity, we have the political will. What we need now is to convert this essence into connectivity, governance and concrete partnership,” he said.

Trade remains below potential

Rakhim Oshakbayev, director of the TALAP Center for Applied Research, described the $923 million in bilateral trade in 2025 as a “long-standing anomaly.”

“Our political relationship is excellent. Many speakers talked about this. We are strategic partners,” he said.

However, he noted that logistical constraints continue to limit economic ties, describing the situation as “high politics, low logistics, big friendship, small trade.”

India accounted for around 0.64% of Kazakhstan’s total foreign trade in 2025. Oshakbayev attributed the limited trade partly to difficult transport routes.

“We are close in the sky and far on the ground,” he said, proposing greater focus on high-value goods and services that depend less on traditional transport links.

Uranium, pharmaceuticals and digital cooperation

Uranium was identified as one of the most promising areas for expanding economic ties. Oshakbayev referred to a long-term contract between Kazatomprom and India’s Department of Atomic Energy, saying press reports have valued it at more than $4 billion.

“Uranium is a perfect product for difficult geography, very high value, very small volume,” he said, proposing broader cooperation around the agreement, including training and the nuclear fuel cycle.

He also highlighted pharmaceutical production in Kazakhstan, which could serve both the domestic market and the wider Eurasian Economic Union market.

Participants identified artificial intelligence, fintech, cybersecurity, e-government and digital payments as other areas of potential cooperation, saying Indian technology companies could use Kazakhstan as a platform for accessing regional markets.

Strategic autonomy and regional cooperation

Former Indian Ambassador to Russia and former Deputy National Security Advisor Pankaj Saran said India and Kazakhstan could contribute to regional stability through diplomacy, economic development and diversified international partnerships.

“Both India and Kazakhstan maintain that independence of decision making. How can we both show to our people and to the region that we can be friends with everyone. We don’t have to choose one against the other,” he said.

Saran highlighted Kazakhstan’s balanced foreign policy and India’s strategic autonomy as areas of commonality, pointing to cooperation in regional stability, Afghanistan, peacekeeping and economic development.

He also cited growing energy requirements linked to the expansion of artificial intelligence and data centers as an area for potential cooperation.

Participants also called for stronger business, academic and people-to-people ties through joint research, healthcare, tourism and education, as well as practical cooperation in transport, energy, critical minerals, agriculture and technology.

The discussions highlighted opportunities to build on the strong political foundation of India-Kazakhstan relations by expanding trade, investment and practical economic cooperation.

World.title: Search Operation Ends After Bodies of Two Missing Service Officers Found In Caspian Sea
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan’s search-and-rescue operation in the Caspian Sea has officially ended after the bodies of two service officers who had been missing following a military exercise were found on Sept. 25, bringing the death toll from the incident to 14.

The bodies were found at around 9:15 a.m. on Sept. 25 during continuous search operations, according to the Defence Ministry. The incident occurred during a training and combat exercise when 17 servicemen were swept into the open sea amid a sudden and sharp deterioration in weather conditions and strong winds. Three service officers were rescued, while 14 died.

Sept. 25 was declared a national day of mourning in Kazakhstan by order of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev following the deaths.

Search operation concludes

The search-and-rescue operation was conducted around the clock under the direction of Defence Minister Lieutenant General of Aviation Dauren Kosanov. An operational headquarters brought together representatives of the Defence Ministry, the Border Service of the National Security Committee, the Ministry of Emergency Situations, the Ministry of Internal Affairs and local executive authorities of the Mangystau Region.

At its peak, the operation involved 252 personnel, 34 units of specialized ground equipment, 37 military divers, 14 vessels and boats, and more than 20 aircraft, including four helicopters. Search teams surveyed the sea, coastal areas and adjacent territory from the air.

The Defence Ministry expressed condolences to the families and relatives of those killed, saying they would receive comprehensive material and psychological assistance.

Criminal investigation continues

A government commission established on the instructions of President Tokayev and headed by Deputy Prime Minister Kanat Bozumbayev continues to oversee the investigation into the circumstances of the incident.

At a government commission meeting on Sept. 24, Deputy Minister of Internal Affairs Sanzhar Adilov reported that criminal proceedings had been launched over negligent attitude toward service resulting in grave consequences and violations of navigation rules.

Investigators are conducting investigative and operational-search measures, while specialists have been involved and the necessary forensic examinations ordered. Bozumbayev instructed authorities to establish the full circumstances of the incident and take measures against those responsible.

“A special commission has been established to establish all the circumstances of the tragedy. Criminal cases have been opened. The investigation must be thorough, objective and prompt. Those whose actions or inaction led to this tragedy will be held accountable to the fullest extent of the law,” Bozumbayev said.

Families to receive assistance

Bozumbayev said the families of the deceased would receive substantial financial assistance in addition to payments provided for by law. Members of the Kazakhstan Khalyk Kenesi and representatives of major businesses have also expressed their intention to provide additional assistance to the families.

The Deputy Prime Minister instructed the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection and the Mangystau regional administration to ensure transparency and oversight in the distribution of funds allocated to the families, stressing that assistance should be provided directly and in full.

President Tokayev earlier expressed condolences to the families and relatives of the servicemen who died in the incident. The service officers rescued during the incident remain in stable condition and are receiving the necessary medical treatment, Deputy Health Minister Manas Ramazanov reported.

World.title: ‘Unresolved issues and conflicting narratives remain’ — Pashinyan on relations with Azerbaijan
World.content:
Pashinyan’s UN address

In his address to the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan spoke about the peace that Armenia and Azerbaijan have established. At the same time, he addressed outstanding issues that the two countries still need to resolve. These include determining the fate of several thousand missing people, carrying out demining operations and securing the return of Armenians, whom Azerbaijan holds in its prisons.

Pashinyan stressed that, beyond these issues of concern to Armenian society, conflicting narratives and discourses among certain circles in Armenia and Azerbaijan also fuel pessimism. Sometimes, officials themselves voice these views.

“I think that we, meaning Armenia and Azerbaijan, have achieved more than satisfactory results. These should mean more to us than the use of conflicting narratives, whether about history, cultural monuments or anything else,” he said.

In effect, the prime minister was responding to a recent visit by diplomats to Karabakh, which Azerbaijani authorities had organised. During the visit, officials attempted to present the Armenian monasteries of Gandzasar and Dadivank as part of “ancient Albanian Christian heritage”.

The move sparked such public outrage that many politicians called on Armenia’s leadership to issue a strong official response. Tensions between Armenia and Azerbaijan rose against this backdrop. Politicians described the situation as a serious crisis that could hinder further progress in the peace process.

Against this backdrop, Pashinyan stressed that Armenia and Azerbaijan must now focus on “safeguarding peace, strengthening it and developing its institutions”.

In his address, Pashinyan also touched on other issues of current importance to Armenia, including the implementation of the Armenian-American “Trump Route” project (TRIPP), relations with the European Union and Russia, as well as the normalisation of relations between Armenia and Turkey.

“The main item on the Yerevan-Baku agenda is signing a peace agreement”

The Armenian prime minister placed particular emphasis on the fact that no one has been killed or injured in border shootings between Armenia and Azerbaijan for the past two and a half years. He described this as “the greatest achievement of cooperation in recent years”.

“Never before have independent Armenia and independent Azerbaijan experienced such a period, despite centuries of peaceful coexistence between Armenians and Azerbaijanis,” Pashinyan said.

In his view, Yerevan and Baku must build relations between the two states on the basis of this shared experience, respecting each other’s territorial integrity, sovereignty and political independence. This is particularly important given that the two countries have already agreed on these principles and even initialled a peace treaty.

“Signing and ratifying this agreement is the next important item on Armenia and Azerbaijan’s joint agenda. We will continue to work consistently towards this goal,”

“The implementation of TRIPP promises major benefits for all countries in the region”

Pashinyan believes that the peace established between Armenia and Azerbaijan has opened up new opportunities for the entire region. He said the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project would play an important role in this process. He assured his audience that its implementation was “becoming a reality” and would mark a historic milestone for Armenia:

“For the first time since the early 1990s, Armenia will have a railway link with Azerbaijan. This will also connect it to Russia, Central Asia and China.”

The “Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity” (TRIPP) is a transport route that will connect Azerbaijan with its exclave of Nakhchivan through Armenian territory.

The prime minister stressed that Azerbaijan had opened transit routes for Armenia and that rail services between Armenia and Azerbaijan had resumed via Georgia. However, he said, the implementation of TRIPP would establish a direct railway link between Armenia and Azerbaijan:

“In the near future, we will restore the railway sections in Meghri and Yeraskh in Armenia, which existed during the Soviet era but were later destroyed. The railway routes I mentioned will then reopen.”

He said Armenia also expected to restore railway links with Turkey. Alongside TRIPP, he described this as a potential milestone in international logistics, one of the most significant developments in decades:

“This will open up a new railway connection between China, Central Asia, Turkey and the European Union.”

Pashinyan says restoring the railway link between Armenia and Azerbaijan (Nakhchivan) will establish a rail connection between the Persian Gulf and the Black Sea:

“This is an important detail because it shows why and how the implementation of TRIPP promises enormous benefits for all countries in the region. These potential benefits could become a cornerstone of long-term stability and peace, particularly between Armenia and Azerbaijan.”

According to Pashinyan, building pipelines, power lines and roads as part of TRIPP would allow not only Armenia but the entire South Caucasus to become a “crossroads of peace”.

“A plan to seize the state was drawn up”: on elections in Armenia

The prime minister also spoke about the circumstances surrounding Armenia’s recent parliamentary elections. For the second time or more, he openly accused foreign actors of interference:

“Several external and internal forces devised and carried out a plan to seize the state. They used mass disinformation, hybrid and other tools, as well as widespread distribution of election bribes.”

He stressed that Armenia’s state institutions had prevented the seizure of power thanks to their resilience. Pashinyan believes this, in turn, reflects the democratic and institutional reforms that the country has carried out in recent years:

“The people of Armenia voted for peace. And we must consistently work to further strengthen and institutionalise peace.”

Ties with the EU deepen as relations with Russia undergo transformation

Pashinyan also spoke about Armenia’s balanced foreign policy. The prime minister noted that in recent years, his government had established strategic relations with Georgia, France, China, the Netherlands, Kazakhstan, Germany, Luxembourg, the United Kingdom, Bulgaria, Croatia, Lithuania, the United States and the European Union.

“The European Commission has approved a decision to introduce autonomous trade measures for Armenia, marking another sign of the new quality of relations between Armenia and the EU,” he stressed.

Relations between Yerevan and Moscow, meanwhile, are undergoing a transformation, according to the prime minister.

In his view, this is a natural process because the Armenian-Azerbaijani conflict had been the main factor shaping Armenia’s relations with Russia throughout the preceding period. The establishment of peace has fundamentally changed the situation.

“We want our relations with Russia to develop on the principles of friendship and mutual respect,” he said.

Relations with neighbouring countries

Nikol Pashinyan noted that normalising and deepening relations with neighbouring countries is crucial for Armenia:

“We have established high-level dialogue with Turkey. I want to reaffirm President Erdoğan’s remarks from this podium a few days ago. We are firmly advancing the process of normalising Armenian-Turkish relations.”

Good-neighbourly relations with Iran and Georgia are also continuing to develop and deepen. Moreover, the prime minister said, these relations are of “exceptional importance” to Yerevan.
